title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Share and width-specialize the combinational divider
motivation:
The baseline achieves 12.12 CoreMark iterations/second at 5.442 MHz.
Its reported worst path crosses forwarding and the combinational ALU,
taking 199.837 ns through 156 cells. The four signed/unsigned division
and remainder expressions are the strongest RTL-level suspect for this
depth, although the available path summary does not identify individual
arithmetic cells. This path limits every cycle, even when no divide is
executing. There are no earlier non-baseline attempts in the local log.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real-arithmetic DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU implementation with
one explicitly shared, fully combinational unsigned restoring divmod
network. Normalize operands to unsigned magnitudes for signed operations,
obtain quotient and remainder from the same network, then restore the
quotient sign from a[31] XOR b[31] and the remainder sign from a[31].
Leave multiplication, base ALU operations, pipeline registers, forwarding,
bus handshakes, and retirement latency unchanged. This is a local logic
optimization, with no iterative unit, additional cycle, or timing exception.

Specialize each of the 32 unrolled steps to the number of dividend prefix
bits processed. For step k=1..32, form the k-bit trial remainder T by
appending dividend_magnitude[32-k] to the previous (k-1)-bit remainder;
the first step starts with a zero remainder. Compute a single (k+1)-bit
zero-extended subtraction D = {0,T} - {0,divisor_magnitude[k-1:0]}.
Accept this subtraction only when D[k] is zero and all divisor bits
above k-1 are zero; at k=32 the latter condition is constant true.
The accepted bit becomes quotient[32-k], and the next remainder is
D[k-1:0] if accepted, otherwise T. Use elaboration-time constant widths
and shared high-divisor prefix-OR signals. The subtraction's borrow
supplies the comparison as well as the candidate remainder, avoiding
independently described compare and subtract networks at every step.
The high-divisor guard is essential: truncating the divisor without it
is incorrect. Avoid unsized arithmetic and invalid boundary part-selects.

Select the quotient or final remainder according to the operation.
Explicitly preserve division-by-zero results (quotient all ones,
remainder the original dividend) and INT_MIN/-1 (INT_MIN, remainder zero).
Preserve truncation toward zero and signed remainder semantics for all
other inputs. Keep the existing RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas unchanged
and place the real divider implementation behind the non-ALTOPS branch.
Preserve the combinational alu module interface and the nret=1 contract.

The predicted gain comes from reducing serial arithmetic depth and
duplicated divider area/routing, with unchanged CoreMark iterations per
cycle. Check it with Gowin median Fmax and the bracketed CoreMark run;
acceptance requires fitness above 12.67752, or Fmax above approximately
5.6924 MHz if the measured iteration rate per cycle is unchanged. Run
the ALU arithmetic tests, normal formal checks, and stalled cosimulation
with canonical CoreMark CRCs. Normal ALTOPS formal alone is insufficient
evidence for the real divider; also prove combinational divmod equivalence
or run the applicable real-arithmetic formal-deep checks. The main risk is
that Gowin already performs equivalent sharing and width reduction, or
that operand normalization and shared routing offset the shorter steps.

Keep the current interface, zero-cycle combinational latency, all
non-division operations, and all ALTOPS formulas unchanged.

random pairs and directed zero, +/-1, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, and high-bit

smaller/equal/larger cases, and all signed operand combinations to

never floating point or Python floor division on signed operands.

title: Move division into a bounded multicycle execute unit
motivation:
The baseline scores 12.12 with median Fmax 5.442 MHz. Its reported worst
path is 199.837 ns across 156 cells through forwarding and the execute
ALU. alu.sv implements signed and unsigned division and remainder with
combinational / and % operators, making these the strongest suspected
source of the deep arithmetic path even when ordinary instructions run.
The history contains only the baseline and no prior structural attempt;
LESSONS.md is absent. Separating division from the ordinary execute path
should trade a few cycles per divide for a substantially faster clock
across the complete CoreMark run.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU execution with one shared, registered,
blocking divider. Capture the post-forwarding operands and operation
once, prepare unsigned magnitudes, perform eight radix-2 restoring
quotient-bit steps per clock for four clocks, and register the signed
quotient or remainder before transferring the instruction to EX/MEM.
Each restoring step uses one extended subtract and its borrow to select
the next remainder. Separate magnitude preparation and sign correction
from the four arithmetic rounds: accept and latch magnitudes at edge 0,
run rounds at edges 1 through 4, register the corrected result at edge 5,
and transfer it to EX/MEM at edge 6. Bound execution to these seven EX
clocks including request capture and result transfer when memory is ready,
so the existing short formal liveness window remains meaningful. This replaces a full
32-step combinational divide with a reused eight-step datapath bounded by
registers. Keep ordinary integer operations and all multiplication
operations at their existing single-cycle execute latency.

Hold PC and ID/EX while a divide is outstanding, but let older EX/MEM and
MEM/WB instructions drain normally. After an older instruction advances,
inject a fully inert EX/MEM bubble on cycles without a completed divide;
merely clearing valid is insufficient because current memory and
forwarding controls are not all valid-qualified. A real dmem stall still
holds its outstanding request. Launch a divide only when that older
memory request can advance, latch operands before their forwarding
sources disappear, and retain a completed result until EX/MEM accepts it.
Consume each request/result once, suppress redirects from invalid or
blocked instructions, and preserve the retiring instruction's captured
source values and metadata. Preserve channel-0-only, in-order retirement,
x0 behavior, reset cancellation, traps, and both memory handshakes.

Preserve RV32M truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder,
division-by-zero results, and INT_MIN/-1 results. Under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain the exact existing XOR formulas while exercising
the same request, busy, completion, and backpressure schedule as hardware.
Remove the real combinational divide/remainder cones from the synthesized
ordinary ALU; adding a sequential unit while retaining those cones would
not establish the intended timing improvement. Keep the decoder and all
evaluation contracts unchanged. Validate real arithmetic and transaction
control in cocotb, then run the existing formal and stalled CoreMark cosim
gates. Measure median Gowin Fmax times marker-bracketed iterations/cycle;
the hypothesis succeeds only if the product exceeds 12.67752, the 4.6%
acceptance threshold. The main risks are residual multiplier or register
file timing becoming dominant and divide stalls offsetting the clock gain.

changes.description:
Add an internal request/busy/result handshake and a shared clocked
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU engine, with four rounds of eight restoring steps,
separate operand and result registers, and a sticky completion until
consumed. Remove synthesizable combinational / and % implementations.
Preserve the existing combinational integer/multiply outputs and all
eight ALTOPS formulas; division ALTOPS uses the same finite handshake
schedule as real division. Keep the divider implementation in this
file so existing ALU unit-test source discovery remains usable.

Recognize valid divide/remainder instructions, capture forwarded
operands once, and drive the ALU request/result handshake. Expose an
execute-wait signal. Retain source values and instruction metadata
while waiting, transfer the completed result exactly once, and emit
zero-control EX/MEM bubbles while older operations drain. Give a real
memory stall priority over EX/MEM updates and gate redirects on valid
instructions actually allowed to advance. Preserve all other execute
paths, including multiplication, branch traps, and link results.

Add execute-wait handling that holds fetch and ID/EX without flushing
the divide or freezing older MEM/WB work. Keep this distinct from
dmem backpressure, which must retain its current request and forwarding
state. Release the front end on the single result-transfer event;
preserve load-use and redirect priorities for ordinary instructions.

Wire execute-wait and divider acceptance through the existing execute
and hazard modules. Preserve every top-level bus and nret=1 RVFI port,
the sole retirement channel, and monotonically incrementing order.

Adapt divider tests to clock/reset and the new bounded handshake,
retaining every existing arithmetic expected-value assertion. Add at
least 30 deterministic and seeded-random operand pairs for each divide
and remainder operation, including all sign combinations, zero,
INT_MIN/-1, high-bit unsigned values, divisor larger than dividend,
and exact divisions. Check back-to-back requests, held completion,
operand changes after acceptance, and reset during a divide. Preserve
all existing integer and multiply checks and their single-cycle path.

Add retirement and result checks for forwarded divide operands,
dependent ALU/load/store/branch consumers, consecutive divides,
divisions writing x0, wrong-path divides, and reset while busy. Mix
imem and dmem stalls with an older load or store ahead of a divide;
verify requests and retirements are neither lost nor duplicated and
RVFI order advances once per accepted instruction. Retain all current
assertions and run the unchanged formal and CoreMark validation gates.

title: Instruction-aware bimodal prediction for the fused fetch/decode stage
motivation:
The baseline always fetches PC+4 and redirects on every taken conditional
branch and every jump. Despite the five-stage description, IF/ID is a
combinational bundle, so each such redirect discards one younger fetch/decode
slot. CoreMark's repeated loops and calls offer an opportunity to eliminate
those bubbles. The only recorded experiment is the 12.12 baseline; there is
no LESSONS.md or prior predictor result. Its measured worst path runs through
forwarding and the combinational ALU, so this proposal targets iterations
per cycle while keeping predictor logic out of that arithmetic path.

branch and every jump. Despite the five-stage description, IF/ID is a

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one instruction-aware next-PC predictor to the existing fused IF/ID
stage: a 128-entry table of two-bit saturating conditional-branch counters,
indexed by fetch PC[8:2], combined with immediate targets from the current
instruction. Initialize counters to weakly not taken (01). Predict a legal
conditional branch taken when its counter MSB is one, and predict legal
direct JAL instructions taken unconditionally. Reconstruct the signed B/J
immediate and add it to the current full 32-bit PC. All other instructions,
including JALR, predict PC+4. Check the BRANCH funct3 and target alignment
before speculating; reserved encodings and misaligned direct targets use
PC+4 and retain the existing decoder/EX trap behavior. No target cache,
return stack, global history, extra pipeline stage, or ISA change is needed.

Carry the exact predicted_next_pc selected for an accepted instruction in
if_id_t and then id_ex_t. The PC update and ID/EX capture must use the same
prediction at the same edge. Ordinary prediction advances the PC only when
the instruction is accepted, never during instruction-bus backpressure,
load-use replay, or a data-memory freeze. Hold prediction metadata together
with the instruction on stalls and clear it on bubbles. Generate predictions
from raw imem_data and the fetch PC, not from a redirect-masked instruction,
to avoid a combinational dependency through the flush controls.

EX still computes the authoritative next PC using the existing forwarded
operands and branch comparisons. Preserve PC+4 link writes and existing
misalignment/trap semantics, including sequential pc_next on target faults.
Replace taken-control-flow redirect with mismatch recovery: redirect only
when an instruction is valid, EX is advancing, and resolved_next_pc differs
from its saved predicted_next_pc. A correct taken prediction therefore keeps
the already fetched target instruction. A false taken prediction recovers
to PC+4; a missed taken branch or unpredicted JALR recovers to the resolved
target. Flush the younger slot before it can reach EX/MEM or issue a data
access. RVFI pc_wdata always reports resolved_next_pc, never a prediction.

Define EX advance as !stall_ex_mem. Train the counter indexed by the
resolving branch's PC exactly once on valid, legal, non-faulting conditional
branch advance, incrementing on taken and decrementing on not taken with
saturation. Do not train on bubbles, JAL/JALR, or held EX cycles. Predictor
updates are hints only; aliases can change accuracy but cannot change the
reconstructed target or architectural behavior. Use the current stored
counter for each update rather than a stale fetch-time counter snapshot.

During a data-memory freeze, suppress both recovery and training and retain
the unresolved EX instruction until it can advance. On that release cycle,
recovery must override an instruction-bus stall or younger load-use stall;
it must set the PC and squash the younger instruction even when imemReady
is low. Retain the existing MEM/WB data retention used for forwarding across
stalls. Preserve nret=1, all decoder checks, and all retirement invariants.

Expected benefit is approximately 10 percent higher fitness, predominantly
from fewer control-flow bubbles rather than higher Fmax. This is an estimate,
not a measured result. At unchanged Fmax, exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance
threshold requires reducing the baseline's 4,491,485 bracketed cycles below
approximately 4.294 million. Predictor aliasing, hard-to-predict branches,
and Gowin placement/area effects are the main risks. Judge the implemented
candidate by the full median-Fmax times measured iterations/cycle product,
with canonical CoreMark CRC/UART checks and both buses stalled as specified.

title: Reduce the iterative divider to six restoring steps per clock
motivation:
The current champion scores 71.56 at 32.14 MHz. Its reported worst path
runs from quotient_q[31] to remainder_q[0] inside u_ex/u_alu, with
37.038 ns arrival and 262 cells. The eight serial restoring steps in
each divider round are therefore a direct target for local timing
optimization. The previous micro_opt attempt, hyp-20261003-001-r1s0,
lost 23.43% by retaining a fully combinational divider despite sharing
and width specialization. The winning registered divider retained the
baseline's reported 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles, suggesting that
a modest increase in division latency will have little measured cost.
This observation is workload evidence, not permission to change any
arithmetic semantics or benchmark timing boundaries.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Tune only the unroll factor of the existing blocking restoring divider:
perform six quotient-bit steps in each of the first five DIV_ROUND
clocks, then two steps in the sixth and final round. This processes
exactly 32 bits while reducing the longest combinational chain from
eight extended subtract/borrow/mux stages to six. Reuse the existing
quotient, remainder, divisor, magnitude-preparation, sign-correction,
and completion registers and the existing execute-wait protocol. This
is a local divider datapath and counter optimization, with the same
core pipeline, arithmetic algorithm, and unit interface.

Widen round_q to three bits, initialize it to zero on acceptance, and
transition from DIV_ROUND to DIV_SIGN after round_q == 5. Elaborate
six unconditional restoring steps, retaining the intermediate quotient
and remainder after step two. At the round-register input select that
two-step pair only for round_q == 5; otherwise select the six-step pair.
Do not insert a round-dependent enable mux into every individual step,
and do not shift through six bits on the last round: either mistake
would undermine the timing improvement or corrupt the arithmetic.
Retain the current extended subtraction and borrow convention exactly.

With ready memory, accept at edge 0, execute rounds at edges 1..6,
register the sign-corrected result at edge 7, and consume at edge 8.
Completion remains asserted until consumed. Division therefore occupies
nine EX clocks instead of seven. Keep the same six-round schedule in
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, preserving every existing XOR formula. Keep signed
truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, division by zero,
INT_MIN/-1, operand capture, reset cancellation, and backpressure behavior.
All ordinary ALU and multiply operations retain their current latency.

Six steps is chosen to respect the unchanged formal progress contract,
not just to improve timing. checks_si.cfg uses liveness trigger 10 and
check 20. Eight four-step rounds with the existing sign and consume
phases would already take eleven EX clocks. Six rounds take nine;
even a taken branch or jump followed by a target DIV/REM should have
a retirement gap of at most ten clocks with both buses ready. Verify
this boundary explicitly, including consecutive dependent divides.
Do not relax formal depths, hide latency in ALTOPS, or change nret=1.

Predict approximately 20% higher fitness through increased Fmax and
nearly unchanged marker-bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle. Require
median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle above 74.85176,
the champion's 4.6% acceptance threshold. If cycles remain unchanged,
this requires approximately 33.62 MHz. Run the existing real-arithmetic
ALU tests, pipeline tests, unchanged formal checks, and stalled CoreMark
cosimulation with canonical CRCs and validation text. Normal ALTOPS
formal does not establish actual divide arithmetic correctness.
Principal risks are the final-round selection mux offsetting the
shorter chain, another path limiting Fmax, and a larger measured
division-cycle penalty than the historical cycle counts suggest.

title: Retiming division to four restoring steps with fused completion
motivation:
The structural champion hyp-20261003-002-r1s1 scores 71.56 at 32.14 MHz.
Its recorded critical path now runs from quotient_q[31] to remainder_q[0]
entirely inside the divider, with 37.038 ns arrival and 262 cells. Moving
division out of the combinational ALU succeeded, but the reused eight-step
restoring recurrence still limits the clock for every instruction.
The experiment log reports the same 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles
for the original combinational divider and the seven-clock divider.
This suggests low sensitivity to divide latency in this workload, rather
than establishing that division is absent. The failed combinational
sharing attempt and the predictor result further favor shortening the
measured arithmetic bottleneck before pursuing instruction throughput.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the existing blocking DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU engine around four
radix-2 restoring steps per clock instead of eight. Reuse this smaller
datapath for eight rounds, retaining operand-magnitude capture and the
extended-subtract borrow selection already used by the champion. Fuse
the final arithmetic round, sign correction, and normal result transfer
into the existing EX/MEM register boundary. This is one structural
change to divider scheduling and register placement; ordinary integer
and multiply instructions retain their current execution paths.

Use the following exact no-backpressure schedule. Edge 0 accepts the
request, captures unsigned magnitudes and sign/operation information,
and saves the forwarded operands and retirement metadata as today.
Edges 1 through 7 each register four quotient-bit steps. During the
cycle preceding edge 8, the last four steps produce quotient_next and
remainder_next; select the requested quantity and apply sign correction
combinationally. Assert result availability in this final-round state,
and capture that corrected result directly in EX/MEM at edge 8 if the
consumer accepts it. Thus a divide occupies nine EX clocks, rather than
adding separate sign and transfer clocks to an eleven-clock operation.
The longest recurrence between registers contains four subtract/mux
steps; the final path additionally contains result selection and sign
correction. No eight-step cone or combinational division operator may
remain on the hardware execution path.

Preserve the existing request/busy/valid/consume interface. div_valid
means that div_result is usable at the upcoming edge: it is asserted
in the final-round state as well as the held-completion state. If the
consumer is blocked at edge 8, register the corrected result locally
and enter DONE, retaining the same result and valid until consumed.
If the final-round result is consumed immediately, return directly to
IDLE and do not offer that result again. Keep busy asserted throughout
computation and held completion; ignore new requests while busy.
Give reset priority in every state, canceling an outstanding operation.
Derive completion from registered state/count, without a combinational
dependency on div_consume or execute_wait. Preserve all 33-bit trial
remainder and 34-bit extended-subtraction information needed by the
current restoring algorithm, including the high-divisor unsigned cases.

Existing EX control must consume the final-round result exactly once,
using the metadata and source values captured when the request was
accepted. Hold PC and ID/EX while waiting, drain older instructions,
retain fully inert EX/MEM bubbles, and preserve actual dmem stall
priority. A completed result releases the front end only when the
transfer can occur. Keep nret=1, channel-0 retirement ordering, x0,
decoder legality, traps, and both memory handshakes unchanged.
Preserve every RV32M arithmetic case, including division by zero,
INT_MIN/-1, truncation toward zero, and dividend-signed remainder.
Keep the exact ALTOPS formulas and run them through the same nine-clock
schedule and completion/backpressure states as real arithmetic.

The unchanged liveness configuration triggers at cycle 10 and checks
the successor retirement at cycle 20. The nine-clock EX bound leaves
one clock for a preceding taken branch or jump's redirect bubble when
both buses are ready, as in the formal wrapper. Explicitly verify that
case and consecutive divides; do not extend formal depths, accelerate
only ALTOPS, or remove progress assertions. Adapt exact-latency unit
checks to the new schedule while retaining all arithmetic assertions.
Run the existing ALU and pipeline suites, unchanged formal checks,
real-arithmetic division checks where practical, and stalled CoreMark
cosimulation with the canonical CRCs and marker-bracketed cycle count.

Expected benefit is a higher global Fmax with little CoreMark cycle
penalty. A 35 percent fitness gain is a prediction, not a measurement.
Measure median Gowin Fmax times iterations per bracketed cycle; the
candidate must exceed 74.85176 fitness, or about 33.62 MHz if cycles
remain 4,491,485, to clear the champion by more than 4.6 percent.
Main risks are the final sign-correction path, the unchanged multiplier
or forwarding path becoming critical, and a larger-than-expected
divide frequency. Use the measured product rather than divider latency
or standalone arithmetic timing as the acceptance criterion.

title: Apply instruction-aware bimodal prediction to the multicycle-divider champion
motivation:
The current champion already removes the dominant combinational divider
path and scores 71.56 at 32.14 MHz, but still fetches sequentially and
squashes a younger fetch/decode slot on every taken branch or jump.
IF/ID is combinational, so each unnecessary redirect loses one slot,
not the two suggested by the textbook five-stage description.
LESSONS.md and log.jsonl show that hyp-20261003-003-r1s2 reduced CoreMark
cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,202,272 with a 128-entry bimodal predictor and
direct-JAL prediction. That candidate retained the old combinational
divider and reached only 5.452 MHz; its regression against the champion
does not demonstrate a predictor failure. Applying this measured cycle
improvement to the current multicycle-divider parent is the strongest
evidence-backed predictor opportunity, with roughly 6.9% fitness upside
if the current clock frequency is maintained.

from the currently fetched instruction and add them to the full 32-bit
fetch PC. Predict PC+4 for all other instructions, including JALR.

prediction, independently of flush-masked instruction outputs, to avoid
a combinational feedback loop through hazards. Carry the exact selected
predicted_next_pc in if_id_t and id_ex_t. An accepted instruction and its
prediction must enter ID/EX at the same edge that updates the fetch PC.
Advance normally only when fetch/decode is accepted: no PC advance on
imem backpressure, load-use replay, dmem freeze, or execute_wait. Hold
metadata with a stalled instruction and clear it with an injected bubble.
The table may receive an older branch update while fetch is stalled;
sample the prediction actually used at eventual acceptance, not a stale
earlier lookup. No BTB, return stack, global history, or extra stage is
needed for this hypothesis.

forwarded branch condition, branch/jump target, and trap rules; on a
target-alignment fault it remains PC+4 as in the current implementation.

differs from the saved predicted_next_pc. Define that advance using

existing divider result-consumption handshake. Correct taken predictions
retain the younger target instruction. False taken predictions recover
to PC+4, and missed taken branches or JALR recover to their resolved
target. Use this same authoritative next PC for RVFI pc_wdata and preserve

can execute, issue a data transaction, launch a divide, or retire.

advance, using its own PC index and actual taken outcome. Saturating

cycles. A same-edge lookup observes the pre-update state; that is safe
because the exact resulting prediction travels with its instruction.
Aliasing affects accuracy only: targets always come from the actual
fetched instruction, and every prediction is checked against execution.

title: Shorten restoring-divider borrow chains with a balanced block prefix
motivation:
The champion scores 93.33 at a median 41.919 MHz. Its reported worst
path starts at divider remainder_q[0], crosses u_alu and u_ex, and
reaches the timed memory logic with 28.756 ns arrival through 134 cells.
The divider contains four serial restoring steps, each with a
full-width subtract followed by a borrow-controlled remainder mux;
their borrow propagation is a direct candidate for reducing this delay.
LESSONS.md and log.jsonl show that reducing serial divider depth helped:
the six-step micro_opt reached 40.582 MHz, while the four-step champion
reached 41.919 MHz. The earlier fully combinational sharing attempt
regressed to 4.169 MHz. Target the remaining intra-step borrow dependency
while retaining the proven registered divider and its exact latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the unsigned trial-subtraction circuit inside each of the
existing four restoring steps with eight four-bit subtract blocks and
a balanced block-borrow prefix. This is a combinational implementation
change within alu.sv: retain eight rounds, acceptance at edge 0, seven
intermediate register updates, and final-round consumption at edge 8.
Keep the current sign correction, captured operands, sticky completion,
reset behavior, and request/consume interface. All ordinary ALU and
multiply operations, pipeline stages, and memory handshakes stay intact.

For each step let T = {remainder, quotient[31]} be the 33-bit unsigned
trial remainder and B be the captured 32-bit divisor magnitude. Split
T[31:0] and B into eight four-bit blocks, indexed least significant
first. For block i compute a five-bit zero-extended base subtraction
Z_i = {0,T_i} - {0,B_i}; G_i = Z_i[4] denotes borrow generation and
P_i = (T_i == B_i) denotes propagation of an incoming borrow. Generate
all block-boundary borrows with an explicit three-level parallel prefix
at distances 1, 2, and 4. The combine rule for a higher group H and
lower group L is G = G_H | (P_H & G_L), P = P_H & P_L. Each level must
read the previous level, using elaboration-time constant indices and
distinct wires, rather than a serial procedural recurrence. Borrow
into block 0 is zero; borrow into block i>0 is the inclusive prefix G
for blocks 0 through i-1, and borrow out of bit 31 is prefix G[7].

Reconstruct each four-bit difference block independently as
(T_i - B_i - borrow_i) modulo 16, with explicit unsigned widths. The
complete 33-bit trial subtraction underflows exactly when
!T[32] && borrow_out_31, because the divisor has an implicit zero high
bit. This handles a set trial high bit without extending a carry chain
through bits 32 and 33. Preserve that high-bit term even if reachable
divider states often make it zero. Select T[31:0] on underflow and the
assembled difference otherwise; append !underflow to the quotient.
Use this identical local circuit for each of the four serial steps.
Keep the borrow network visibly balanced and the arithmetic blocks
short; do not reconstruct the original full-width subtract or a
ripple chain of block borrows. Portable combinational SystemVerilog
should express the structure without vendor primitives or timing
exceptions, so both Gowin synthesis and the formal frontend can use it.

Preserve signed magnitude normalization, truncation toward zero,
dividend-signed remainder, zero-divisor results, and INT_MIN/-1.
Leave every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula and its nine-clock control
schedule unchanged; ALTOPS alone cannot validate the new arithmetic.
Preserve all top-level ports, nret=1, decoder legality, traps, and
contiguous channel-0 retirement. No changes outside the allowed RTL
and cocotb tests are needed.

A standalone Python model of this exact prefix and reconstruction
passed 102,048 directed and seeded-random trial-subtraction comparisons,
including both values of T[32], and 16,096 complete RV32M division and
remainder comparisons. This supports the arithmetic formulation, but
is not an RTL equivalence proof or a measured FPGA timing result.

Expect roughly 15 percent higher fitness from shorter borrow paths
with unchanged CoreMark cycles, subject to Gowin mapping and routing.
The history reports 4,491,485 bracketed cycles for both registered
divider champions; measure cycles again rather than assuming that
count. Acceptance requires fitness above 97.62318, more than 4.6 percent
above 93.33, or approximately 43.85 MHz if iterations/cycle is unchanged.
Validate the real arithmetic and existing exact handshake schedule in
ALU tests, the unchanged pipeline and formal gates, and stalled
CoreMark cosimulation with canonical CRCs and marker timing. Check
actual-arithmetic equivalence of the local trial step or the relevant
formal-deep arithmetic properties in addition to ALTOPS formal.
Compare median vendor Fmax times measured iterations/cycle. Principal
risks are prefix routing and duplicated local subtraction area,
synthesis collapsing the intended structure, or final sign correction
and another path limiting Fmax after the borrow chains are shortened.

Replace the divider's four serial radix-2 restoring steps per clock
with two serial radix-4 restoring digits. Each radix-4 digit chooses
two quotient bits by computing trial remainders for D, 2D, and 3D
in parallel, then selecting the largest nonnegative subtraction.
This is a single structural change to the divider datapath topology:
parallel trial arithmetic replaces serial bit-by-bit decisions.
Reuse the current eight-round controller, operand capture, fused
completion boundary, and blocking execute handshake. Ordinary ALU
and multiply operations retain their current paths and latency.

At acceptance edge 0, capture unsigned operand magnitudes and the
existing quotient/remainder and sign metadata. Register the divisor
magnitude and its 3D multiple with sufficient width; form 2D by
wiring shifts. All trial multiples must come from captured state,
with no 3D adder repeated inside either digit's feedback chain.
Compute 3D from the normalized unsigned magnitude, not from the raw
signed operand. Explicitly widen before shifts and addition: D and
2D fit in 34 bits, and 3D needs all 34 bits for high unsigned divisors.
The edge-0 magnitude-to-3D path is also a real timing path to measure.

For each digit let T = {remainder[31:0], quotient[31:30]}, a 34-bit
unsigned trial value. Compute three 35-bit extended differences
{1'b0,T} - {1'b0,kD} for k = 1, 2, 3 independently. Bit 34 is the
unsigned borrow indicator. Select k=3 if its subtraction has no
borrow, else k=2, else k=1, else k=0. The next remainder is the
selected difference, or T for k=0; the next quotient is
{quotient[29:0],k[1:0]}. Use parallel one-hot digit qualifications and
an AND/OR data selection so an avoidable cascaded priority data mux
does not recreate the serial depth. Retain full-width differences
through digit selection, then store the low 32 remainder bits only
after establishing the invariant R < D for D != 0. For D=0 the
selection naturally produces digit 3 every time and retains the
shifted dividend, yielding an all-ones quotient and the dividend
remainder after all 16 digits. Preserve the existing suppression
of quotient sign correction on division by zero.

Chain exactly two such digits in each of eight rounds, processing
exactly 32 dividend bits. Edges 1 through 7 register intermediate
quotient and remainder values. Before edge 8, the final two digits
feed the existing quotient/remainder selector and sign correction;
EX/MEM captures the corrected result directly on consumption.
If consumption is blocked at edge 8, retain the corrected result
in DONE until accepted. Derive div_valid solely from registered
state/count, keep busy asserted until consumption, ignore competing
requests while busy, and cancel pending work on reset. Preserve
the exact edge-0 acceptance to edge-8 transfer schedule for both
real arithmetic and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, including every existing
XOR formula. Do not add a preparation or sign-correction clock.

Retain captured forwarded operands and RVFI metadata, inert bubbles
while older operations drain, real dmem-stall priority, exactly-once
completion, x0 behavior, decoder legality and traps, both memory
handshakes, and single-channel nret=1 retirement ordering. Preserve
truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, division by zero,
and INT_MIN/-1 for all four DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU operations. No changes
to formal depths, wrappers, evaluation files, or retirement width.

Validate the recurrence with exact integer reference arithmetic and
real-arithmetic ALU tests, then run existing pipeline, formal, and
stalled CoreMark gates with canonical CRCs and validation text.
Include high-bit unsigned divisors, all digit thresholds, zero
divisors, signed corner cases, completion backpressure, and reset.
Preserve the ready-bus maximum ten-clock retirement gap for a taken
branch or jump followed by a divide and for consecutive divides.
A proposal-stage Python model of these two radix-4 digits per round
matched 82,992 DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU reference results from directed and
seeded-random inputs, including checks on intermediate width and
remainder bounds. This validates the proposed arithmetic recurrence,
not an RTL implementation, formal proof, or FPGA timing result.

Predict a 25 percent fitness improvement from fewer serial carry
chains, with unchanged instruction timing and little area pressure
relative to the 10,000-LUT target. This is an estimate, not a timing
measurement. Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax times measured
bracketed iterations/cycle greater than 97.62318, which is 4.6 percent
above 93.33. At 4,491,485 cycles for ten iterations this requires
approximately 43.85 MHz. The principal risks are wider parallel
subtractors and selection routing erasing the depth gain, the new
magnitude-to-3D capture path, final sign correction, or another
existing path becoming critical. Judge the complete timed core.

title: Timing-lean bimodal prediction with direction-only recovery
motivation:
The current champion scores 93.33 at 41.919 MHz and 4,491,485 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its fused combinational IF/ID stage loses one younger
instruction slot whenever EX redirects a taken branch or jump. Both
prior predictor attempts reduced that count to 4,202,272 cycles using
128 bimodal counters and direct-JAL prediction. The second attempt
used the older eight-step divider parent: it increased fitness from
71.56 to 74.95, but lost approximately 2% Fmax and did not beat the
newer divider champion. It also added 982 LUT4s and 287 FFs relative
to its own parent. The demonstrated cycle benefit is worth preserving,
but its approximately 6.9% throughput upside leaves little timing
margin above the required 4.6% fitness improvement. This proposal
specializes prediction and recovery to reduce predictor overhead on
the current four-step-divider champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add an instruction-aware 128-entry, two-bit bimodal direction predictor
with unconditional direct-JAL prediction, but implement it with local
counter updates and just one saved prediction bit per instruction.
This is one predictor architecture change. Preserve the champion's
arithmetic, nine-clock divider schedule, pipeline boundaries, memory
behavior, decoder legality rules, and nret=1 retirement contract.

Index the counters by fetch PC[8:2], initialize them to weakly not
taken (01), and use the selected MSB to predict legal conditional
branches. Derive full-width signed B/J targets from the current raw
imem_data and fetch PC; predict legal direct JAL taken unconditionally.
Only select a direct target when it is word aligned. All other
instructions, including JALR and reserved branch encodings, predict
PC+4. No cached targets, global history, return stack, or extra stage
are needed. Generate predictions independently of redirect-masked
instruction outputs to avoid feedback through flush and hazards.

Implement the table as 128 small constant-index counter cells in a
generate loop. Each cell has its own synchronous enable comparing
the EX update index with its constant index, and computes saturation
from its own two state bits. Only the MSBs feed the asynchronous
fetch-indexed lookup. Avoid a variable-index read-modify-write path
that multiplexes a second 128-entry table read into shared update
logic and fans that result back to all cells. Read-before-write is
sufficient; do not add a same-cycle update bypass. Train exactly once
when a valid, legal, non-faulting conditional branch advances in EX,
incrementing on taken and decrementing on not taken. Held instructions,
bubbles, jumps, reset, and pending divides must not train the table.

Carry only predicted_taken through if_id_t and id_ex_t, sampled from
the actual PC selection at the instruction's acceptance edge. No
32-bit predicted_next_pc register or target equality comparator is
required: every predicted target is reconstructed from the same PC
and immediate as the captured instruction's authoritative EX target.
Therefore direction agreement implies target agreement for supported
direct transfers. This property relies on not predicting JALR or
using a BTB. Hold the bit with its instruction during stalls and
clear it with the bundle on bubbles, flush, or reset.

In EX, define actual_taken as a legal, non-faulting taken conditional
branch or jump, and recover when actual_taken XOR predicted_taken
on valid EX advance. Define EX advance as in.valid && !reset &&
!stall_ex_mem && !execute_wait. An unpredicted legal JALR consequently
retains its existing redirect. Select the resolved target on actual
taken and PC+4 otherwise, using the existing sequential-next-PC rule
on a target-alignment fault. A predicted-taken branch that is actually
not taken must recover to PC+4. Direction disagreement with a direct
target equal to PC+4 may conservatively insert a recovery bubble;
it must not require a wide comparison to suppress that harmless case.
Do not gate the architectural PC+4 link write or RVFI pc_next on
whether recovery occurs: correctly predicted JAL still writes its
link, and RVFI always reports the resolved architectural next PC.

Fetch priorities remain reset, then accepted EX recovery, then
ordinary accepted prediction. Advance the PC and capture the matching
instruction/prediction together only when imem is ready and no
load-use, data-memory, or execute_wait hold blocks acceptance. If an
older EX branch trains while fetch is stalled, sample the lookup
actually used when acceptance eventually occurs. A correct taken
prediction preserves the fetched target instruction. A recovery
squashes the younger slot before it can launch a divide, access data
memory, or retire. Suppress recovery and training throughout a dmem
freeze; on release, recovery overrides imem backpressure or younger
load-use hold. Preserve the existing MEM/WB forwarding-data retention
and all divider request, saved-operand, completion, and consume logic.

Expect approximately 7% higher fitness if the previously demonstrated
cycle reduction transfers and Fmax is maintained. This is an estimate,
not a new measurement. Fitness must exceed 97.62318 to beat 93.33 by
4.6%; at 4,202,272 cycles for ten iterations this requires more than
41.02391 MHz, allowing only about 2.1% clock loss. Local update logic
and direction-only recovery aim to protect that margin without
changing the measured predictor policy. Counter enable fanout,
direct-target addition, conservative same-target recoveries, and
Gowin placement effects remain risks. Evaluate the actual median
Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle, with the unchanged formal,
cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART, stall, and marker gates.

title: Use validity at ID/EX instead of muxing fetched instructions to NOP
motivation:
The champion scores 103.91 at 46.673 MHz. A fresh vendor placement-0
run reproduces 46.361 MHz, with a 26.865 ns multiplier path and an
almost tied 26.864 ns branch/control path. The detailed control path
passes from the register file through EX branch comparison, IF
instruction masking, a hazard source-register comparison, and ID
register control. IF currently replaces the entire instruction with
a NOP on redirect or instruction-bus stall even though IF also marks
that instruction invalid and ID separately flushes on redirect.
Removing this redundant data-path squash should shorten the control
path and reduce redirect fanout without adding prediction or stages.
Prior micro_opt borrow-prefix work regressed despite fewer cells;
actual Gowin timing is therefore the criterion for this local change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Carry imem_data directly in the combinational IF/ID instruction field
on every cycle. Keep out.valid = !(flush || redirect), the existing
PC update, and redirect-over-stall priority. Move invalid-instruction
neutralization to the receiving ID/EX register: reset or explicit
flush clears the whole payload; otherwise a stall holds it; otherwise
invalid IF/ID clears the whole payload; otherwise decode and capture
normally. This replaces the wide instruction-to-NOP mux and its
redirect-dependent source addresses with narrow validity control at
the register boundary. It is one local bubble-insertion optimization,
with no changed pipeline stages, branch policy, or instruction latency.

In id_stage preserve the exact precedence with, for example:
if (reset || flush) reg_q <= '0;
else if (!stall && !in.valid) reg_q <= '0;
else if (!stall) capture the existing decoded fields;
otherwise hold. Do not clear a held instruction merely because the
current fetch is invalid. A dmem-stalled or divider-held instruction
must survive simultaneous imem backpressure. Clear every control in
an accepted bubble, not just valid: memory and forwarding units use
some controls without independently checking valid. Do not retain
decoded load/store/reg_write controls from an invalid raw instruction.

The hazard unit will now see raw fetched rs fields. Preserve its
equations and priorities. If fetch is stalled, PC already holds and
ID either captures an inert bubble or the load-use condition inserts
one. If dmem or execute waits, existing stall priority holds ID/EX.
On a real redirect the executing instruction is a branch or jump,
not a load, and the explicit ID flush wins; a raw wrong-path source
match cannot turn that redirect into a load-use stall. Validate these
interactions with directed tests instead of adding a late redirect
qualification to the source address bus, which recreates the path.

Preserve the decoder's illegal-by-default policy, trap behavior,
memory handshakes, forwarded operands, and all arithmetic including
exact real and ALTOPS divider schedules. Preserve nret=1 ports and
contiguous single-channel RVFI order. Fetched wrong-path or unready
instructions must never retire or cause memory/register side effects.
Meaningful instruction behavior and marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles
should remain unchanged; only invalid pipeline payloads differ.

Proposal-stage measurement of this exact two-file prototype produced
Gowin frequencies of 48.395, 50.514, and 50.514 MHz for placement
options 0, 1, and 2. The median is 50.514 MHz versus the champion's
46.673 MHz. Logic fell from 2909 to 2880 with 641 registers unchanged.
Existing decoder and pipeline cocotb runners and all 53 unchanged
normal formal checks passed. The unchanged cosimulation evaluator
passed both available ELFs, including stalled
selftest comparison and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC validation.
The unchanged CoreMark IPC evaluator measured exactly 4,491,485
marker-bracketed cycles for ten iterations, equal to the champion.
These measurements imply fitness 112.466, an 8.23 percent gain over
103.91, exceeding the required 108.68986 acceptance threshold.

Expect approximately 8 percent higher fitness. These are temporary
prototype measurements, not a recorded tournament acceptance; the
implementation phase must reproduce the change and run its full
unchanged gates. The timing benefit comes from actual removal of
instruction masking and control dependencies, with unchanged useful
work and arithmetic latency. Remaining risks are placement variation,
another arithmetic path becoming critical, and incorrect stall/flush
priority when implementing invalid-payload clearing. Keep canonical
CRCs, validation text, timing brackets, and all formal checks intact.

title: Localize fetch squashing at the ID/EX control boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 103.91 at 46.673 MHz with 4,491,485 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Prior structural changes shortened division, but
the timing limit now includes a front-end control loop. A local
make timing TARGET=bench reproduced placement-0 Fmax of 46.361 MHz.
Its worst path crosses the multiplier at 26.865 ns, while a nearly
identical 26.864 ns path crosses register-file read, forwarding,
branch resolution, IF instruction masking, load-use detection, and
the ID operand-register reset. Replacing a killed fetch with a NOP
sends a late redirect back through source-address and hazard logic.
Moving squash handling to the receiving pipeline boundary should
shorten this feedback without increasing instruction cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the IF-to-ID bubble protocol so instruction data travels
independently of squash control. Represent a missing or killed fetch
with its valid bit, and make ID/EX control capture the point where
invalid work becomes inert. This is one structural change to the
front-end control topology: move the kill boundary from the wide
fetch instruction bus to the registered decoded-control boundary.
Keep the current pipeline depth, acceptance schedule, register file,
forwarding, arithmetic units, and branch policy.

In if_stage.sv, drive out.instr directly from imem_data even during
flush or redirect. Keep out.pc tied to the current PC and retain
out.valid = !(flush || redirect). Preserve reset priority, redirect
priority over stall, and ordinary PC advance only when not stalled.
Remove the NOP-substitution mux from instruction and register-file
address paths. Do not recreate squash gating on these data paths.

In id_stage.sv, preserve reset/flush priority over hold and capture.
When capture is allowed, assign reg_q.ctrl = in.valid ? ctrl_decoded
: '0, and capture reg_q.valid = in.valid. Other payload fields retain
their current capture behavior; their values are irrelevant when
valid is zero. A held ID/EX instruction retains all controls and
operands, including a held divide or an instruction behind a stalled
memory operation. A redirect or load-use flush still clears ID/EX.

Clearing every invalid decoded control is essential. hazard_unit
reads id_ex.ctrl.mem_read without qualifying it by id_ex.valid.
Merely clearing valid would let raw stalled imem_data create a ghost
load dependency after fetch resumes. EX must retain its existing
fully inert EX/MEM bubble for invalid input because memory and
forwarding consumers are not universally valid-qualified. Keep the
decoder's default-illegal policy and all checks on valid encodings;
sanitizing an invalid fetch must not legalize a valid illegal opcode.

Keep current hazard priorities. Raw source fields of an invalid
fetch may alias a load destination, but during imem backpressure the
PC is already held and either load-use flush or invalid-control
capture creates an inert ID/EX bubble. A real dmem hold preserves
the current instruction. An accepted EX redirect uses the existing
flush_id to squash the younger slot regardless of raw source fields.
Check these cases explicitly instead of depending on fabricated NOP
operands. Preserve reset, traps, x0, both bus handshakes, memory
effects, forwarded operands, nret=1 RVFI, contiguous order, and all
arithmetic and divider real/ALTOPS behavior and timing.

A minimal proposal-stage probe with direct instruction transport and
valid-qualified ID control capture achieved Gowin Fmax values of
49.478, 49.050, and 49.050 MHz for placement options 0, 1, and 2.
The 49.050 MHz median is 5.09 percent above the champion's 46.673.
Logic count was 2,875 versus 2,909, with 641 registers in both.
The existing pipeline test runner passed on this exact two-line
RTL probe. This is not a complete formal or CoreMark evaluation.
Expect unchanged bracketed cycles because accepted instructions and
pipeline latencies are unchanged. At the champion's cycle count,
the measured median projects about 109.21 iterations per second.
Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle
greater than 108.68986; at 4,491,485 cycles for ten iterations this
means median Fmax greater than 48.81789 MHz. Estimate a 5 percent
fitness gain. The margin is narrow; rerun the full median and actual
marker-bracketed cycles after implementation. The probe's RTL changes

title: Sixteen-entry agree prediction with instruction-derived branch bias
motivation:
The current champion scores 103.91 at 46.673 MHz and 4,491,485 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. All three previous predictor attempts reduced cycles to
4,202,272, but their timing cost prevented selection over the concurrent
arithmetic champions. Even the direction-only, locally updated 128-entry
predictor in r3s2 lowered Fmax from its own parent's 41.919 to 40.725 MHz.
Its 6.9% instruction-throughput benefit leaves only about 2.1% allowable
clock loss above the 4.6% acceptance threshold. The promising next step is
to retain that accuracy with a substantially smaller direction table.

A proposal-stage reference-interpreter trace of the canonical compiled
2K CoreMark program contains 529,588 conditional branches, 49,367 JALs,
and 13,735 JALRs between the MMIO markers. Offline direction replay gave
54,452 misses for a cold 128-entry bimodal table and 55,124 misses for a
cold 16-entry agree table biased by the instruction's displacement sign.
This supports reducing counter storage from 256 bits to 32 bits with
almost unchanged accuracy. These are architectural trace-model results,
not measured RTL cycles, formal results, or FPGA timing measurements.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a compact instruction-biased agree predictor to the existing fused
fetch/decode stage. This is one predictor architecture change: replace
absolute taken/not-taken learning with learning agreement with a branch's
own static direction bias, allowing just sixteen two-bit counters indexed
by fetch PC[5:2]. Use backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias, where bias is
the raw branch instruction's bit 31. Counter MSB one predicts agreement
with that bias; MSB zero predicts its inverse. Equivalently, conditional
predicted_taken = bias XNOR counter[1]. Reset every counter to 2'b10,
weakly agree. Train toward agreement when actual_taken equals bias and
toward disagreement otherwise, with conventional unsigned saturation.
Oppositely biased branches sharing a counter can reinforce each other
instead of fighting over an absolute direction. No benchmark PC constants
or instruction-address-specific initialization are permitted.

Predict only legal BRANCH encodings using this table. Predict direct JAL
taken unconditionally, obtaining both B and J targets from the current
raw instruction's sign-extended immediate plus the full 32-bit fetch PC.
Require word-aligned direct targets before selecting them. JALR and all
other instructions predict PC+4; reserved branch encodings and misaligned
direct targets retain sequential prediction and existing trap handling.
No target cache, return stack, global history, added stage, or arithmetic
change is part of this proposal.

Implement sixteen constant-index counter cells with local saturating
next-state logic and synchronous update enables. Only their MSBs feed
the 16:1 asynchronous prediction lookup. Avoid a second indexed table
read for training and avoid same-cycle update-to-prediction bypass.
Export resolving PC[5:2], the resolving instruction's own displacement
sign, and actual branch outcome from EX; preferably reduce the latter
two to one agreement bit there. Update exactly once when a valid, legal,
non-faulting conditional branch advances in EX. EX advance requires
!reset && !stall_ex_mem && !execute_wait. Bubbles, jumps, held branches,
and pending divides must not train. Read-before-write behavior is valid.

Carry only the actual selected predicted_taken bit through if_id_t and
id_ex_t. Keep it with the instruction on every hold and clear it with
bubbles, reset, and flush. Because direct targets are reconstructed from
the same PC/immediate at fetch and EX, direction agreement implies target
agreement for the supported transfers. No saved 32-bit target or target
equality comparator is necessary. Alignment suppression must also clear
predicted_taken. Derive prediction from raw imem_data, not the instruction
masked by flush, to avoid a combinational loop through recovery/hazards.

EX remains authoritative: compute actual_taken for a legal, non-faulting
taken branch or jump and recover on actual_taken XOR predicted_taken,
qualified by valid EX advance. An unpredicted JALR still redirects as
today. A wrongly predicted taken branch recovers to PC+4; a missed taken
transfer recovers to its resolved target. Preserve the current sequential
PC rule on target-misalignment traps. Direction disagreement when a direct
target equals PC+4 may conservatively cause a harmless recovery bubble.
Preserve PC+4 link writes even for correctly predicted JAL, and always
report the resolved architectural successor through RVFI pc_next.

Fetch-PC priority is reset, accepted EX recovery, then ordinary accepted
prediction. Normal PC advance and ID/EX capture must use the same lookup
at the same acceptance edge, with no advance on imem backpressure,
load-use replay, dmem freeze, or execute_wait. An older branch may update
the table while fetch waits: use the lookup at eventual acceptance, not
a stale earlier prediction. Suppress recovery and training during dmem
holds. On release, recovery overrides imem backpressure and squashes the
younger slot before it can execute, issue a data access, launch a divide,
or retire. Correct predictions retain that younger instruction. Preserve
MEM/WB forwarding-data retention, divider operand capture and completion,
all arithmetic paths and latencies, decoder legality, and nret=1.

Expect about 7% higher fitness if the previous cycle savings transfer
while the much smaller table protects Fmax. The cold trace model removes
approximately 288,668 redirect events, suggesting roughly 4.203 million
cycles if each event saves one cycle; actual stalled RTL can differ.
Fitness must exceed 108.68986 to beat 103.91 by 4.6%. At approximately
4.203 million cycles for ten iterations this requires about 45.68 MHz.
Thus this proposal still needs close to the champion's clock rate, and
confidence is medium. Added direct-target arithmetic, recovery routing,
aliasing on other code, and Gowin placement remain risks. Evaluate the
actual median vendor Fmax times bracketed iterations/cycle, preserving
every existing formal, cosim, canonical CRC/UART, marker, and stall gate.

title: Isolate memory addresses from the general ALU result mux
motivation:
The champion scores 113.18 at 47.574 MHz with 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. A fresh Gowin option-0 baseline reproduced 46.485 MHz
and its 26.807 ns worst path. The detailed report crosses register-file
output, operand muxes, the unsigned multiply DSP and general result
selection before reaching a data-memory address input. A divider path
to the same memory is nearly tied. Loads/stores need only forwarded
rs1 plus immediate, yet the memory interface uses the general ALU result.

Prior micro_opt history shows that fewer arithmetic cells do not ensure
better timing: the r3 borrow-prefix rewrite regressed, while the r4
fetch-bubble optimization improved its parent but was superseded by
the predictor champion. Separate address transport from general result
transport at the existing EX/MEM boundary to shorten the timed circuit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 32-bit effective_addr field to ex_mem_t and drive it from an
independently controlled EX/MEM address register. Its input is the
full, unmasked, modulo-2^32 sum of forwarded rs1 and in.imm. Reuse the
existing jalr_sum signal, which already computes exactly this sum.
Do not use jump_target: JALR bit-zero clearing would corrupt byte
accesses. Keep the original alu_result path for forwarding, integer
and M-extension results, links and writeback.

Use precisely this address-register schedule:
  if (reset) effective_addr_q <= 32'b0;
  else if (!stall) effective_addr_q <= jalr_sum;
Here stall is the existing EX/MEM dmem hold. Do not qualify this data
register by in.valid, execute_wait, div_consume, recovery or memory-op
decode. Existing control and valid registers retain every original
reset, hold, divide-completion and bubble rule. An unused address can
change during bubbles or division, when memory controls are inert.
A real dmem stall must hold the address together with its request.

A concrete implementation retains reg_q and its original updates,
declares effective_addr_q separately, and constructs out by copying
reg_q then overriding out.effective_addr = effective_addr_q. This
gives the address its independent capture enable at the same pipeline
boundary. The overridden reg_q.effective_addr is not a second functional
driver. Add no stage or instruction latency.

In mem_stage use effective_addr for dmem_addr, byte-lane masks,
alignment checking, byte/halfword extraction and aligned RVFI memory
addresses. Retain in.alu_result for MEM/WB alu_result and non-memory
writeback. Preserve full address width, byte offsets, store replication,
misalignment traps, request suppression and handshake timing. For every
actual load/store the new address equals the old alu_result, since
legal memory instructions select ADD of forwarded rs1 and immediate.
Idle addresses can differ with read/write requests inactive. Preserve
every bounds check and RVFI assertion.

This is one local datapath/control optimization. Keep the sixteen-entry
agree predictor, forwarding, load-use rules, decoder legality,
arithmetic, real and ALTOPS divider schedules, retirement order and
nret=1 external interface unchanged. Draining forwarding sources during
a divide may change the unused address but must never issue a request.

title: Bank EX/MEM results and select them after the arithmetic registers
motivation:
The champion scores 113.18 at median 47.574 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. The previous structural divider changes succeeded,
but the bottleneck has moved beyond the divider recurrence. A fresh
Gowin placement-option-0 run reproduces 46.485 MHz: the worst path is
26.807 ns from register-file BSRAM through operand selection, the
unsigned multiplier DSP, the execute result mux, and the data-memory
BSRAM address input. The next three paths start in divider remainder
state and end at the same memory address input, within 0.06 ns of the
worst path. Both arise because EX/MEM.alu_result carries arithmetic
results as well as effective addresses, and mem_stage drives it onto
dmem_addr even for non-memory instructions. Registering functional-unit
results before their common selection mux can shorten both arithmetic
paths. A dedicated registered memory-address channel is necessary to
preserve block-RAM inference when selection moves after the registers.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single shared EX/MEM result register with parallel result
banks, moving functional-unit result selection after their registers.
This is one restructuring of the EX/MEM boundary by result producer and
consumer: an ordinary ALU bank, a divider-completion bank, a PC+4 link
bank, and a separately registered effective-address channel for memory.
Keep the same pipeline depth, instruction acceptance/retirement edges,
branch policy, forwarding interface, and nine-clock divide schedule.

In ex_stage, add three 32-bit result registers and a three-bit one-hot
registered selector. On reset clear all banks and the selector. On an
actual dmem stall hold every bank and selector together with EX/MEM.
Otherwise use the existing EX/MEM event priority: div_consume captures
div_result into the divider bank and selects it; execute_wait or invalid
EX input clears only the selector; a normal jump captures PC+4 into the
link bank and selects it; every other normal instruction captures the
existing combinational alu_result into the ALU bank and selects it.
Unselected banks retain their values. The ordinary bank includes the
existing integer and multiply results and the existing results on
loads/stores. Do not add a special memory-instruction zero-result mux.

Expose out.alu_result as the parallel AND/OR of these registered banks
masked by their registered one-hot selector. An all-zero selector emits
zero for a bubble. Remove the obsolete shared result-register writes
from the metadata register; avoid recreating the original pre-register
divider/link/ordinary-result mux. Keep all other EX/MEM metadata and
controls governed by their original priorities. In particular, divider
consumption still transfers the captured div_metadata_q exactly once.
Result selection cannot depend on a younger instruction's live controls.
Forwarding and MEM/WB receive the selected value at the same cycle as
before. No change to the ALU's internal operation selection is required.

Add a full-width effective_addr field to ex_mem_t. In EX, compute it
from the already-forwarded rs1 plus the decoded sign-extended immediate
using a dedicated address-generation adder. Capture it on every normal
EX/MEM instruction advance alongside memory controls and store data;
preserve the existing whole-bundle reset, bubble, hold, and divider
metadata behavior. This memory channel must bypass the new post-register
result mux. It must not come from alu_result, div_result, or a multiply
output. This separation is integral to the banked boundary: a probe with
post-register result selection driving the existing shared dmem address
prevented Gowin from inferring the wrapper's memory as block RAM and
exceeded device capacity. Do not change the wrapper or force memory
mapping with a timing exception; provide a directly registered address.

Route every memory-address consumer in mem_stage from effective_addr:
the external byte address, byte-lane masks, load extraction offset,
alignment-fault detection, and word-aligned RVFI memory address. Keep
the existing load data, store replication, writeback, and trap rules.
The address adder must use the exact post-forwarding source consumed
by the instruction, including MEM/WB load forwarding. Preserve full
32-bit addition, wraparound, immediate sign extension, and MMIO; do not
truncate to the FPGA wrapper's local memory index. Sharing the simple
addition itself with another equal expression is harmless, but the
address channel must bypass the common arithmetic-result mux.

A valid load/store captures its effective address on normal EX advance.
Hold its address and all request controls throughout dmem backpressure,
releasing them together on the existing acceptance edge. Reset,
flush-generated bubbles, invalid EX input, and divider-wait bubbles
retain the current inert memory controls. Divider metadata/completion
must never launch a memory operation. Non-memory instructions may
carry an unobserved address value, but that value must not be selected
from an arithmetic result. Do not add a downstream alu_result fallback
or an operation-result mux to the external address path. Preserve
captured RVFI source values, nret=1, contiguous channel-0 retirement,
x0, legal/illegal decoding, branch behavior, and both bus handshakes.
Keep all real and ALTOPS arithmetic formulas and execution schedules.

The complete proposal-stage RTL probe achieved Gowin Fmax values of
51.360, 50.356, and 50.356 MHz for placement options 0, 1, and 2. Its
50.356 MHz median is 5.85 percent above the champion's 47.574 MHz.
Option 0 uses 3,165 logic cells and 774 registers, versus 3,181 and
675 in the parent, with unchanged eight LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs, and six
DSPs. The worst path has moved to branch recovery and register-file
control; multiplier and divider paths now end at their own result-bank
registers. Address separation alone reached only 49.393 MHz median,
below acceptance, so retain both parts of the banked boundary.

The complete banked-boundary probe passed all 23 existing pipeline
cocotb cases and full retirement-trace cosimulation of selftest plus
random1/random2/random3, each with and without both bus stall streams.
Its canonical -O3 2K CoreMark run passed all CRCs and validation text,
reached EBREAK without out-of-bounds access, and measured exactly
4,203,513 cycles between markers, identical to the parent. Combining
those measured cycles with the measured median clock gives 119.795
iterations/second, 5.84 percent above 113.18. The temporary RTL probe
was restored after measurement; implement this proposal normally.

Expect about 6 percent higher fitness with unchanged instruction cycles.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 118.38628,
or about 49.764 MHz at that cycle count. Remaining branch recovery,
operand forwarding, divider recurrence, output selection on forwarding
paths, and placement sensitivity are risks; the acceptance margin is
modest. Judge the final median Gowin Fmax times measured CoreMark
iterations/cycle, including all existing stall logic. Full formal and
final implementation evaluation remain required; these timing results
are proposal-stage evidence, not an accepted tournament outcome.

Validate byte, halfword, and word accesses; signed/unsigned loads;
misalignment traps with no external request; negative immediates;
MMIO markers; arithmetic/load/divide producers of base addresses;
load-use interlocks; and prolonged dmem stalls coincident with imem
stalls. Alternate ordinary ALU, multiply, divide, and jump results with
immediate dependent consumers to expose stale-bank selection, including
consecutive divides, x0 destinations, bubbles, reset during a divide,
wrong-path operations, and held completion. Check exact RVFI operands,
results, PCs, addresses, masks, data, and no duplicated stores or
retirements. Run unchanged formal and stalled cosim/CoreMark gates,
including canonical CRCs, validation text, and timing brackets. Compare
the candidate's critical paths with the reproduced parent report.

title: Reuse the predictor's direct target through an acceptance-latched target field
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct JAL and uses sixteen two-bit agree
counters for conditional branches, achieving 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark
cycles at 47.574 MHz and fitness 113.18. Prior 128-entry predictors lost
timing margin, and the recorded architectural trace estimates only
55,124 remaining conditional-direction misses: perfect direction alone
would save about 1.3% of current cycles. Predictor hardware cost is the
more promising angle than increasing direction-table complexity.

Fetch already computes the exact full-width PC-relative destination for
every direct branch/JAL, independently of its predicted direction. EX
nevertheless reconstructs the same destination with another PC-plus-
immediate adder. Reusing that instruction-derived destination removes
redundant target arithmetic from the recovery network while retaining
the champion's prediction behavior. Proposal-stage probes found this
variant better than smaller tables, static prediction, one-bit training,
or single-bit recovery squash, although none cleared the acceptance bar.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a direct_target field to the combinational IF/ID bundle and its own
acceptance-latched field in ID/EX. Drive it from the existing IF
direct_target = pc + direct_imm computation on raw imem_data. Capture
this value alongside the instruction and predicted_taken at the same
edge; hold it on every ID/EX stall and clear it with reset/flush.
Preserve the existing immediate field and every current capture enable.
This is one predictor-datapath change: reuse the front end's exact
instruction-derived destination for direct-transfer resolution.

Carry the raw computed destination even for a predicted-not-taken
conditional branch and even when target alignment suppresses prediction.
It must not be next_pc, the selected prediction, or an aligned/truncated
version of the destination. EX needs the original low target bits to
preserve misalignment traps, and a missed taken branch needs its real
target rather than PC+4. Use all 32 target bits, including wraparound.

In EX replace branch_target = in.pc + in.imm with the captured
in.direct_target. For JAL select the same captured direct_target. For
JALR retain the forwarded rs1 + original immediate computation and bit-0
clearing. Preserve all existing branch comparisons, legality checks,
misalignment detection, actual_taken, direction-XOR recovery, PC+4 link
writes and resolved architectural pc_next. Direction prediction remains
speculative; this target is exact for its accepted direct instruction
because it was calculated from that instruction's PC and immediate.
No BTB, target alias, target prediction, or target-match comparator is
introduced. Non-control instructions ignore the new field.

Keep the sixteen PC[5:2]-indexed agreement counters, displacement-sign
bias, saturation, reset value, local training and read-before-write
behavior unchanged. Keep JALR sequential prediction, one-shot training
on valid non-faulting EX advance, immediate recovery priority over imem
stalls, and all current squash and memory/divider hold rules. Do not
combine this proposal with counter resizing or recovery retiming. Keep
nret=1, decoded immediates, real/ALTOPS arithmetic, decoder defaults,
forwarding and all retirement invariants unchanged.

An exact temporary prototype with a separate ID/EX direct_target field
measured Gowin placement frequencies 46.472, 48.336 and 48.336 MHz,
for median 48.336 MHz. Logic fell from 3,181 to 3,070; registers rose
from 675 to 706. The existing 23-test pipeline suite passed. The
unchanged CoreMark IPC evaluator passed canonical CRC/UART and marker
validation and measured exactly 4,203,513 cycles for ten iterations
with both buses stalled. This projects fitness 114.9895, approximately
1.60% above 113.18. These are proposal-stage measurements, not a recorded
tournament acceptance. The exact separate-field variant has not yet
completed the full formal and full-trace cosim gates.

Expect about 2% fitness improvement with low confidence in acceptance.
The measured probe does NOT exceed the required 4.6% margin: fitness
must exceed 118.38628, requiring about 49.765 MHz at unchanged cycles.
The unchanged multiplier/forwarding path remains clock-limiting, so
removing target logic may not provide enough timing headroom. Prefer
this narrowly scoped, measured predictor improvement to claiming an
unsupported gain above the threshold; the implementation phase must
rerun the actual median and all unchanged correctness gates.

Extend the existing prediction scoreboard to check that accepted
direct_target metadata matches independent full-width PC-plus-immediate
calculation and stays paired with its instruction under stalls. Cover
correctly predicted and mispredicted branches, predicted-not-taken
branches that resolve taken, direct JAL links, JALR fallback, targets
equal to PC+4, negative displacements, address carry/wrap boundaries,
misaligned direct targets, reserved encodings, reset, load-use replay,
imem backpressure on recovery, dmem release and divider holds. Retain
wrong-path store/divide/illegal-instruction checks and exact RVFI PC,
order, operand, trap and progress assertions. Preserve every formal,
cosim, canonical CRC/UART, memory-bound and marker-only timing gate.

title: Keep register-file reads asynchronous and independent of recovery
motivation: The champion scores 121.67 at 51.146 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its register file is mapped to block RAM with operand registers absorbed into the memory implementation. Detailed Gowin reports show nearly tied multiplier and branch-recovery paths starting at register-file block RAM; recovery also feeds the fetched-instruction NOP mux and returns through register-file read addressing. The prior micro_opt hyp-20261003-001-r4s0 removed that masking globally and gained on its older parent, but a fresh whole-payload-squash probe on this champion regressed to 47.842 MHz. Target the register-file read implementation directly while retaining the established instruction-validity and decode protocol.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the existing 32x32, two-read/one-write integer register file as asynchronous distributed RAM, using Gowin's supported syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" attribute on regs. Keep the ID/EX operand registers as the existing pipeline boundary. Preserve the exact register-file behavioral RTL: synchronous reset clears all architectural registers, x0 always reads zero and ignores writes, and a matching same-cycle WB write bypasses the stored value. Do not introduce vendor primitives, clocks, pipeline stages, latency, or any change to architectural reset semantics.

For this asynchronous read implementation, drive only u_rf.rs1_addr and u_rf.rs2_addr directly from io_imemData[19:15] and [24:20]. Disconnect the now-unused id_stage read-address outputs and remove their top-level wires. Keep IF's instruction-to-NOP mux, IF/ID validity, decoder inputs, ID/EX capture and flush priorities, raw load-use comparisons, prediction, branch training, and all EX forwarding unchanged. An asynchronous RAM must not sit after a late recovery-dependent address mux: the direct addresses are integral to this mapping change. The attribute alone measured only 42.786 MHz, while direct addresses alone measured 50.962 MHz.

Every accepted valid instruction has identical raw and masked source fields. On a killed or unready fetch, arbitrary register-read values are harmless because the existing invalid-instruction/bubble protocol suppresses execution and retirement; retain that protocol verbatim. During dmem or divider holds, ID/EX retains its old operands regardless of changing raw fetch addresses. Preserve the current write-first bypass, held MEM/WB forwarding information, independent effective-address register and dmem hold behavior, arithmetic and ALTOPS schedules, trap checks, and nret=1 interface and RVFI order. No benchmark, wrapper, timing constraints, or decoder legality changes are needed.

A proposal-stage implementation measured 53.023, 53.438, and 53.438 MHz for Gowin placement options 0, 1, and 2. Its median is 53.438 MHz versus the reproduced parent median of 51.146 MHz. It uses 3,335 logic cells, 668 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs, versus 3,080/707/eight/six/six for the parent. The worst paths now cross forwarding/multiplication or divider completion rather than register-file recovery feedback. All 53 unchanged formal checks, register-file and pipeline unit runners, and cosimulation of five ELFs passed. The canonical stalled CoreMark run passed CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and retained exactly 4,203,513 bracketed cycles.

This prototype gives about 4.48 percent higher fitness, just below the required 4.6 percent acceptance margin. The integer expectation is 5 percent, with medium confidence; no tournament acceptance is claimed. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 127.26682, or median Fmax above 53.4968 MHz at unchanged cycles. Remaining arithmetic timing and routing sensitivity are the main risks. Reproduce the final median and actual benchmark cycles, and preserve every unchanged correctness gate. Temporary RTL edits were restored after testing; implement this proposal normally. Keep load-use detection unchanged, including comparisons of both raw source fields: the unchanged full-trace cosim checks their RVFI values even for instructions with an unused source. title: Retiming forwarding decisions into the ID/EX register
motivation:
The champion scores 121.67 at median 51.146 MHz and 4,203,513
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path runs from
register-file storage through execute and branch recovery back to
register-file control. Prior structural divider improvements moved the
bottleneck, and round-five result banking also exposed this recovery
path. The current EX forwarding decision performs destination compares
and priority selection before operand muxing, arithmetic, and branch
resolution. Those register identities are already available one cycle
earlier. Registering the selections with the consumer can remove this
control depth without increasing instruction or recovery latency.
