hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move forwarding dependency resolution from EX into the preceding
decode interval, storing two two-bit selectors in ID/EX. Keep the actual
forwarded data muxes in EX and retain their existing encoding: 0 selects
the captured register-file value, 1 selects EX/MEM.alu_result, and 2
selects the MEM/WB writeback value. This is one retiming of the operand
forwarding boundary; preserve the pipeline depth, predictor, recovery,
load-use interlock, register file, address channel, and divider schedule.

For an instruction being accepted into ID/EX, compare its raw fetched
rs1/rs2 fields against the current ID/EX destination for the next-cycle
EX/MEM source, and against the current EX/MEM destination for the
next-cycle MEM/WB source. Use the existing forward_unit priority logic
and x0 exclusions. Rewire its source inputs to io_imemData[19:15] and
io_imemData[24:20], its first producer to id_ex_w.rd, and its second
producer to ex_mem_w.rd. Do not add a redirect-dependent instruction
mask to these raw comparison inputs. EX receives the selectors stored
in id_ex_w, not the live outputs of forward_unit.

Producer eligibility must describe the control that will be registered
at the receiving boundary, including trap suppression. Expose an EX
next_reg_write output equal to in.valid AND ctrl_with_trap.reg_write,
and a MEM next_reg_write output equal to ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. Feed
these respectively to the existing comparator's ex_mem_w_en and
mem_wb_w_en inputs. The EX flag includes jump-target misalignment
suppression; the MEM flag includes misaligned load suppression. Do not
use raw decoder reg_write for these decisions. MEM eligibility must
retain the parent's distinction between forwarding state and retirement
valid; do not replace it with wb_w_en or add a mem_wb.valid qualifier.

Capture both selectors on exactly the existing ID/EX capture edge.
Reset and flush clear them with the bundle; ID/EX holds retain them.
When decode accepts, the older stages advance together, so the compared
producer identities become the selected sources on the next cycle.
During a dmem hold, EX/MEM and the retained MEM/WB forwarding fields stay
stable with ID/EX. During divider execution, source values are already
saved at request acceptance; keep that metadata capture and request/
completion schedule unchanged. When the divider completes, a following
consumer captures selector 1 and receives the newly registered result.
Preserve the load-use bubble: an immediately dependent load consumer is
accepted only when the load will be in MEM/WB, selecting 2. Correctly
predicted transfers, recovered transfers, imem bubbles and held slots
must keep their existing acceptance and retirement cycles.

A proposal-stage implementation of this exact five-RTL-file change
achieved Gowin Fmax values 51.936, 56.239, and 56.239 MHz for placement

champion's 51.146 MHz. Option 0 uses 3,118 logic cells and 701 registers,

cocotb runner passed all 27 cases, and all 53 unchanged normal formal
checks passed. The unchanged cosim evaluator passed selftest retirement
comparison with and without stalls and the canonical stalled CoreMark
CRC/UART validation. CoreMark measured exactly 4,203,513 bracketed
cycles for ten iterations, identical to the champion. Combining this
cycle count with the measured median gives 133.79 iterations/second,
about 9.96 percent above 121.67. These are proposal-stage measurements,
not tournament acceptance. Temporary RTL was restored after measuring;
implement the proposal normally and rerun the unchanged gates.

Expect approximately 10 percent higher fitness at unchanged bracketed
cycles. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 127.26682, about
53.499 MHz at the champion's cycle count. Principal risks are selector
misalignment under holds or bubbles, incorrect eligibility on a fault,
and placement sensitivity with remaining divider and recovery paths.
Preserve all top-level nret=1 ports, contiguous channel-0 retirement,

and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket checks. Require unchanged

title: Move predictor squash to a registered EX kill bit and keep fetch data unmasked
motivation:
The champion's recorded worst path crosses EX branch resolution, IF
recovery masking and register-file control. Its sixteen-entry agree
predictor already captures most available direction benefit: prior
architectural tracing estimated only 55,124 conditional misses and 13,735
JALRs against 4,203,513 bracketed cycles. Accuracy alone offers too little
headroom. The previous direct-target reuse attempt gained only 1.60
percent. Retiming the predictor's squash action, while keeping PC repair
immediate, can break the feedback path through fetch decoding and
register-file reads without adding a misprediction bubble or violating the
existing ten-clock divide-successor progress bound.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's recorded worst path crosses EX branch resolution, IF
recovery masking and register-file control. Its sixteen-entry agree
predictor already captures most available direction benefit: prior
architectural tracing estimated only 55,124 conditional misses and 13,735
JALRs against 4,203,513 bracketed cycles. Accuracy alone offers too little
headroom. The previous direct-target reuse attempt gained only 1.60
percent. Retiming the predictor's squash action, while keeping PC repair
immediate, can break the feedback path through fetch decoding and
register-file reads without adding a misprediction bubble or violating the
existing ten-clock divide-successor progress bound.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the existing sixteen-entry agree predictor and all target and
direction calculations. Split recovery into immediate PC repair and a one-
cycle-delayed annulment of the wrong-path EX slot. A valid, advancing EX
misprediction still redirects the IF PC register to resolved_pc_next at
the same edge as today. However, that combinational redirect must no
longer mask the IF instruction, alter source-register addresses, clear IF
valid/predicted_taken, or flush ID/EX. Instead, register a single kill_ex
bit from the accepted redirect. No new target register, predicted-target
metadata, target mux or ordinary pipeline stage is needed.

On the misprediction edge, the resolving branch/jump advances normally to
EX/MEM, the PC captures its architectural successor, and the current
younger wrong-path instruction may enter ID/EX. During the following
cycle, kill_ex annuls that younger EX instruction before any side effect
while fetch/decode already sees the repaired PC. At the next edge, EX/MEM
receives a complete inert bubble and ID/EX accepts the repaired target
instruction. This is the same single lost execute slot as the present
design, which inserts that bubble directly into ID/EX one edge earlier.
Correct predictions remain unchanged.

Implement kill_ex as reset-to-zero state assigned from redirect every
clock; redirect itself is qualified by !kill_ex, valid, !reset, !stall and
!execute_wait. Suppress predictor training and further recovery for the
annulled EX slot. Exclude kill_ex instructions from is_div so they cannot
launch or consume division, assert execute_wait, or capture divider
metadata. In the EX/MEM update, preserve reset and older dmem-hold
priority, then clear all control bits and validity for the annulled slot
while letting unused datapath fields capture normally. Do not add a kill-
controlled clear to arithmetic result data. Do not merely clear valid
because memory and forwarding consumers are not uniformly validity
qualified. Keep the independently controlled effective-address register on
its original reset/hold/capture schedule; its unused sum is harmless with
memory controls zero.

The annulled younger instruction must not trigger a load-use stall for the
repaired target. Qualify the existing id_ex_mem_read input to the hazard
unit with id_ex_w.valid && !kill_ex, or apply equivalent gating inside the
hazard unit. Invalid imem slots now carry raw decoded controls, so both
validity and annulment qualification are required. Remove immediate
redirect from flush_if and flush_id: flush_if remains imem backpressure,
and flush_id remains the existing qualified load-use bubble. Preserve
data-memory and divider holds and MEM/WB forwarding-data retention. The
resolving transfer is not a load, so immediate PC recovery cannot conflict
with a real load-use hazard. The one-cycle kill cannot be lost to an older
dmem hold: it is generated only on accepted EX transfer advance, and that
transfer occupying EX/MEM in the kill cycle has no memory request. Still
retain the original older-memory stall priority.

In IF, retain reset then immediate redirect then ordinary accepted
prediction as PC-register priorities. Remove the instruction-to-NOP mux
entirely: out.instr = imem_data, out.valid = !flush, and
out.predicted_taken = predicted_taken && !(reset || flush), where flush is
now imem backpressure only. Thus recovery and unavailable fetches are
represented by registered validity/kill metadata, while the instruction
data and register-file read addresses remain unmasked. Immediate redirect
must not feed these combinational payload fields. Retain the existing EX
execute_wait || !in.valid full-bundle bubble rule so arbitrary controls
decoded from an invalid fetch cannot reach EX/MEM; only a valid but
annulled slot uses control-and-valid-only clearing. The wrong-path
instruction's direction metadata may be captured but is ignored by
kill_ex. On an imem-stalled recovery edge, the PC still repairs and an
invalid slot may be admitted; kill_ex remains harmless. On the following
cycle, an imem stall simply postpones target acceptance without changing
repair or retirement. Keep raw-instruction lookup and all normal
acceptance-edge metadata holds.

Preserve EX training exactly once on the resolving non-faulting branch's
advance. Preserve resolved architectural pc_next and original PC+4 links,
JALR masking, target alignment traps, decoder legality, all arithmetic and
ALTOPS schedules, full addresses, nret=1, and every retirement/memory
invariant. Do not relax the existing ten-clock ready-bus retirement gap or
formal liveness depth; redirected division must retain its current
latency.

A temporary prototype of this exact raw-fetch, separate-kill-bit design
measured Gowin placement frequencies of 49.260, 52.089 and 52.089 MHz, for
a median of 52.089 MHz. Option-0 logic usage was 3,106 with 708 registers,
eight LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs and six DSPs. The adapted pipeline and IF
cocotb suites passed, including an added killed-load dependency and wrong-
path side-effect test that preserves the ten-clock redirected-divide
bound. The unchanged cosim evaluator passed both available ELFs, including
stalled selftest comparison and canonical CoreMark validation. The
unchanged CoreMark IPC evaluator measured exactly 4,203,513 bracketed
cycles for ten iterations, equal to the champion. All 53 unchanged
normal formal checks passed on this exact final prototype.

These measurements project fitness 123.9178, approximately 1.85 percent
above 121.67. Expect about 2 percent improvement, with low confidence in
acceptance: this measured prototype does NOT clear the required 4.6
percent margin. Acceptance at unchanged cycles requires Fmax strictly
above about 53.497 MHz. The remaining measured critical path crosses the
register file, ID and combinational ALU into EX/MEM, so eliminating
predictor-recovery feedback alone may not provide enough clock headroom.
Report this limitation honestly and rerun all unchanged gates during
implementation; do not weaken checks or claim the candidate has won.

MHz. For the proposed design, leave the original invalid-input/divide
bubble schedule intact, use control-and-valid-only clearing specifically

masking from the instruction data bus. Keep the separate kill bit and
original ID/EX validity capture; folding repair into that validity bit was

title: Precompute the first radix-4 digit during divider operand capture
motivation: The champion scores 133.79 at median 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path crosses divider completion from quotient_q[30] to EX/MEM alu_result[30], taking 24.549 ns through 80 cells. Completion currently contains two serial radix-4 digits followed by sign correction. Prior borrow-prefix arithmetic regressed through routing overhead, and proposal-stage experiments with speculative sign correction also regressed. Target the amount of arithmetic on the completion edge while preserving the current external latency and ordinary two-digit recurrence.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 133.79 at median 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path crosses divider completion from quotient_q[30] to EX/MEM alu_result[30], taking 24.549 ns through 80 cells. Completion currently contains two serial radix-4 digits followed by sign correction. Prior borrow-prefix arithmetic regressed through routing overhead, and proposal-stage experiments with speculative sign correction also regressed. Target the amount of arithmetic on the completion edge while preserving the current external latency and ordinary two-digit recurrence.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compute the first radix-4 quotient digit on the existing operand-capture edge, using a small exact predecode of the dividend's top two magnitude bits and the divisor magnitude. Keep the existing seven intermediate clocks of two radix-4 digits each, then use only the first digit of the existing two-digit network for final completion. The total is 1 + 7*2 + 1 = 16 radix-4 digits. Acceptance remains edge 0, intermediate updates remain edges 1 through 7, availability still asserts before edge 8, and direct consumption still occurs at edge 8. This is one local optimization of divider launch/completion arithmetic, with no new pipeline stage, state register, bus protocol, or instruction cycle.

Let A and D be the same unsigned magnitudes already used by the divider, and P=A[31:30]. Since 0 <= P <= 3, compute the initial quotient digit q0 and remainder r0 using only these cases: D=0 gives q0=3,r0=P; D=1 gives q0=P,r0=0; D=2 gives q0={0,P[1]},r0={0,P[0]}; D=3 gives q0=(P==3),r0=(P==3 ? 0 : P); every D>=4 gives q0=0,r0=P. Use explicitly sized unsigned expressions and full-width divisor equality tests, or an equivalent shared high-bit-zero guard plus low-bit decode. Do not truncate D before deciding whether it exceeds three. Share the existing signed-magnitude normalization.

On accepted div_request initialize quotient_q to {A[29:0],q0} and remainder_q to the zero-extended r0. Capture divisor_q, divisor3_q, negate_q, and remainder_op_q exactly as before. Preserve the existing round counter, IDLE/ROUND/DONE transitions, busy/valid logic, reset priority, operand capture, and completion storage. In the seven non-final rounds continue registering digit_quotient[2] and digit_remainder[2]. For final_result only, select digit_quotient[1] or digit_remainder[1] using remainder_op_q, then apply the existing conditional sign correction. Do not change quotient_next/remainder_next globally to one-digit results: the intermediate rounds must still process four bits each. The unused second digit on the final round may evaluate but must not affect completion.

After operand capture two dividend bits have been processed. After intermediate edge e=1..7, exactly 2+4*e bits have been processed; before completion 30 bits are done and one radix-4 digit completes all 32. For each registered boundary, compare quotient and remainder to independent integer division of that consumed dividend prefix. For a zero divisor the consumed quotient prefix is all ones and the remainder is the consumed dividend prefix. These invariants validate both the launch predecode and the shifted recurrence schedule.

Keep signed truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, zero-divisor results, quotient sign suppression for zero divisor, and INT_MIN/-1 behavior. Keep all RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and their exact existing handshake schedule. Preserve forwarded-operand metadata capture, stalled completion, immediate dependent consumers, all top-level nret=1 ports, RVFI order, decoder legality, memory handshakes, and all correctness/progress gates. No changes to EX, forwarding, prediction, register-file mapping, or the multiplier are part of this proposal.

Expect approximately 8 percent higher fitness at unchanged CoreMark cycles. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 139.94434, or approximately 58.83 MHz at the champion's measured cycle count. This is a hypothesis, not an accepted result. The timing benefit is removing one wide subtract/borrow/select layer from the completion-to-EX/MEM path without increasing the depth of the recurring two-digit path. The capture predecode is narrow, but magnitude normalization followed by its divisor-zero/small-divisor tests could become critical. Recurrence, multiplication, branch recovery, and placement sensitivity remain risks.

Run the real and ALTOPS ALU suites with their original external latency/reset/backpressure assertions intact. Update only the internal prefix-state expectations to reflect the intentional initial two-bit step, and add focused D=0,1,2,3,4 tests for each possible P and all operand signs, including INT_MIN. Preserve every existing assertion's arithmetic meaning. Run unchanged pipeline/formal/liveness checks, stalled retirement cosim, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation. Measure all three Gowin placement options and actual marker-bracketed cycles; do not infer a fitness win from fewer logic cells. ALTOPS alone does not prove real arithmetic, so also validate the new launch step exhaustively over its small P/D equivalence classes and retain actual-arithmetic recurrence tests.

title: Replace the inferred register RAM with flop words and balanced reads
motivation: The champion scores 133.79 at median 56.239 MHz with 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Multiple recent timing reports expose a register-file read path through operand capture and execute arithmetic or recovery control. The r6s0 distributed-RAM attempt improved its parent by 4.49 percent but missed acceptance and retained a memory-based read structure. The champion's registered forwarding decisions remove comparator depth from EX, making the remaining register-file storage/read boundary a useful structural target. Current area is only 3,118 LUTs and 701 registers, leaving room to exchange storage density for a shorter clock path.

Current area is only 3,118 LUTs and 701 registers, leaving room to exchange storage density for a shorter clock path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the inferred 32x32 register-file memory with 31 independently instantiated 32-bit flip-flop words, shared by two explicitly balanced combinational read trees. Implement x0 as a constant zero leaf rather than storage. This is one structural storage-and-read topology change inside reg_file.sv. Preserve the module interface, pipeline depth, all instruction acceptance and retirement cycles, and the current reset, write-first bypass, and x0 semantics.

Use a generate block for each architectural word 1 through 31. Each block owns its own local 32-bit value_q register and synchronous always_ff process: reset clears that word; otherwise an enabled write whose address equals the word index captures w_data. Do not declare a dynamically written packed memory array or force a vendor RAM primitive. The purpose is to make the architectural state explicit flops and retain the existing ID/EX operand-register boundary rather than allow a synchronous-memory implementation to absorb it. Confirm the actual mapping in the Gowin reports; source-level naming alone is not evidence of the intended circuit.

For each read port, decode its five-bit source address into one word select per nonzero register. Gate each word's 32-bit value with that select, use a zero leaf for x0, and reduce the 32 leaves through an explicit five-level balanced binary OR tree. Only the selected word contributes. Keep the existing final write-first bypass and x0 priority: a read of zero returns zero even during a write to zero; an enabled matching nonzero WB write returns w_data in the same cycle; otherwise use the read-tree result. Preserve reset-before-write priority and every architectural register's zero reset state. Do not change read addresses, add a new clock or read latency, or alter ID/EX hold/flush behavior.

The intended benefit is to replace the timing-sensitive inferred memory read and control path with ordinary flops and shallow logic, giving placement more freedom while preserving throughput. Extra flops, decode fanout, reset/write distribution, and read-tree routing are the principal costs. This does not presume that more flops are always faster: measure the complete circuit across all three Gowin placement options. Existing multiply/divider and recovery paths may cap the gain.

Preserve nret=1, all external ports, contiguous channel-0 retirement, decoder legality, traps, both bus handshakes, exact real and ALTOPS arithmetic, independent effective-address capture, the champion's registered forwarding selectors, and the ten-cycle ready-bus progress bound. Run existing register-file and pipeline tests, unchanged formal, stalled retirement cosim, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/MMIO-bracket checks. Check all 31 writable registers, both simultaneous reads, zero reads/writes, same-cycle WB bypass, reset/write overlap, consecutive writes, and dependencies across long dmem holds and imem gaps. Expect unchanged CoreMark cycles; do not weaken any checks to accept altered initialization or operand capture.

Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle strictly above 139.94434, approximately 58.828 MHz at the champion's cycle count. The expected gain is an estimate pending complete timing and correctness validation. Keep the change confined to this register-file topology rather than combining unrelated divider or predictor changes.

Retain every current assertion and verify all architectural words through both ports, independent simultaneous reads, matching/nonmatching writes, write-first bypass, x0 immunity, reset/write overlap, and repeated writes. Require identical zero-reset behavior.

Keep all existing architectural, forwarding, memory, and progress assertions. Exercise WB-to-decode reads and dependencies spanning load-use bubbles, division, recovery, and prolonged memory holds, comparing exact RVFI sources, results, order, and once-only retirement.

title: Preselect the opposite prediction offset for immediate branch recovery
motivation:
The champion's sixteen-entry agree predictor already removes most control-flow
bubbles. Prior tracing estimated only 55,124 conditional misses and 13,735
JALRs in 4,203,513 bracketed cycles, leaving little accuracy headroom.
Direct-target reuse and delayed EX annulment previously failed the acceptance
margin. Current EX recovery routes resolved_pc_next to IF: a late
forwarded-operand branch comparison selects a full-width address before PC
repair. On a direction mismatch, the saved prediction already identifies the
required recovery destination. Preparing that address independently is a
narrowly scoped predictor timing hypothesis.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate the speculative recovery-address datapath from the architectural
resolved-next-PC datapath. Preserve the current sixteen-entry agree predictor,
direct-JAL prediction, direction-XOR recovery detection, training, immediate
PC repair, and single-bubble miss penalty. Select the recovery displacement

In ex_stage, compute recovery_offset = in.predicted_taken ? 32'd4 : in.imm and
recovery_direct = in.pc + recovery_offset. Drive redirect_target =
(in.ctrl.is_jalr && !in.predicted_taken) ? {jalr_sum[31:1], 1'b0} :
recovery_direct, reusing the existing full-width forwarded rs1+imm jalr_sum.
Keep redirect = in.valid && ex_advance && (actual_taken ^ in.predicted_taken)
unchanged. Do not add a prediction-inversion field, counter-update register,
target register or pipeline stage.

Correctness follows from the existing mismatch condition: whenever redirect is
asserted, actual_taken is the inverse of in.predicted_taken. A false taken
prediction therefore repairs to PC+4, and a missed taken direct transfer
repairs to PC+imm. An unpredicted legal JALR uses its forwarded target with
bit zero cleared. The !in.predicted_taken qualification on the JALR selection
also preserves sequential recovery if a predicted-taken instruction were to
resolve to a fault. Use the prediction captured with this exact accepted
instruction, never the live table lookup.

The prepared recovery address need equal resolved_pc_next only while redirect
is asserted. Keep the existing actual-outcome calculation of resolved_pc_next
for EX/MEM pc_next and RVFI pc_wdata; do not substitute the speculative
recovery address there. Preserve original PC+4 link writes, branch
comparisons, full 32-bit modular arithmetic, legality checks, JALR masking,
target-misalignment suppression, and sequential architectural next PC on
traps. Preserve the independent effective-address register and all real/ALTOPS
arithmetic.

Leave ex_advance's reset, dmem-stall and execute-wait qualifications intact.
IF retains reset then accepted redirect then ordinary accepted prediction as
PC-update priorities. Recovery still overrides imem backpressure on dmem
release and squashes the younger slot before any side effect. Prediction
metadata holds with its instruction through memory freezes, load-use replay
and division. No accuracy improvement or reduced miss penalty is claimed. Keep
nret=1, retirement order, all bus handshakes and every existing progress bound
and correctness gate.

The intended mechanism removes the actual branch outcome from the wide
recovery-address mux and moves the displacement choice ahead of a PC adder. It
leaves only the one-bit redirect enable dependent on late resolution. This
does not remove the champion's divider/multiplier timing limit, and actual
Gowin results do not currently support a net gain.

An exact temporary prototype passed the existing IF and pipeline cocotb suites
without changing their assertions, plus selftest RVFI cosimulation with ready
buses and with both buses stalled. The unchanged CoreMark IPC evaluator passed

bracketed cycles for ten iterations. Gowin placement options measured 50.671,
53.799 and 53.799 MHz, giving median 53.799 MHz; option-zero usage was 3,170
logic cells, 701 registers, eight LUT RAMs, six BSRAMs and six DSPs. All 53
unchanged normal formal checks also passed. A same-session unchanged-baseline
build reproduced its recorded 56.239 MHz median, confirming the comparison.
These are proposal-stage measurements, not tournament acceptance. The
temporary RTL and test probes have been restored; implement the proposal
normally from the champion.

That measured product is fitness 127.9858, approximately 4.34 percent BELOW

negative result rather than claiming that shorter logical feedback implies a

median; do not relax checks or accept below the required fitness product.

title: Share all multiply variants through one signed 33-bit product
motivation:
The champion reaches 133.79 iterations/second at median 56.239 MHz,
using six DSP resources and 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles.
Its reported placement-option-0 path ends at EX/MEM through divider
completion, but recent experiments expose a competing register-file
to multiplier to EX/MEM path. In particular, the previous micro_opt
that shortened divider completion regressed to 49.741 MHz with that
multiplication path critical. The ALU still describes three separate
signed/signed, unsigned/unsigned, and signed/unsigned products.
Explicit sharing can reduce multiplier resources and output selection
without another divider or pipeline change.

title: Capture parallel execute result banks with only the memory hold
motivation: The champion scores 133.79 at median 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path runs from divider quotient state through 80 cells into the shared EX/MEM arithmetic-result register. Other recent paths enter that register through the multiplier. The r5s1 structural result-banking attempt improved its older parent by 5.85 percent but lost to another tournament candidate; its bottleneck moved to recovery/register-file control. Since then the champion has gained an independent registered memory address and retimed forwarding selectors, which changes the context for placing result selection after arithmetic registers. The proposal tests that single boundary change on the current champion, without increasing instruction latency.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 133.79 at median 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path runs from divider quotient state through 80 cells into the shared EX/MEM arithmetic-result register. Other recent paths enter that register through the multiplier. The r5s1 structural result-banking attempt improved its older parent by 5.85 percent but lost to another tournament candidate; its bottleneck moved to recovery/register-file control. The proposal tests that single boundary change on the current champion, without increasing instruction latency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX/MEM's shared arithmetic-result register with three parallel result banks: ordinary ALU/multiply, completed divide/remainder, and PC+4 link. Register a three-bit one-hot result selector with the same instruction. Drive out.alu_result from a parallel masked-OR of the registered banks. This moves functional-unit selection after the result flops and removes the divider/link selection mux from the ends of both the multiply and divider arithmetic paths. Keep the current ALU internals, registered forwarding decisions, register file, predictor, pipeline depth and nine-clock division schedule.

On reset clear all three banks and the selector. A real dmem stall holds all banks and the selector together with EX/MEM metadata. On EVERY other edge capture alu_result into the ordinary bank, div_result into the divide bank and in.pc+4 into the link bank, regardless of instruction validity, execute_wait, div_consume or is_jump. Unselected values are unobservable. This control-independent data capture is central to the hypothesis: arithmetic-bank enables must depend only on reset and the existing dmem hold, just like the champion's independent effective-address register. Do not gate their capture by operation type, valid, divider completion or bubble controls.

Only the registered selector uses instruction-dependent control. On a non-stalled edge select the divide bank for div_consume; clear the selector for execute_wait or invalid EX input; otherwise select the link bank for a jump and the ordinary bank for any other instruction. Preserve the exact existing EX/MEM metadata priorities, including div_metadata_q on completion, inert bubbles and trap controls. The selected bank captures the corresponding value on the same edge as its selector and metadata. Other banks may capture unused values. Preserve misaligned-jump handling and all suppressed writebacks.

Encode ordinary, divide and link selections as 001, 010 and 100. Compute the visible result as (alu_bank & replicate(sel[0])) OR (div_bank & replicate(sel[1])) OR (link_bank & replicate(sel[2])). The zero selector produces a zero bubble result. Remove the old functional writes to reg_q.alu_result so the synthesized circuit cannot retain a duplicate pre-register selection cone. Result selection must depend only on the registered selector, never the younger ID/EX instruction or live div_consume. Hold all selected data and metadata coherently under backpressure. Existing EX/MEM-to-EX forwarding and MEM/WB capture use the selected bank result on exactly their original cycles.

Keep the champion's independent effective_addr_q register and its full-width forwarded rs1+imm input completely outside this bank selector. Its reset and dmem-hold-only behavior, and every mem_stage address/mask/extraction/alignment consumer, stay unchanged. Earlier result-banking work showed that routing dmem addresses through a post-register arithmetic mux can prevent Gowin BSRAM inference. The separate address channel is already present in this parent; do not reconstruct it or change its capture semantics.

This extends the earlier result-register topology by removing instruction-dependent data-bank enables, on a parent whose forwarding boundary has also changed. The old r5s1 measurements do not apply to the current core. Additional register bits and the post-register forwarding mux can move timing pressure to operand selection, branch recovery or register-file control. Preserve the current forwarding selectors and trap-aware producer eligibility. Do not combine this with divider-radix changes, a multicycle multiplier, a fetch queue or register-file remapping.

Preserve nret=1 and all external ports, exact RV32IM and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arithmetic, default-illegal decoding, trap behavior, x0, both bus handshakes, contiguous channel-0 retirement and every existing progress bound. Divide acceptance, captured operands/metadata, final-round availability and completion retention must be unchanged. A waiting or invalid instruction must still leave all memory controls inert. No formal-depth, liveness, memory-wrapper, benchmark or timing-constraint changes are permitted.

A preliminary banked implementation with instruction-dependent capture enables passed the unchanged pipeline cocotb suite, selftest retirement cosimulation with ready and stalled buses, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/MMIO-bracket validation at exactly 4,203,513 cycles. Its median Fmax was only 55.139 MHz, so that gated-bank version missed acceptance. The final proposal removes those data-bank enables as specified above; that variant must be evaluated separately. Do not attribute the preliminary timing to this refinement or claim tournament acceptance. Final vendor timing and unchanged formal determine whether the new register placement succeeds. Temporary RTL is restored after investigation; implement the described topology from the champion and rerun the gates.

Extend tests by alternating ordinary integer, multiply, divide, JAL and JALR producers followed immediately by dependent ALU operations, branches, stores and memory-base consumers. Cover x0, faults, bubbles, long dmem holds, simultaneous imem stalls, divide completion after backpressure, reset and recovery. Check exact forwarded operands, source metadata, bank selection, results, RVFI order/PCs, and once-only retirement and stores. Keep every existing assertion and the ten-cycle progress bound. Expect unchanged CoreMark cycles. Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle strictly above 139.94434, approximately 58.826 MHz at the champion's cycle count. Report measured timing honestly even if the result misses that threshold.

title: Look ahead one fetch to register the agreement-predictor lookup
motivation:
The champion already removes most control-flow bubbles with sixteen agreement
counters and direct-JAL prediction. Earlier target-reuse, delayed-squash and
opposite-offset recovery experiments failed the acceptance margin. Enlarging the
predictor offers little cycle headroom: prior tracing estimated 55,124 conditional
misses and 13,735 JALRs in 4,203,513 bracketed cycles. A distinct timing opportunity
is the asynchronous counter lookup inside the current fetch-PC feedback loop. Move
that lookup across the existing PC register boundary by preparing a single agreement
bit for the destination PC.

opposite-offset recovery experiments failed the acceptance margin. Enlarging the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the sixteen two-bit agreement counters, immediate EX training,
displacement-sign bias, direct-JAL prediction, and direction-XOR recovery. Add
exactly one predictor state bit, predict_agree_q, alongside the fetch PC. It stores
the counter MSB read for the destination selected at the previous PC-update edge.
Conditional prediction becomes the current raw instruction's displacement sign XNOR
predict_agree_q, still qualified by legal BRANCH encoding and aligned direct target.
Direct JAL remains unconditionally predicted when aligned; JALR remains sequential.

Compute one four-bit next_predict_index: redirect ? redirect_target[5:2] :
predicted_taken ? direct_target[5:2] : pc[5:2] + 4'd1. Read
agree_msb[next_predict_index] and capture it into predict_agree_q only when the PC
register updates. Reset sets the bit to one; otherwise redirect || !stall enables
capture; otherwise hold. Redirect takes priority in both the index mux and PC
update, including during stalls. Select the narrow index before one shared
asynchronous MSB lookup; do not replicate three candidate lookup trees. The table
remains sixteen local counter cells with its existing update logic and no new memory
primitive.

The PC and agreement snapshot must always advance or hold together. Preserve the
full 32-bit PC and existing target additions; the four-bit sequential-index
increment is only predictor indexing and wraps modulo sixteen. A redirect to the
same PC still refreshes the snapshot. Reset sets both PC zero and snapshot one,
matching the counters' weak-agree 2'b10 initialization. Do not insert an instruction
stage, delay recovery, change branch resolution, or register the instruction memory
interface.

Use read-before-write semantics with no EX-training bypass: at a PC-update edge, the
snapshot reads the old counter state even if that same row trains at that edge.
While PC is held for imem backpressure, load-use, dmem freeze or division, keep its
snapshot unchanged even if older branches update its table row. This deliberately
freezes a speculative direction hint for the resident PC. At eventual instruction
acceptance both next-PC selection and captured predicted_taken must use that exact
held bit. EX remains authoritative and recovers every actual direction mismatch, so
stale snapshots can affect accuracy but cannot alter architectural behavior. Never
recompute captured prediction metadata from the live table during a hold.

Keep EX training on each valid, legal, non-faulting conditional branch advance
exactly as in the champion, updating the cell's current two-bit state. Preserve
reset, saturation, no training from held or wrong-path instructions, immediate
recovery over imem stalls, complete younger-slot squash, accepted-instruction
metadata holds, architectural pc_next and link writes, traps, and the existing
ten-clock ready-bus progress bound. Preserve nret=1, external ports, registered
forwarding, independent effective-address capture, all real/ALTOPS arithmetic,
decoder checks, memory handshakes and retirement order.

The intended timing mechanism removes the live 16:1 table selection from the
current-PC-to-predicted-next-PC path, at the cost of one register, a four-bit index
mux and a four-bit sequential-index increment. Prediction refresh and recovery-index
routing may instead become critical, and the unchanged multiplier/divider can still
cap Fmax. This is a timing hypothesis rather than a claim of greater predictor
accuracy.

A temporary prototype of this exact common-index lookahead design measured Gowin
placement frequencies 49.152, 53.311 and 53.311 MHz, with median 53.311 MHz.
Option-zero usage was 3,127 logic cells, 702 registers, eight LUT RAMs, six BSRAMs
and six DSPs. Selftest cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker
validation passed; CoreMark measured 4,203,504 bracketed cycles for ten iterations.
A same-session unchanged-reference build reproduced the champion's 56.239 MHz
median. Both adapted IF/pipeline cocotb suites passed while retaining all
architectural and progress assertions, and all 53 unchanged normal formal checks
passed on this exact prototype. These are proposal-stage measurements, not
tournament acceptance.

That measured product is approximately 126.83 fitness, about 5.2 percent BELOW the
133.79 champion. Expected impact is therefore -5 percent with low confidence in
improvement. This candidate does NOT clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
Acceptance requires a measured product strictly above 139.94434, about 58.826 MHz at
this cycle count. The unchanged divider/multiplier and recovery paths still limit
timing; removal of an asynchronous lookup from one path is not evidence of a
whole-core speedup. Implement and remeasure normally without relaxing any
correctness or timing gates. Temporary RTL and test probes are restored after
validation, leaving this YAML as the deliverable.

motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz with 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent micro_opt attempts on divider completion and
multiplier sharing exposed competing register-file-to-multiply and
recovery-to-register-file paths. The r6s0 distributed-RAM experiment
nearly cleared acceptance before forwarding was retimed, whereas
r7s1's flop register file regressed with recovery-dependent addresses.

distributed storage and removing serial bank and writeback selection.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the existing 32-word register file as two explicit 16x32
distributed-RAM banks, covering x0..x15 and x16..x31. For each read
port, read both banks with address[3:0] and select among low-bank
data, high-bank data and same-cycle WB data using three mutually
exclusive masks and a parallel masked-OR. This is one local storage
mapping and read-mux optimization. Preserve both asynchronous reads,
one synchronous write, the existing ID/EX boundary and all latency.

Mark both arrays with Gowin's supported
syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" attribute. Split writes using
w_addr[4] and index the selected bank with w_addr[3:0]. Preserve the
existing synchronous reset semantics by clearing every bank word on
reset, and retain the write guard w_en && w_addr!=0 with reset taking
priority. Do not substitute uninitialized data or a new reset-valid
bitmap for the existing architectural zero values. Keep x0 hardwired
to zero on reads and discard writes to it.

For each source address r, compute nz=(r!=0) and
hit=w_en && (w_addr==r). Define select_wb=nz && hit,
select_lo=nz && !hit && !r[4], and
select_hi=nz && !hit && r[4]. Produce the read value as
({32{select_wb}} & w_data) OR
({32{select_lo}} & bank_lo[r[3:0]]) OR
({32{select_hi}} & bank_hi[r[3:0]]).
Implement the masks and parallel reduction explicitly; do not build
a bank-output mux followed by another writeback mux and x0 mux.
For x0 all masks are zero; otherwise exactly one is set. Matching
same-cycle writes must win even before the array's write edge,
exactly as in the original write-first interface. Preserve its
behavior during reset as well as after reset.

address outputs and removing obsolete top-level wires. This prevents

have identical raw and masked source addresses. Invalid fetches may
read arbitrary registers but cannot commit those values; held ID/EX
operands remain unchanged during dmem or divider stalls.

Native 16-word banks match the FPGA's distributed-memory granularity.

as WB bypass is intended to remove a serial mux from RAM data to the
existing operand registers. It should also shorten the portion of
recovery feedback that currently enters register-file addressing.

title: Predivide the leading nibble to isolate divider sign correction
motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts in divider quotient
state and ends in EX/MEM after two radix-4 digits and sign correction.
The r8s1 result-banking attempt regressed by 4.90 percent and merely
moved the worst endpoint to the divider's own held-result register:
23.912 ns across 75 cells. This points to the final arithmetic chain,
rather than just its destination mux. Adding a completion clock would
violate the existing redirect-plus-divide progress bound. A specialized
leading-nibble step can free a clock for correction without increasing
the nine-clock execution latency.

hypothesis.motivation:

CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts in divider quotient
state and ends in EX/MEM after two radix-4 digits and sign correction.
The r8s1 result-banking attempt regressed by 4.90 percent and merely
moved the worst endpoint to the divider's own held-result register:
23.912 ns across 75 cells. This points to the final arithmetic chain,
rather than just its destination mux. Adding a completion clock would
violate the existing redirect-plus-divide progress bound. A specialized
leading-nibble step can free a clock for correction without increasing
the nine-clock execution latency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Reschedule the blocking divider so the request-capture edge also resolves
the most significant four dividend bits, seven subsequent clocks each
compute the existing two radix-4 digits, and the ninth EX clock only
selects and sign-corrects a fully registered quotient or remainder.
This is one structural change to division scheduling and register
placement. Preserve the ordinary ALU, multiplier, fetch prediction,
register file, forwarding topology, independent effective-address
register, pipeline depth and all instruction acceptance/retirement cycles.

Let A and D be the existing 32-bit unsigned operand magnitudes and let
N=A[31:28]. At request edge 0, compute the exact quotient nibble q0 and
remainder r0 for N divided by D. If any D[31:4] bit is set, D>=16>N,
hence q0=0 and r0=N. Otherwise use a small, purely combinational 4-bit
unsigned divider for N and D[3:0]. Implement it as four width-bounded
restoring bit steps with five-bit trial/subtraction temporaries, not a
32-bit divider, large variable shift or inferred / or % operator. D=0
naturally produces q0=15 and r0=N. Start the existing recurrence with
quotient_q={A[27:0],q0} and remainder_q=zero_extend(r0). Capture D, 3D,
sign, operation and forwarded instruction metadata exactly as today.
The high-divisor bypass must use the full normalized D; truncating D
before this classification would corrupt unsigned high-bit divisors.

Edges 1 through 7 perform seven rounds of two existing radix-4 digits,
registering quotient_next and remainder_next on every round, including
the last one. Together with the capture nibble this consumes all 32
dividend bits. In the cycle after edge 7, div_valid is high from a
registered completion state and div_result selects quotient_q or
remainder_q and applies the captured sign. Edge 8 consumes that corrected
result into the unchanged EX/MEM register and returns the divider to
IDLE. Thus availability and transfer occur on exactly the champion's
cycles, but no path combines two full-width radix-4 digits with final
negation. Remove the old final-round bypass from quotient_next or
remainder_next into div_result and the corrected-result register that
currently receives the same long chain under backpressure.

If completion is blocked, retain the final raw quotient, remainder,
sign and operation state until consumption; div_result remains stable
through the short correction cone. Keep busy high and ignore additional
requests throughout calculation and held completion. Completion must
depend only on registered state, never div_consume. Reset cancels the
transaction. Preserve single acceptance, single transfer, operand capture
before forwarding sources drain, inert EX/MEM bubbles, real dmem hold
priority and the existing front-end release event. EX must still use the
saved divide metadata and exact source values. Do not add a latency cycle
or special-case ALTOPS to conceal a longer real-arithmetic schedule.

Preserve RV32M signed truncation, dividend-signed remainder, all unsigned
cases, division by zero and INT_MIN/-1. Keep all existing ALTOPS constants
and formulas, executing their results through the identical nine-clock
request/busy/valid/consume schedule. Preserve nret=1, all external ports,
decoder legality, traps, x0, contiguous channel-0 RVFI order, both memory
handshakes and every existing liveness assertion. No evaluation-contract
changes are part of this proposal.

Validate the small leading-nibble circuit exhaustively for all 256 N/D
low-nibble pairs and check the full-width bypass with D>=16, including
high-bit unsigned and normalized signed divisors. Update internal-state
checks to verify four consumed dividend bits immediately after request
and 4+4*k bits after round k, while retaining every arithmetic expected
value, exact nine-clock handshake assertion and ten-clock architectural
progress bound. Exercise final-result backpressure, changing live inputs,
reset in every state, consecutive divides, dependencies and redirect to
divide. Run existing ALU/pipeline tests, unchanged formal and real stalled
CoreMark retirement cosimulation with canonical CRC/UART/bounds/markers.

A standalone integer model of this schedule passed all 256 small-divider
input pairs and 41,296 full-width DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU cases from directed
boundaries and seeded-random operands, checking each registered recurrence
against exact prefix division. This supports the arithmetic construction;
it is not RTL verification, a formal pass or a timing measurement.

Expected benefit is unchanged CoreMark cycles and shorter final-divider
timing. The leading-nibble work lengthens operand capture; magnitude
generation followed by the small divider or the unchanged multiply and
recovery paths may become limiting. Check complete Gowin timing rather
than treating removal of the old endpoint as proof. Acceptance requires
measured median Fmax times iterations/cycle above 139.94434, approximately
58.826 MHz at 4,203,513 cycles. The expected gain below is unmeasured.

title: Compile the saved prediction into a direct branch-miss predicate
motivation:
The sixteen-entry agreement predictor already leaves little cycle headroom:
earlier tracing estimated 55,124 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs in
4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent worst paths repeatedly cross EX
recovery, IF masking and register-file controls. Larger tables or a return
predictor cannot plausibly clear the 4.6 percent margin from cycle savings
alone. Target preselection in r7s2 and a registered predictor lookup in r8s2
both regressed. Attack the late recovery-enable calculation itself while
retaining the current predictor, acceptance rules and one-bubble miss penalty.

hypothesis.motivation:
The sixteen-entry agreement predictor already leaves little cycle headroom:
earlier tracing estimated 55,124 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs in
4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent worst paths repeatedly cross EX
recovery, IF masking and register-file controls. Larger tables or a return
predictor cannot plausibly clear the 4.6 percent margin from cycle savings
alone. Target preselection in r7s2 and a registered predictor lookup in r8s2
both regressed. Attack the late recovery-enable calculation itself while
retaining the current predictor, acceptance rules and one-bubble miss penalty.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compile each accepted branch's prediction into a decode-time recovery
descriptor, so EX directly evaluates whether the prediction was wrong instead
of resolving direction, qualifying actual_taken, then XORing predicted_taken.
Keep the sixteen local agreement counters, sign bias, immediate training,
raw-instruction prediction, direct-JAL prediction and current pipeline depth.
This is one predictor-recovery timing change, not an accuracy experiment.

Add to id_ex_t a three-bit miss_branch_op and a branch_recovery_enable bit.
In ID, miss_branch_op = decoded branch_op XOR {2'b00, in.predicted_taken}.
The low funct3 bit complements each legal relation: BEQ/BNE, BLT/BGE and
BLTU/BGEU. Compute branch_recovery_enable from legal conditional-branch
decode and word alignment of the direct target. Determine alignment with
the exact two-bit sum of in.pc[1:0] and imm[1:0], without a new full-width
adder. Capture both fields with the same instruction and exact prediction
used to advance fetch; hold on stalls and clear on reset or flush.

EX evaluates one set of forwarded equality, signed-less-than and
unsigned-less-than predicates. Use the captured miss_branch_op to select
the appropriate predicate or its complement directly as branch_miss.
Share the underlying comparisons with the original actual branch-condition
selector used for architectural pc_next, target traps and training. Keep
ctrl.branch_op architectural. Do not put actual_taken XOR predicted_taken
back after the miss comparator. Only the recovery-enable cone changes.

Recovery enable becomes valid && ex_advance &&
((branch_recovery_enable && branch_miss) ||
(legal_JALR && aligned_JALR_target)). Existing decoded is_jalr and
!is_illegal establish legal_JALR. Use the exact low two bits of the existing
forwarded rs1+imm sum to test alignment after clearing bit zero; keep
the full sum for its target. Do not wait for high target bits to qualify
recovery. Valid aligned direct JAL always has a correct taken prediction
in this predictor and needs no recovery; illegal instructions and
misaligned direct targets were predicted sequentially and need none.
A legal aligned JALR is always unpredicted and needs recovery. Preserve
authoritative EX misalignment detection and trap/write suppression.
These simplifications are specific to the current instruction-derived
predictor; tests must establish their assumptions rather than weaken
recovery for a hypothetical target-cache predictor.

Keep redirect_target = resolved_pc_next and retain the champion's target
additions and actual-outcome selection exactly. Do not introduce the
opposite-prediction displacement adder from r7s2. This proposal specifically
moves prediction polarity and direct-target legality/alignment qualification
ahead of EX's late compare-to-redirect path. It does not add a target cache,
prepare a second recovery address or claim any prediction-accuracy gain.

Keep reset and recovery priority in IF, the immediate younger-slot squash,
all current hazard controls, registered forwarding and the independent
effective-address register. Qualify recovery and training on exactly the
existing EX advance event: never during dmem hold, execute_wait, reset or
bubbles. Recovery on release must still override imem backpressure. Train
once per legal non-faulting advancing conditional branch using its actual
outcome, never branch_miss. Correct predictions must keep their younger
instruction. No extra recovery cycle, delayed kill, new instruction stage,
lookup pipeline, table resizing or arithmetic-unit changes are included.

Preserve nret=1, the complete external port contract, all RV32IM and
ALTOPS behavior, default-illegal decoding, traps, full-width PC arithmetic,
link writes, x0, both bus handshakes and contiguous retirement order.
Keep the existing ten-clock ready-bus progress bound and exact redirected-
divide retirement-cycle assertions. Do not change formal depth, wrappers,
timing constraints, benchmarks or any evaluation contract.

The intended benefit is Fmax at unchanged CoreMark cycles. A temporary
prototype of this exact separate-descriptor, original-target topology
passed all existing IF/pipeline tests after updating only the forwarding
monitor's packed-field offsets for the four added bits. Gowin placement
options measured 54.002, 54.827 and 54.827 MHz, giving median 54.827 MHz,
with 3,144 logic cells, 702 registers, eight LUT RAMs, six BSRAMs and six
DSPs. Selftest RVFI cosimulation passed with ready and stalled buses.
Canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/MMIO-marker validation passed
at exactly 4,203,513 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. All 53 unchanged
normal riscv-formal checks passed on this final prototype. The measured
product is fitness 130.4314, approximately 2.51 percent below 133.79.
Expected impact is therefore -3 percent with low confidence in improvement.
The proposal does NOT clear the required acceptance margin. The remaining
multiplier/divider and register-file paths limit whole-core timing despite
the simpler recovery-enable logic. At 4,203,513 cycles,
acceptance requires median Fmax above approximately 58.826 MHz and measured
fitness strictly above 139.94434. Require unchanged formal, stalled cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and all scored Gowin
placement options before judging success. These are proposal-stage
measurements, not tournament acceptance. The deliverable is this YAML;
temporary RTL and test probes are restored after validation.

title: Bypass PC and immediate selection on multiplier operand paths
motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz. Recent divider-completion
changes exposed a competing register-file/forwarding-to-multiplier path:
r9s1 removed divider paths from the worst 25 but regressed to 52.540 MHz.
Every multiplier currently receives alu_a and alu_b after the AUIPC-PC
and immediate selectors, although all four legal multiply instructions
always multiply the forwarded register operands. Those selectors are
unnecessary on the multiplier's timed data inputs. The r8s0 experiment
shared products through one 33-bit multiply and regressed; this proposal
preserves the existing products and specializes only their input routing,
without changing register-file mapping or forwarding arbitration.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz. Recent divider-completion
changes exposed a competing register-file/forwarding-to-multiplier path:
r9s1 removed divider paths from the worst 25 but regressed to 52.540 MHz.
Every multiplier currently receives alu_a and alu_b after the AUIPC-PC
and immediate selectors, although all four legal multiply instructions
always multiply the forwarded register operands. Those selectors are
unnecessary on the multiplier's timed data inputs. The r8s0 experiment

preserves the existing products and specializes only their input routing,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the real multiplier expressions a dedicated pair of operands wired
directly to EX's already-forwarded rs1 and rs2. Keep the existing alu_a
and alu_b paths for integer ALU operations and divider operand capture.
This removes the subsequent PC/immediate selection from each multiplier
input without moving a register, adding a cycle, changing forwarding
priority or sharing the three signedness-specific products.

In alu.sv add two internal-module input ports for the raw forwarded
multiply operands. To preserve existing standalone ALU semantics, provide
a compile-time parameter, default false, selecting whether multiply
expressions use these ports or ordinary a/b. Instantiate this parameter
as true only in ex_stage.sv and connect the new ports directly to rs1
and rs2, before alu_a/alu_b selection. As an elaboration constant, the
parameter must not create a runtime mux. Do not connect the new ports
to alu_a/alu_b or gate them with the multiply opcode.

Route all three existing mul_ss, mul_uu and mul_su expressions through
the selected multiply operand pair. Preserve their current widths,
signed/unsigned extensions, low/high-half selection and combinational
latency. Preserve distinct products and normal Gowin DSP inference;
do not introduce shared 33-bit multiplication, partial-product LUT
arithmetic, DSP primitives or additional multiplier pipeline stages.
Keep multiply result selection in the existing ALU/EX result path.

Use the same selected multiply operand pair in the four multiply ALTOPS
formulas, retaining their exact addition/subtraction and XOR constants.
In default standalone mode this remains exactly a/b. In the core's
specialized mode these values equal a/b for every accepted legal MUL,
MULH, MULHU and MULHSU because their decoded is_auipc and alu_src bits
are both zero. Leave DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU, their ALTOPS formulas, magnitude
capture, recurrence, correction and nine-clock handshake untouched.

Preserve the original forwarding muxes and ID/EX-captured binary
selectors. The new multiply inputs must observe EX/MEM before MEM/WB,
x0 behavior, retained WB data during memory holds and the same captured
instruction as the rest of EX. Do not use unforwarded register-file
outputs. Raw rs1/rs2 remain the source of RVFI operand metadata, stores,
branch comparison and JALR. Preserve independent effective-address
transport, all bubble and hold rules, predictor behavior, decoder
legality, nret=1 ports, bus handshakes and contiguous retirement order.

The expected benefit is removing a serial selection from both sides of
the DSP path and reducing DSP load on the general ALU-input mux outputs,
with unchanged CoreMark cycles. The multiplier-only scope matters:
proposal-stage broader one-hot operand selection measured 52.232 MHz,
and combining write-through bypass with one-hot forwarding measured
54.738 MHz, both below the champion despite passing pipeline checks.
Those prototypes are excluded. This exact dedicated-multiplier-input
proposal has not been implemented or timed; those measurements do not
establish its correctness or performance. Divider completion and
recovery remain competing limits, and increased raw-operand fanout or
changed DSP placement may erase the benefit. Confidence is therefore low.

Validate default and specialized ALU modes with real arithmetic and
ALTOPS. In specialized-mode tests deliberately make ordinary a/b differ
from the multiply inputs: all multiply results must use the latter,
while non-multiply operations must still use a/b. Cover signed extrema,
high unsigned values, zero, minus one, both operand orders and all four
multiply variants. Add pipeline cases for each forwarding source on
either multiply operand, simultaneous source matches, younger-writer
priority, a load feeding multiplication, divide-result dependencies,
memory holds and wrong-path multiplies. Check exact RVFI source values
and single retirement without relaxing existing assertions.

Require unchanged formal/liveness gates, real arithmetic tests, stalled
retirement cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker
checks. Inspect the Gowin netlist to confirm DSP inputs actually bypass
PC/immediate selection and inspect the full competing timing paths.
Acceptance requires measured fitness strictly above 139.94434,
approximately 58.826 MHz at the champion's 4,203,513 bracketed cycles.

title: Pipeline M-extension completion across the existing EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent structural attempts show competing arithmetic
limits: r8s1 result banking left divider completion critical, while
r9s1 removed divider-origin worst paths but exposed the register-file
through multiplier path and regressed 6.58 percent. Rearranging only
result muxes or only divider capture has not cleared the acceptance
margin. MEM currently transports an already finished M-extension result;
use that existing pipeline interval to finish arithmetic instead.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent structural attempts show competing arithmetic
limits: r8s1 result banking left divider completion critical, while
r9s1 removed divider-origin worst paths but exposed the register-file
through multiplier path and regressed 6.58 percent. Rearranging only
result muxes or only divider capture has not cleared the acceptance
margin. MEM currently transports an already finished M-extension result;
use that existing pipeline interval to finish arithmetic instead.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming M-extension execution across the existing EX/MEM boundary is
the single structural change. Make MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU and completed
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU late-result producers, like loads: EX/MEM transports
registered partial arithmetic and MEM completes it into MEM/WB. Keep
ordinary integer execution, branch resolution, the predictor, the
independent effective-address register, memory transactions, pipeline
depth and single retirement port. This is a true arithmetic register
boundary, not parallel banks containing already completed results.

For multiplication, replace the three full-width combinational products
with four parallel 16-bit-limb partial products. Treat each low limb as
positive signed 17-bit {0, operand[15:0]}. Treat each high limb as signed
17-bit {signed_operand && operand[31], operand[31:16]}; signed_operand
is true for both operands on MULH, only rs1 on MULHSU, and neither on
MULHU or MUL. Compute the four signed 34-bit limb products from the
exact forwarded operands and register them at EX/MEM with the selected
operation and metadata. In MEM, sign-extend each product to 64 bits,
shift the two cross products by 16 and the high-high product by 32,
and sum modulo 2^64. Use a balanced carry-save reduction of these four
rows followed by one carry-propagate addition, rather than three serial
full-width additions. Select low or high 32 bits by the registered op
and capture the result in MEM/WB. Preserve one multiply accepted per
cycle for independent instructions. Remove the old full-width multiply
cones from the timed design; do not retain a combinational MUL bypass.
Give every product and shifted row an explicit signedness and width:
widen to 64 bits before shifting, and discard only overflow above bit
63. For carry-save reduction, reduce three rows to XOR-sum and shifted
majority-carry, then reduce those two plus the fourth row the same way
before the final addition. No arithmetic right shifts are involved.

Apply the same boundary to divider completion without increasing its
nine-clock EX occupancy or delaying retirement. Edge 0 captures operand
magnitudes and signs as today. Edges 1 through 7 perform the existing
two radix-4 digits per edge, consuming 28 bits. At edge 8, execute only
the first digit of the last pair and transfer the resulting quotient,
remainder, divisor, registered 3D, quotient/remainder selection and sign
into EX/MEM with the saved instruction metadata. This token represents
exactly 30 consumed dividend bits. During MEM, perform the final radix-4
digit, select quotient or remainder, and restore the sign; edge 9
captures the finished result in MEM/WB, the same retirement boundary as
the champion. Thus neither the EX completion path nor the MEM completion
path contains two serial digits followed by negation and EX result muxing.
Normal divider recurrence still performs two digits per clock.

The divider's completion availability remains state-derived and becomes
true on the same cycle as today. If EX/MEM cannot accept at edge 8, save
the 30-bit-prefix token locally and hold it unchanged until acceptance;
do not repeatedly apply the penultimate digit while waiting. Consume a
request once and clear busy only on token transfer. Capture operands
before forwarding sources drain; use the existing saved source values
and instruction metadata on completion. Preserve reset cancellation,
early-consume rejection, ignored competing requests and inert wait
bubbles. Divider finalization must use only the registered token, never
live EX inputs or divider state belonging to a younger instruction.

Extend the existing load-use interlock into a late-result interlock.
A valid, nonfaulting instruction in ID/EX is late-result when it is a
load or any M-extension operation. A matching nonzero destination
stalls the fetched consumer and inserts one bubble on producer advance;
divider execute_wait and real dmem holds retain their existing higher
priorities. Do not bubble away the blocked producer or its consumer.
On divider completion an immediately dependent consumer waits one
additional cycle, then captures selector 2 and obtains the final value
from MEM/WB. Independent consumers can enter EX immediately. Never
select EX/MEM partial data as a register value. Preserve youngest-writer
priority, x0 exclusions, trap-aware producer eligibility, held MEM/WB
forwarding data and registered selector alignment. Retain the current
conservative raw source-field comparisons; source-use optimization is
outside this proposal.

Add an explicit registered M-result kind and payload to EX/MEM. Hold
the payload coherently with its metadata on actual dmem backpressure,
clear its kind for bubbles/reset, and choose the final M value in MEM
before MEM/WB's ALU-result capture. A late-result instruction is not a
memory request: do not overload mem_read, mem_write or mem_to_reg to
represent it. Keep all memory ports, byte lanes, load extraction,
alignment traps and the separately registered full-width address path
unchanged, retaining Gowin's wrapper BSRAM inference. RVFI uses exact
captured architectural operands and the completed writeback result.

Preserve every RV32M corner case, including signed truncation toward
zero, dividend-signed remainder, unsigned high bits, zero divisors and
INT_MIN/-1. Carry the existing ALTOPS formulas through the same late
result classification, interlock and register boundaries; never use
ALTOPS to hide a different real-hardware dependency schedule. Preserve
nret=1, default-illegal decoding, traps, x0, both bus handshakes,
contiguous RVFI order and the existing ready-bus liveness bound. Do not
change formal depth, evaluation wrappers, constraints or benchmarks.

Validate multiplication reconstruction and the 30-bit divider token with
directed and seeded-random exact integer reference models. Adapt ALU
tests to observe the complete two-stage arithmetic path, retaining all
result assertions and checking the new internal boundary rather than
asserting that an intermediate token is already a final result. Keep
the nine-clock divider transfer and original architectural retirement
bounds. Update implementation-specific checks to expect MEM/WB selector
2 for an immediately dependent M consumer, and a ten-clock rather than
nine-clock retirement gap between dependent divides. Keep the existing
universal ten-clock ready-bus maximum and the exact first-divide
retirement timing following a redirect. Do not relax arithmetic,
architectural state, order, trap or progress assertions. Cover
consecutive independent M operations, immediate and
distance-two dependencies, youngest writers, M-to-branch/address/store
dependencies, blocked token transfer, reset, wrong-path M operations,
faults and simultaneous bus stalls. Run unchanged normal formal,
real-arithmetic unit tests, relevant formal-deep checks and stalled
retirement cosimulation with canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/markers.

Proposal-stage exact integer models passed 100,676 multiply cases
covering all four signedness modes and the two-level carry-save
reconstruction, and 100,676 DIV/REM cases checking the 30-bit-prefix
token and final digit/sign restoration. Inputs included limb boundaries,
signed extremes, zero divisors and 25,000 seeded-random operand pairs.
These are mathematical checks, not RTL simulation or formal proofs.

Read-only execution of the available CoreMark ELF with the unchanged
reference interpreter counted 2,922,015 retired instructions between
the MMIO markers: 93,960 MUL instructions, no other M operations, and
35,640 immediately following instructions whose raw source fields
matched the M destination. Charging one new bubble to each gives
0.848 percent of the champion's cycles before overlap with existing
stalls; changing instruction timing also changes the ready-stream
interaction, so this is a workload estimate, not a measured cycle
delta or strict bound. The divider still needs retiming because its
hardware limits Fmax even when no divide executes inside the bracket.

feedback are the main risks. Measure the actual dependency penalty;

median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle above 139.94434. If
cycles rise by a fraction p, Fmax must exceed approximately
58.826 MHz times (1+p), or about 59.325 MHz with the nominal 35,640
extra cycles. The 12 percent expected gain is an unmeasured
architectural estimate, not a claim of a validated improvement.

title: Hold a registered predictor correction PC until fetch acceptance
motivation:
The champion's sixteen-entry agree predictor already leaves only about
55,124 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs in 4,203,513 CoreMark cycles,
according to prior proposal tracing. Accuracy alone therefore offers
too little headroom for the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Experiments
r6s2 through r9s2 reduced pieces of recovery or lookup logic but retained
competing EX-to-fetch/decode timing paths. In particular, r6s2 registered
the younger-slot kill while still repairing the ordinary PC directly
from combinational EX. Cut both parts of that recovery feedback at a
register boundary while preserving the single lost execute slot.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's sixteen-entry agree predictor already leaves only about
55,124 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs in 4,203,513 CoreMark cycles,
according to prior proposal tracing. Accuracy alone therefore offers
too little headroom for the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Experiments
r6s2 through r9s2 reduced pieces of recovery or lookup logic but retained

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one predictor-recovery architecture: register the resolved
correction address and misprediction event, then bypass that registered
address onto fetch in the following cycle. Preserve the existing sixteen
local agreement counters, lookup, training policy and direct-JAL prediction.
This is a timing hypothesis, with no claimed prediction-accuracy gain.

IF holds a speculative pc_q and a recovery_pc_q plus recovery_pending_q.
The effective fetch PC is recovery_pending_q ? recovery_pc_q : pc_q.
Use that same full-width effective PC for imem_addr, the outgoing
instruction PC, predictor index, direct-target addition and PC+4.
Set recovery_pending_q on an accepted EX redirect; clear it when fetch
advances without a new redirect, and otherwise hold it. Equivalently,
pending_next = redirect || (recovery_pending_q && stall_if), with reset
priority. Capture redirect_target into recovery_pc_q only on redirect,
and hold it otherwise. EX already qualifies redirect by advancement.
The dedicated correction-address register must not be a muxed post-ALU
result and must not rely on RVFI-only metadata remaining synthesized.

Remove combinational EX redirect from pc_q's data/enable selection.
Its update is reset -> zero; otherwise if !stall_if -> predicted next PC
computed from effective fetch PC; otherwise hold. Keep the correction
bypass selected throughout an instruction-memory stall, rather than
copying correction into pc_q through an extra hold-case data mux. When
the corrected fetch is accepted, pc_q captures that instruction's
predicted successor and pending clears at the same edge. A newly captured
redirect wins over ordinary acceptance. Keep all PC arithmetic at 32 bits,
including wraparound, and never overwrite a stalled correction address.

At the miss edge, the resolving instruction enters EX/MEM, the correction
registers capture its recovery, and the younger wrong-path instruction
may enter ID/EX. In the immediately following cycle the imem port already
addresses recovery_pc_q, while recovery_pending_q annuls that one transient
wrong-path EX slot. At the next edge ID/EX accepts the corrected instruction
and EX/MEM receives an inert bubble. With ready buses this loses exactly
the same one EX slot as the champion, without an extra recovery cycle.
If instruction memory is unavailable, pending remains set while invalid
slots follow the annulled instruction; clear pending at corrected-fetch
acceptance so the corrected instruction is never killed in EX. Correct
predictions continue to admit one instruction per available cycle.

Remove redirect-dependent and imem-dependent instruction-to-NOP masking:
deliver raw imem_data to decode and represent unavailable fetches with
valid=0. IF prediction and valid must not be suppressed by the registered
recovery bypass, since its fetched instruction is already the correct
target. Remove the immediate redirect from hazard flush_if/flush_id;
retain imem invalidation and the qualified load-use bubble. ID/EX retains
its existing reset/flush/hold behavior and captured forwarding selectors.
Suppress load-use generation unless ID/EX is valid and not annulled.

Feed recovery_pending_q to EX as kill_ex. An annulled instruction cannot
redirect, train, launch/consume a divide, assert execute_wait, advertise
next_reg_write, or reach a memory side effect. Preserve reset and older
dmem-hold priority. For a valid annulled slot, clear every EX/MEM control
and valid bit while allowing unused data fields to capture normally;
do not put kill_ex into the arithmetic-result data reset/enable cone.
Retain the existing full inert bubble rule for invalid inputs and divide
waits. Keep the independent effective-address register unchanged.
The kill cannot be lost to an older dmem hold: a recovery is generated
only when the resolving transfer advances, and that non-memory transfer
occupies EX/MEM during the first kill cycle; later pending cycles contain
only bubbles. Explicitly verify that property and that no corrected
instruction enters EX while the pending kill remains asserted.

Predictor training remains exactly once per valid, non-annulled, legal,
non-faulting advancing conditional branch. Use the accepted instruction's
saved predicted_taken in EX; no history snapshot or counter bypass is
added. Keep authoritative resolved_pc_next and misalignment checks for
RVFI, PC+4 link writes, JALR bit-zero clearing, forwarded operands,
decoder legality, all RV32IM/ALTOPS arithmetic, and nret=1 unchanged.
Preserve both bus handshakes, retained MEM/WB forwarding, contiguous
retirement order, and the existing ready-bus redirected-divide liveness
bound. No wrapper, formal depth, benchmark or timing-constraint change.

The intended win is removing combinational recovery from ordinary fetch
PC updates, instruction masking and ID/EX clearing simultaneously. The
cost is a 32-bit registered-address bypass ahead of instruction memory
and prediction; this may instead become critical, and multiplier/divider
paths can still limit Fmax. A temporary prototype of this held-correction
topology measured 50.422, 55.254 and 55.254 MHz across the scored Gowin
placement options, giving median 55.254 MHz, with 3,060 logic cells,
734 registers, eight LUT RAMs, six BSRAMs and six DSPs. Both adapted
IF and pipeline cocotb suites passed without weakening architectural
or ready-bus progress assertions. Selftest RVFI cosimulation passed
with ready and stalled buses. Canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/MMIO
marker validation passed at exactly 4,203,513 bracketed cycles for ten
iterations. All 53 unchanged normal riscv-formal checks passed on this
exact held-correction prototype. These are proposal-stage measurements,
not acceptance.

This measured product is approximately 131.45 fitness, 1.75 percent
below the 133.79 champion. Expected impact is consequently -2 percent,
with low confidence in an improvement; the tested candidate does NOT
clear the acceptance margin. The remaining worst paths pass through
the register file/multiplier and divider completion. At unchanged cycles,
acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 58.826 MHz
and measured fitness strictly above 139.94434. Require unchanged formal,
stalled RVFI cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks;
judge the measured fitness product rather than logical recovery depth.
Temporary RTL and test edits are restored; the YAML is the deliverable.
