title: Predecode one-hot execution-result producers at the ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz. Both the divider-completion
and register-file-to-multiplier paths repeatedly approach the timing
limit. Removing only divider arithmetic depth has exposed multiplication
and recovery as competing limits; the r10s0 multiplier-input change
also regressed. Both arithmetic results currently traverse result
selection: the ALU opcode mux, followed by EX link/divider overrides
and bubble clearing. Flattening that shared selection can address both
arithmetic paths without changing their schedules or adding result banks.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz. Both the divider-completion
and register-file-to-multiplier paths repeatedly approach the timing
limit. Removing only divider arithmetic depth has exposed multiplication
and recovery as competing limits; the r10s0 multiplier-input change
also regressed. Both arithmetic results currently traverse result
selection: the ALU opcode mux, followed by EX link/divider overrides

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the cascaded ALU/EX result selectors with one parallel
selection of distinct result producers, controlled by one-hot enables
registered alongside the instruction in ID/EX. This is one local
execution-result mux optimization. Preserve the pipeline stages,
multiplier implementation, divider recurrence, nine-clock divide
latency, operand forwarding and branch policy.

Define 17 result producers: the eleven existing integer ALU results
ADD through LUI, the four existing multiply results, one completed
divider result, and one PC+4 link result. Allocate exactly one enable
to the shared divider producer, rather than four enables for DIV,
DIVU, REM and REMU. Their existing binary alu_op still controls
divider operand normalization and operation capture. Keep alu_op and
all original decoded controls intact; producer selection is additional
local metadata, not a replacement ISA decoder or legality decision.

Compute producer enables in ID from the fully validated decoder
outputs. A legal jump selects the link producer; a legal divide or
remainder selects the single divider producer; another supported ALU
operation selects its corresponding producer. Clear all enables for
an invalid fetch or illegal instruction. Register the 17-bit vector
on the same edge as ID/EX. Reset or explicit flush clears it; an ID/EX
hold preserves it even if the current fetch is invalid; otherwise
capture the decoded vector. A dedicated ID-to-EX sideband register
and wire can preserve existing packed-bundle layouts and their
monitoring tests. Do not independently advance this metadata.

Inside the ALU, retain the original arithmetic expressions and
real/ALTOPS formulas. Expose their distinct candidate values to an
explicitly parallel masked-OR result selection. The divider candidate
is the existing div_result, including its final-round bypass and
held-completion value. The link candidate is EX's full-width PC+4.
Use each registered producer enable directly; do not reconstruct
enables from the live opcode, use a priority case, or OR together
four registered divide-operation enables after ID/EX. Express the
masked-data reduction as a balanced tree to avoid an accidental
serial procedural reduction. No speculative reverse subtractors,
extra divider multiples, or new arithmetic pipeline banks are needed.

Preserve standalone ALU behavior with an elaboration-time parameter
defaulting to the original opcode-selected out interface; enable the
new producer selection only in the core instance. Add internal-module
inputs for the producer vector and link value. Keep the public divider
handshake and div_result output for standalone tests. The parameter
must elaborate away, with no runtime mode mux. In specialized mode,
the same real and ALTOPS candidate values feed the producer tree.

Capture the unified selected value in a single 32-bit EX/MEM result
register, reset to zero and held only by actual dmem backpressure.
On other edges it may capture an unused value during an invalid slot
or execute_wait. Keep the original EX/MEM metadata and controls under
their existing stall/div_consume/execute_wait/normal priorities, and
continue clearing all controls for bubbles. Override out.alu_result
with this shared result register and remove the old pre-register
jump/divide/zero-result overrides. Do not introduce a post-register
selection among result banks. The resulting single register remains
the original EX/MEM forwarding source and advances on the same useful
instruction edges.

During division, ID/EX and its divider-producer bit hold throughout
execute_wait while older work drains. Nonfinal captured result data
is unobservable because EX/MEM controls are inert. At consumption,
the existing divider result and saved div_metadata_q become visible
together. A dmem stall must retain both metadata and result; after a
blocked completion, the stable DIV_DONE result is captured on release.
Keep request, busy, valid, consume and reset behavior unchanged.
Ordinary, multiply and link results retain their existing forwarding
and retirement cycles, including trap suppression of misaligned jumps.

Preserve the separate effective-address register, all memory request
controls, retained MEM/WB forwarding after retirement, x0, decoder
defaults, trap rules, predictor updates, nret=1 ports and contiguous
RVFI order. Only invalid arithmetic payloads may differ; invalid
controls must remain inert and no invalid slot may train, write,
access memory or retire. Do not remove any validity qualification
from producer eligibility or any existing architectural assertion.

Proposal research tested a related 20-bit opcode-one-hot prototype
with separate DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU enables and a procedural OR reduction.
It passed the existing ALU and pipeline runners and measured Gowin
Fmax values 53.401, 54.285 and 54.285 MHz, with 3034 logic cells and
720 registers. That median is below the 56.239 MHz champion and is
not a successful result. A binary unified-selector prototype also
regressed to 53.591 MHz. Neither prototype is the final proposal.
The final refinement uses distinct producer enables, one divide bit,
explicit balanced reduction and invalid-slot enable suppression; it
has not been implemented or timed. Temporary RTL is restored.

The expected gain is speculative: early producer control and removal
of serial output selectors may shorten both arithmetic paths, while
reduced selection logic may help placement. High fanout, decode cost
and unchanged recovery paths may erase the benefit. Confidence is low,
and the measured near-neighbor regressions are material counterevidence.
Acceptance requires actual fitness above 139.94434, approximately
58.826 MHz at the champion's 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles.

title: Overlap instruction and backend stalls with a two-entry elastic fetch queue
motivation:
The champion takes 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles at 56.239 MHz.
Its fused fetch/decode stage cannot retain an instruction independently
of ID/EX: load-use, data-memory and divider stalls hold the fetch PC,
while an instruction-bus stall injects a bubble even if earlier cycles
had spare fetch bandwidth. Prior structural changes repeatedly moved
the timing limit between divider completion, multiplication and
register-file/recovery feedback. In particular, r10s1 added 35,538
cycles without improving Fmax. An elastic instruction queue instead
targets lost bus overlap and removes recovery masking from decode data,
without adding arithmetic dependency latency.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion takes 4,203,513 bracketed CoreMark cycles at 56.239 MHz.
Its fused fetch/decode stage cannot retain an instruction independently
of ID/EX: load-use, data-memory and divider stalls hold the fetch PC,
while an instruction-bus stall injects a bubble even if earlier cycles
had spare fetch bandwidth. Prior structural changes repeatedly moved
the timing limit between divider completion, multiplication and
register-file/recovery feedback. In particular, r10s1 added 35,538
cycles without improving Fmax. An elastic instruction queue instead
targets lost bus overlap and removes recovery masking from decode data,
without adding arithmetic dependency latency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert a two-entry, fall-through, in-order instruction queue between
fetch and decode. This is a single structural change to the front-end
pipeline and its backpressure topology. Each entry contains PC, the
unmodified instruction and its fetch-time predicted_taken bit. Fetch
uses the existing sixteen-entry agree predictor and direct-JAL target
calculation. Advance the fetch PC only when a ready bus word is actually
accepted, or on an accepted EX recovery. Decode consumes the registered
head when occupied and the live bus word when empty and imemReady is
high. This empty-queue bypass is required to preserve the existing
single-slot recovery penalty and ten-clock ready-bus progress bound
for a mispredicted branch or JALR immediately followed by a divide.

Fetch may enqueue while ID/EX is held by load-use, a data-memory request
or a divide, until the queue fills. Decode may dequeue while imemReady
is low. Support simultaneous push/pop, including a full queue replacing
its consumed head, so steady-state throughput remains one instruction
per clock. A live word consumed through the empty-queue bypass advances
the fetch PC without occupying a queue entry. If decode cannot accept
it, save it in the empty queue and still advance the fetch PC. Use two
compacting entry registers with a registered count or equivalent
occupancy bits: the head is directly available without
a variable-index RAM read. For a simultaneous pop/push at occupancy one,
replace the head with the incoming entry; at occupancy two, move the
tail to the head and capture the new tail. Hold entries not being
written. Select queued versus live payload using registered occupancy
only; never put redirect, imemReady or a NOP mask on this data mux.

Define decode acceptance from head_valid and actual ID/EX capture
permission, excluding reset, redirect, load-use, execute_wait and real
dmem holds. head_valid is queue_nonempty OR imemReady. Fetch acceptance
requires imemReady and free space after any accepted buffered dequeue.
Store an accepted fetch unless the empty-queue bypass consumed it
directly. A resolving EX redirect overrides all events: invalidate all
queued younger instructions, discard the current bus word, bubble
ID/EX, and install the resolved fetch PC even if imemReady is low or the
queue was full. The target can bypass into ID/EX on the next ready
cycle, restoring the champion's recovery schedule. Preserve
EX's existing advance qualification so held branches do not redirect or
train repeatedly. A correctly predicted branch keeps its queued path.
Predictor training still occurs once at branch execution; queued
predictions are immutable snapshots and must never be recomputed from
subsequently trained counters.

Separate front-end bus availability from backend hazards. Remove the
global rule that imemReady=0 flushes decode: starvation means both
queue_empty and !imemReady. On an unavailable slot and backend advance,
inject zero controls into ID/EX; on a backend hold, preserve the existing
instruction. Retain redirect/flush priority and fully inert EX/MEM
bubbles. Read the register file and compare load-use/forwarding sources
from the selected queued-or-live head instruction, not unconditionally
io_imemData and not a recovery-masked NOP. Capture forwarding selectors
as that head enters ID/EX, against the then-current producers. Never cache
register values or selectors at enqueue time. Preserve trap-aware
producer eligibility, youngest-writer priority, x0 exclusions and held
MEM/WB forwarding data.

Keep EX/MEM/WB execution, the independent effective-address register,
nine-clock divider, real and ALTOPS arithmetic, and all dmem transaction
rules unchanged. Preserve the nret=1 interface, exact RVFI operands and
PCs, contiguous retirement order, illegal/default decoder behavior,
misalignment traps, reset cancellation and once-only side effects.
Buffered entries retain their fetch-time prediction; the bypass keeps
the original empty-queue latency and no-stall issue throughput. Do not
change the predictor algorithm or add caches, arithmetic optimizations,
benchmark special cases or evaluation edits.

Add a queue transaction scoreboard and exercise empty/full transitions,
simultaneous push/pop, prolonged independent bus stalls, held divides,
load-use dependencies at the queue head, predictor updates while an
entry waits, and recovery with full/empty queues and imemReady low.
Wrong-path loads, stores, divides and illegal words must never execute
or retire. Update implementation-specific fetch/predictor monitors to
track enqueue and dequeue separately while preserving their exact
architectural and once-only assertions. Run existing formal, arithmetic
tests and stalled retirement cosimulation, including canonical CoreMark
CRCs, UART text, memory bounds and marker timing. Keep the existing
formal depth and ten-clock ready-bus progress bound. Explicitly cover
recovery directly to DIV/REM with an empty queue; do not weaken the
existing maximum-retirement-gap assertions.

Proposal-stage evidence: read-only execution of the available canonical
CoreMark ELF with the unchanged reference interpreter supplied a dynamic
instruction trace. A separate cycle model included the sixteen agree
counters, raw-field load-use comparisons, EX branch recovery, nine-clock
division and the exact xorshift ready sequence, advanced twice per cycle
from 0xDEADBEEF. Its unbuffered case reproduced the logged 4,203,513
marker-bracketed cycles exactly. The two-entry fall-through case took
3,987,564 modeled cycles: 5.14 percent fewer cycles, or 5.42 percent more
iterations/cycle. Modeled empty-instruction starvation fell from 816,370
to 601,102 cycles; 168,321 decode acceptances occurred with imemReady low.
Both cases had 68,869 recoveries. One entry modeled 4,025,416 cycles;
four entries modeled 3,978,076, only 0.24 percent fewer than two entries.
This motivates the small two-entry structure. These are calibrated
scheduling estimates, not RTL simulation, formal proof or FPGA timing;
the trace supplies correct architectural values and cannot detect
implementation errors in forwarding, operands or memory transactions.

The expected benefit is fewer instruction starvation bubbles through
overlap with existing backend stalls, with a possible timing benefit
from removing recovery-dependent payload masking. The main risks are
wasted speculative bandwidth, the head mux, queue control routing and the
unchanged arithmetic timing floor. Acceptance requires measured median
Gowin Fmax times measured CoreMark iterations/cycle above 139.94434.
At the modeled cycle count, the acceptance threshold requires Fmax above
55.804 MHz, leaving only about 0.8 percent margin below the champion's
clock rate. The 9 percent expected gain assumes about 58.15 MHz from
removing the recovery-to-decode data feedback; that timing gain remains
unmeasured. Retain the smallest head mux and occupancy/control cones,
inspect actual median Gowin timing, and evaluate the complete product.

title: Register prediction recovery and defer the resolving transfer by one cycle
motivation:
The sixteen-entry agree predictor already leaves only about 55,124
conditional misses and 13,735 unpredicted JALRs in 4,203,513 CoreMark
cycles. Accuracy alone cannot clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
Prior recovery optimizations retained competing combinational feedback;
r10s2 added a registered correction-address bypass ahead of instruction
memory and regressed. A distinct recovery architecture can trade one
additional miss cycle for a complete registered EX-to-fetch boundary.

The sixteen-entry agree predictor already leaves only about 55,124
conditional misses and 13,735 unpredicted JALRs in 4,203,513 CoreMark
cycles. Accuracy alone cannot clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the current sixteen-entry agreement predictor, training policy,
direct-JAL prediction and direction-only prediction metadata. Register
each accepted EX misprediction event and its resolved full-width target.
Repair the ordinary fetch PC from those registers on the following edge,
with no correction-address mux on io_imemAddr. Only the registered event
drives fetch recovery and younger-slot flushing. The immediate EX miss
must not feed PC enables, fetch instruction masking, decode flushing,
load-use interlocks or execute_wait.

At the same time defer the mispredicting transfer's passage to MEM by
exactly one cycle. At the miss-detection edge capture its normal EX/MEM
data and metadata, but expose an inert bubble to MEM and forwarding in
the ensuing recovery-pending cycle. Retain its legal resolved controls
separately. During that cycle kill the transient wrong-path ID/EX slot,
hold the captured EX/MEM data, and at the PC-repair edge activate the
saved resolving transfer's controls/valid for MEM. Retain the transfer's
exact forwarded operands and metadata captured at original resolution;
never recompute them from forwarding sources after they drain.

Isolate the jump link needed by deferred recovery from ordinary arithmetic
capture. Use an independent 32-bit link_q register for in.pc+4, reset to
zero and enabled by !stall_ex_mem && !recovery_pending. Normal ALU/divider
results use a separate 32-bit result_q at the same EX/MEM boundary: reset
to zero, otherwise capture div_consume ? div_result : alu_result whenever
!stall_ex_mem, including unused sums during bubbles and recovery. Remove
the old shared reg_q.alu_result storage and its pre-register link mux.
Drive out.alu_result = reg_q.ctrl.is_jump ? link_q : result_q. This single
registered-control mux also supplies EX/MEM forwarding. The link register
retains the resolving JALR's return address through the deferred cycle,
while recovery no longer adds a hold enable to ordinary arithmetic data.
Keep all normal result latencies and the divider consume edge unchanged.

During registered recovery suppress the wrong-path EX instruction's
redirect detection, predictor training, next_reg_write, divider request
and consume, execute_wait, and load-use producer eligibility. Clear the
younger ID/EX slot on the registered recovery edge even when imem is
stalled. Gate every exposed EX/MEM memory/register control as well as
valid during the deferred cycle, since downstream consumers are not all
valid-qualified. Preserve older dmem-hold priority. A recovery can be
captured only on normal non-stalled EX advance, and its deferred producer
is a branch or jump, so the recovery-pending cycle has no outstanding
EX/MEM memory operation and can always complete. Reset cancels pending
recovery and clears the saved controls and all side-effect eligibility.

Train exactly once at original accepted resolution of a legal,
non-faulting conditional branch, including a misprediction; do not train
again when its saved payload becomes active. The registered PC repair
overrides imem backpressure. Correct predictions retain present throughput
and latency. A miss now loses two younger execution slots, but delaying
the resolving transfer's retirement by one cycle preserves the existing
maximum ten-clock ready-bus gap to a nine-clock DIV/REM successor.
Prove that property with the unchanged liveness formal configuration and
retain the pipeline tests' maximum-gap assertions. Exact absolute-cycle
expectations may reflect the new miss latency, never a relaxed gap bound.

Keep authoritative resolved_pc_next, misalignment traps and sequential
trap recovery, decoder legality, full-width address wraparound, x0,
nret=1, both memory handshakes, retained MEM/WB forwarding, divider
arithmetic/latency and all ALTOPS behavior. The effective-address register
can capture irrelevant sums during inert bubbles; it must retain its
existing dmem hold and normal valid-memory behavior. Change no evaluation
contracts, formal depth, timing constraints or benchmark sources.

The intended gain is Fmax from removing combinational branch recovery
from fetch/decode while keeping io_imemAddr directly driven by the PC
register. The approximate one-cycle cost per remaining redirect is 1.6
percent before bus-stall overlap. A temporary prototype of this exact
separate-link recovery topology passed all 28 adapted pipeline cocotb
tests, retaining the maximum ten-clock ready-bus retirement-gap checks.
Selftest RVFI cosimulation passed with ready and stalled buses, and the
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation passed at 4,271,994
bracketed cycles for ten iterations, 1.63 percent more than the champion.
All 53 unchanged normal riscv-formal checks passed.

Scored Gowin placement options measured 51.934, 54.617 and 54.617 MHz,
giving median 54.617 MHz; option-zero usage was 3,136 logic cells, 775
registers, eight LUT RAMs, six BSRAMs and six DSPs. That product is about
127.85 fitness, 4.44 percent below the 133.79 champion. Expected impact
is therefore -4 percent, with low confidence in improvement. These are
proposal-stage measurements, not an accepted tournament result. This
candidate does NOT clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. At the measured
cycle count acceptance requires median Fmax strictly above about 59.79 MHz
and fitness above 139.94434. The remaining register-file/multiplier and
divider-completion paths still limit timing despite the recovery boundary.
Implement and rerun all unchanged gates and the scored vendor median;
do not infer a speedup from shorter logical recovery depth. Temporary
RTL/test probes are restored, leaving this YAML as the sole deliverable.

title: Separate register-file reset state from RAM data and flatten read selection
motivation:
Register-file-to-multiplier and recovery-to-register-file paths repeatedly
compete with divider completion for the clock limit. The current register
array describes clearing all data on reset, although architectural reset
only requires subsequent reads to return zero until a register is written.
Earlier distributed-RAM and banked-read attempts did not clear acceptance.
Target the register file's reset implementation and read selection while
retaining inference freedom, architectural reset semantics and all latency.

hypothesis.motivation:
Register-file-to-multiplier and recovery-to-register-file paths repeatedly
compete with divider completion for the clock limit. The current register
array describes clearing all data on reset, although architectural reset

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the register file's resettable data array with an ordinary
synchronous-write array plus one resettable initialized bit per register.
Flatten initialized-state masking, x0 and same-cycle writeback bypass
into two mutually exclusive read masks. This is one local register-file
implementation optimization, with no pipeline or instruction changes.

Keep regs[0:31] as 32-bit words with no RAM-style attribute and no data
reset loop. On a rising edge write regs[w_addr] only when !reset,
w_en and w_addr!=0. In a separate clocked block clear the entire
initialized vector on reset; otherwise set initialized[w_addr] when
w_en and w_addr!=0. Reset has priority over initialization. The x0
initialized bit remains zero. Old RAM contents after a reset are
unobservable until overwritten; they must never substitute for the
required architectural zero. Do not rely on FPGA power-up RAM values.

For each read address r compute:
  select_wb = (r!=0) && w_en && (w_addr==r);
  select_ram = (r!=0) && initialized[r] && !select_wb;
  read_data = ({32{select_wb}} & w_data)
            | ({32{select_ram}} & regs[r]).
Express the two masked terms in parallel, not as a nested RAM-data,
initialized, writeback and x0 mux chain. The masks are mutually
exclusive. Both are zero for x0 and for an unwritten register without
bypass. A matching same-cycle write must bypass even when initialized
is zero. Preserve the original combinational bypass behavior during
reset as well: reset suppresses storage writes at the edge, but the
existing read interface gives matching w_en/w_addr priority. After
reset with w_en deasserted, every architectural register reads zero.

Connect only u_rf's read addresses directly to raw io_imemData[19:15]
and [24:20], removing the unused ID-to-regfile address wires and
explicitly disconnecting ID's address outputs. Keep IF's NOP mask,
instruction validity, decoder inputs and the entire flush/hold protocol
intact. Raw addressing keeps late recovery out of this memory access
path. Valid accepted instructions have identical raw and masked source
fields; invalid reads cannot commit, and stalled ID/EX operands hold.

Preserve existing binary registered forwarding selectors, trap-aware
producer eligibility, youngest-writer priority, retained MEM/WB data,
raw load-use comparisons including unused instruction fields, effective
addresses, nine-clock division, actual arithmetic and ALTOPS, branch
prediction, default-illegal decoding, nret=1 and contiguous RVFI order.
No regfile stage, additional cycle, changed reset-visible value,
distributed-RAM requirement or explicit vendor primitive is proposed.

A temporary implementation of this exact parallel-read variant passed
the existing register-file and pipeline cocotb runners. Gowin's three
placement options produced a median of 56.719 MHz versus the champion's
56.239 MHz, about 0.85% higher. The rounded fitness expectation is 1%,
with low confidence in acceptance. This is NOT a demonstrated tournament
win: it is below the required 4.6% margin even if CoreMark cycles remain
unchanged. Full formal and CoreMark evaluation were not run on this
prototype, so unchanged cycles and final correctness remain to be
verified. At 4203513 bracketed cycles the projected fitness is about
134.93, whereas acceptance requires strictly more than 139.94434.

The unforced-memory variant with nested read selection reached only
55.829 MHz; forcing distributed RAM reached 51.503 MHz. These are
counterevidence against treating removal of the data reset alone as
sufficient. Preserve the specified parallel read equations and normal
memory inference. Other proposal-stage probes of divider arithmetic,
operand clearing and forwarding encoding regressed and are excluded.
Temporary RTL is restored after research; implement only this proposal.

Strengthen reset tests with nonzero writes to every register followed
by reset, repeated resets, and reset coincident with a write. Check
unwritten reads, first writes, overwritten values, independent read
ports, x0 and same-cycle bypass before and after the clock edge.
The invariant is initialized[r]==0 implies a zero non-bypassed read;
initialized[r]==1 implies the RAM holds the latest post-reset write.
Preserve existing assertions and add an independent architectural
register model. Exercise arbitrary raw read fields during invalid
fetches, recovery and prolonged overlapping memory/divider holds.

cycles with median Gowin Fmax. Inspect inferred storage and all
competing paths. Added validity fanout, memory-output selection and

title: Repartition execution around fully resolved operand registers
motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural r10s1 successfully split M arithmetic
across EX/MEM, but its 55.621 MHz result was limited by a path from
the register file through execute, recovery and back into register-file
control. Its extra M dependency bubbles cost only 35,538 cycles.
Earlier divider-only and result-bank changes similarly exposed the
register-file/multiplier path. The missing structural change is a
complete execution partition: registered, already-forwarded operands
launching arithmetic, with late M completion behind EX/MEM. This
targets the competing paths together through one pipeline repartition.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.79 at 56.239 MHz and 4,203,513 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural r10s1 successfully split M arithmetic
across EX/MEM, but its 55.621 MHz result was limited by a path from
the register file through execute, recovery and back into register-file
control. Its extra M dependency bubbles cost only 35,538 cycles.
Earlier divider-only and result-bank changes similarly exposed the
register-file/multiplier path. The missing structural change is a
complete execution partition: registered, already-forwarded operands
launching arithmetic, with late M completion behind EX/MEM. This
targets the competing paths together through one pipeline repartition.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the existing decode/execute/memory pipeline without adding
an instruction stage. Move operand forwarding and ALU input selection
to the input side of ID/EX, so execute consumes fully resolved operand
registers directly. Ordinary EX results feed the next instruction's
operand registers through an EX-to-decode bypass. Loads and M operations
finish in MEM and feed a MEM-to-decode bypass. EX/MEM is a real partial-
arithmetic boundary for M operations. This is one structural execution
and bypass-topology change, not a predictor, cache or ISA extension.

Name the existing stages D, X, M and W. For each raw D source register,
choose the youngest eligible producer: current X's finished ordinary
ALU/link value, otherwise current M's finished architectural result,
otherwise the register file with its current W write-first bypass.
Exclude x0 and invalid or fault-suppressed producers. A matching X load
or M-extension producer is not ready: hold D and inject one X bubble
when that producer advances. Never fall through to an older writer
when the youngest matching writer is unfinished. The following cycle
obtains the completed value directly from M, including aligned and
sign-extended load data. A real dmem hold and an outstanding divide
retain their existing priority over this interlock.

Capture exact resolved rs1/rs2 values and preselected ALU operands
(PC versus rs1, immediate versus rs2) at ID/EX. Branch comparisons,
effective-address generation, multiplication and divider capture then
use registered values, without an EX forwarding mux. Preserve source
addresses and values for RVFI. Held X operands are immutable and do
not depend on draining M/W forwarding sources. Remove the old registered
forwarding selectors and their EX data muxes rather than retaining a
second bypass network. Consecutive ordinary dependent ALU instructions
must still issue every ready cycle: the recurrence is operand flop,
ALU, decode bypass mux, operand flop. Immediate load consumers retain
the existing one-bubble penalty; immediate M consumers pay one bubble.
Inspect Gowin's mapped launch points to confirm that the full operand
bypass is followed by data flops: absorbing only read addresses into
register RAM must not erase the intended post-forwarding boundary.

Keep the raw instruction, register-file read addresses, immediate and
producer comparisons independent of redirect and instruction readiness.
Remove IF's instruction-to-NOP mux; squash at registered D-to-X valid
and control capture. On an advancing invalid slot or recovery, clear
all side-effect and late-result controls, not just valid. Holds preserve
the valid instruction and its resolved operands. Operand data on bubble
slots may be captured harmlessly; avoid reset/flush selection muxes on
arithmetic data where metadata already makes those values unobservable.
Reset still initializes all architectural state. This localization is
necessary to prevent the old EX-recovery-to-register-address feedback
from surviving the new operand boundary. Keep immediate EX recovery,
the sixteen-entry agree predictor, and the existing one-slot miss
penalty; do not add a recovery register or fetch queue.

Make the M boundary concrete as follows. For MUL variants, form four
parallel 16-bit-limb products in X and register them at EX/MEM. Low
limbs are positive signed 17-bit values; high limbs are signed 17-bit
values with an extension bit selected by the operation's signedness.
In M, widen products to 64 bits before positioning them at shifts
0, 16, 16 and 32, reduce with two carry-save levels and one final carry-
propagate addition, and select the low or high word. Signedness is
both operands for MULH, rs1 only for MULHSU, neither for MULHU/MUL.
Remove the old full-width combinational products. Independent multiplies
retain one-per-cycle throughput. The finished M result feeds both the
registered W result and D's operand bypass; partial products never do.

For division, retain magnitude capture at edge 0 and two radix-4 digits
at edges 1 through 7. At edge 8, execute only the penultimate digit and
transfer the 30-consumed-bit quotient/remainder prefix, divisor, 3D,
operation and sign into EX/MEM. M performs the last radix-4 digit and
sign correction, capturing the final value in W at edge 9, as in the
champion's retirement schedule. This removes the two-digit-plus-sign
chain from completion without lengthening the nine-clock X occupancy.
If token transfer is blocked, save the prefix once and retain it until
accepted; never apply the penultimate digit repeatedly. Use only the
registered token to finalize M, independently of younger divider state.
Preserve captured source metadata, reset cancellation, and once-only
request/consume events. ALTOPS uses the exact existing formulas through
the same boundaries, interlocks and handshake schedule as real arithmetic.

Keep a dedicated effective-address register at EX/MEM, driven by full
registered rs1 plus immediate and held only by actual dmem backpressure.
Do not place M completion or any result mux on the dmem-address channel;
preserve Gowin BSRAM inference and byte-address low bits. M result kind
and payload must hold with their instruction. Preserve memory masks,
load extraction, misalignment suppression, held W data, exact RVFI,
channel-0-only retirement, contiguous order, both ready handshakes,
x0, illegal-default decoding, and all RV32M corner cases. No external
interface, nret, benchmark, formal-depth or progress-bound changes.

The two register cuts are complementary: fully resolved operand flops
remove RAM output and forwarding selection from arithmetic launch,
while partial M registers remove deep completion from its destination.
Earlier r10s1 supplied only the latter cut and left recovery-dependent
register reads intact. This proposal must implement the complete
partition, rather than merely attach another operand mux to that design.
Primary timing risks are the new EX/MEM-to-D bypass endpoints, M's
partial-product reduction, and the unchanged two-digit divider rounds.

Verify back-to-back ordinary dependencies have no new bubbles, load
dependencies retain one bubble, and M dependencies add exactly one.
Cover both source ports, competing writers, x0, load/M-to-branch and
address/store dependencies, traps suppressing a younger writer, held
instructions while W drains, simultaneous bus stalls, divide completion
holds, and recovery directly to DIV/REM. Keep the existing universal
ten-clock ready-bus retirement-gap assertion and formal liveness checks.
Retain all arithmetic expected values; adapt internal pipeline monitors
only to the new operand and partial-result boundaries. Run unchanged
formal, real arithmetic tests, and stalled CoreMark retirement cosim
with canonical CRCs, UART validation, bounds and marker timing.

No new timing or RTL validation is claimed at proposal time. r10s1's
measured 4,239,051 cycles is a useful planning reference for the same
M dependency schedule, not a guarantee for this implementation. At
that cycle count, acceptance above 139.94434 requires median Gowin
Fmax greater than about 59.324 MHz; a 15 percent fitness gain requires
about 65.22 MHz. Measure the full product and inspect actual bypass,
arithmetic and recovery paths rather than relying on logic depth.

title: Confine immediate prediction squash to ID/EX controls
motivation:
Predictor recovery currently masks every fetched instruction bit to NOP
and clears every ID/EX data field. This puts the forwarded EX branch
decision upstream of register-file read addresses, decode data, and many
register clear controls. Prior hyp-20261003-001-r4s0 showed that removing
instruction masking can improve timing, but still cleared the entire
ID/EX bundle. The separate EX kill in r6s2 moved annulment downstream;
r10s2 and r11s2 added recovery state and failed to improve the champion.
Test a distinct predictor recovery boundary: preserve immediate PC repair
and squash in ID/EX, restricting squash to side-effect controls and
prediction validity while keeping instruction and operand data independent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one change to prediction recovery: separate ID/EX control
annulment from ID/EX data capture. Keep the existing sixteen local two-bit
agreement counters, direct JAL prediction, target additions, prediction
metadata, and direction-XOR EX recovery. Add no target cache, prediction
table, kill register, pipeline stage, or recovery cycle.

IF always emits raw imem_data as out.instr. Preserve out.valid =
!(flush || redirect) and the existing predicted_taken qualification.
Preserve reset then accepted EX redirect then ordinary accepted prediction
as PC priorities. The EX miss signal repairs PC at the same edge and
invalidates the younger slot, but no longer selects a NOP on instruction
bits driving decode and register-file addresses. Predictor lookup and the
existing hazard/forwarding comparisons continue using the raw instruction.
Keep all hazard equations and priorities unchanged.

Split the ID/EX register into two update domains without changing its
bundle type. The data domain contains pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, imm, rd,
rs1_addr, rs2_addr, both forwarding selectors, and instr. Reset clears
those fields; otherwise capture their ordinary decoded/raw values exactly
when !stall, independently of flush and in.valid; otherwise hold them.
Neither recovery nor unavailable-fetch validity clears or masks data.
Data may be captured during a recovery bubble, or retained during a
simultaneous load-use stall and explicit flush. It remains inert.

The control domain contains the ENTIRE ctrl_t, valid, and predicted_taken.
Its priority is reset, explicit flush, hold, then capture. Reset or flush
clears all three fields. If stalled without flush, retain them even if
the current fetch is invalid. Otherwise valid captures in.valid;
predicted_taken captures in.valid && in.predicted_taken; ctrl captures
ctrl_decoded when in.valid, and all zero otherwise. Never clear only valid:
downstream memory and some forwarding consumers do not independently
qualify every control. Do not mask live decoded data or register-file
addresses with recovery.

On a miss EX advances the resolving transfer, PC immediately takes the
architectural successor, and ID/EX receives inert controls at that same
edge. The younger raw data may reside in ID/EX but cannot issue a memory
transaction, write a register, launch division, train prediction, redirect,
or retire. EX's existing !in.valid bubble path remains intact. This loses
exactly the existing one execute slot; correct predictions retain their
younger instruction. Do not introduce delayed EX annulment or alter the
independent EX/MEM effective-address register's capture schedule. Harmless
sums from invalid slots have zero memory controls.

Preserve complete ID/EX holds during dmem and divide waits, the load-use
control bubble, MEM/WB forwarding-data retention, and recovery priority
over imem backpressure on memory release. Hold selectors with their data
on a real stall; selectors need not become zero in an invalid bubble.
Prediction lookup and captured prediction must agree at acceptance.
Train exactly once per advancing legal non-faulting branch under the
existing conditions. Preserve decoder legality, traps, architectural
RVFI next PC and link values, contiguous order, nret=1, both memory
handshakes, real/ALTOPS arithmetic, and the unchanged maximum ten-clock
ready-bus retirement gap. Modify no correctness or timing contract.

A temporary prototype of this exact control-only ID/EX squash measured
Gowin placement frequencies 49.548, 53.274, and 53.274 MHz, median 53.274 MHz.
Option-zero usage was 3,129 logic cells, 701 registers, eight LUT RAMs,
six BSRAMs, and six DSPs. The IF suite and pipeline suite passed, including
an added directed case with a squashed raw store and nonzero forwarding
metadata retained in ID/EX while every control is inert. All 53 unchanged
normal formal checks passed. Selftest RVFI cosimulation passed with ready
and stalled buses; canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation
passed at exactly 4,203,513 bracketed cycles for ten iterations.
These are proposal-stage measurements, not tournament acceptance. The
intended mechanism did not remove the remaining register-file to EX/MEM
arithmetic and divider-completion bottlenecks. The measured product is
about 126.74 fitness, approximately 5.3 percent BELOW
133.79. Expected impact is therefore -5 percent with low confidence in
improvement; this candidate is not an observed speedup.

Rerun all unchanged formal and stalled cosim gates, canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation, and the scored Gowin median during
implementation. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 139.94434;
at 4,203,513 bracketed cycles for ten iterations it requires median Fmax
above approximately 58.826 MHz. Do not relax correctness or progress
checks. Restore temporary prototype RTL after research; this YAML is
the sole proposal deliverable.

title: Compute signed final-divider candidates before radix-4 selection
motivation:
The current champion scores 161.66 at 68.530 MHz and 4,239,051
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
EX/MEM div_token.quotient[30], crosses u_mem/u_finish, and ends at
ID/EX alu_a[22], with 19.987 ns arrival through 43 cells. In the
current m_finish.sv, final trial subtraction and digit selection
precede quotient/remainder selection and a full-width conditional
negation. A late quotient digit can therefore propagate through
a second carry chain before decode captures the forwarded value.
The r12s1 operand and partial-result registers made this completion
path directly actionable. Prior micro_opt r3s0 lost 28.15 percent
by replacing native borrow chains with a routing-heavy prefix;
r11s0 result predecode and r12s0 register-file changes left the
arithmetic bottleneck intact. This proposal instead removes a
serial arithmetic dependence using native fixed-width arithmetic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the combinational final radix-4 division digit in
m_finish.sv. Speculate the signed architectural result for each of
the four possible quotient digits in parallel with the existing
full-width trial comparisons, then select the completed candidate
with the existing one-hot digit signals. Remove the full-width
conditional negation after digit and quotient/remainder selection.
This is a local arithmetic implementation change with no new stage,
no changed recurrence, and no additional instruction or dependency
cycle. Multiplication and all pipeline/bus control remain as today.

Let T={token.remainder,token.quotient[31:30]} be the 34-bit final
trial remainder, D the captured 34-bit divisor, and P the 30-bit
token.quotient[29:0]. Retain the three independent 35-bit unsigned
differences T-D, T-2D and T-3D and their borrow-based selection of
the largest k in 0..3 satisfying kD<=T. Preserve full-width borrow
decisions, including high unsigned divisors and D=0 selecting k=3.
The captured 3D value supplies the third multiple as it does now.

For each k, the positive remainder candidate is (T-kD) modulo 2^32,
reusing the current difference bits; k=0 uses T[31:0]. Compute the
negative remainder candidate directly as (kD-T) modulo 2^32 using
a separate native 32-bit subtraction driven by registered operands.
For k=0 use -T[31:0]. Do not compute -(T-kD), which would retain two
serial carry chains. The upper bits of each multiple are needed for
selection but not for these modular candidate results. Only the
selected remainder must satisfy the architectural range invariant;
unselected speculative candidates may wrap. Choose each candidate's
sign using the registered token.negate before the final one-hot mux.

For quotient candidates, the positive value is {P,k}. Compute
negP=(-P) modulo 2^30 in parallel with the trial comparisons. The
exact negative quotient candidates are {negP,2'b00} for k=0 and
{~P,2'b11}, {~P,2'b10}, {~P,2'b01} for k=1,2,3 respectively. This
follows from -(4P+k)=4*(-P) when k=0, and
-(4P+k)=4*(~P)+(4-k) modulo 2^32 otherwise. Thus digit selection
never launches a full-width quotient negation. Keep every operand,
complement, concatenation and subtraction width explicit.

Use the registered remainder_op and negate flags to prepare one
complete 32-bit architectural candidate for each k, then combine
four masked candidates in a balanced OR tree with the current
one-hot digit selection. No add/subtract operation may follow this
selection on the division-result path. Keep the M-kind result mux
and downstream forwarding behavior unchanged. Inspect Gowin's
mapped path to verify that synthesis retains parallel candidate
arithmetic rather than recreating a late sign-correction carry chain.

Preserve signed truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainders,
division by zero and INT_MIN/-1. In particular, use the existing
captured negate bit, whose zero-divisor quotient suppression is
already correct. Leave RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS results and timing intact;
ALTOPS proof alone cannot verify this real-arithmetic rewrite.
Keep the nine-clock X divide occupancy, prefix transfer/hold rules,
one M dependency bubble, token independence from younger divides,
memory-ready behavior, reset cancellation, nret=1 and every invariant.

Validate the modular candidate identities and the selected digit
against the old finalizer, preferably by local combinational
equivalence, plus the existing exact RV32M tests. Exercise all four
final digits, positive and negative quotients/remainders, P=0 and
P near its 30-bit boundaries, borrow thresholds, high-bit unsigned
divisors, zero divisors and signed overflow. Run unchanged pipeline
tests, formal gates and stalled CoreMark cosimulation with canonical
CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Expect exactly the champion's cycle
count because no sequential behavior changes; measure it again.

A temporary RTL prototype of exactly this construction measured
Gowin placement-option frequencies 78.235, 81.140 and 81.140 MHz,
with a scored median of 81.140 MHz. Option zero used 3,971 logic
cells versus the champion's 3,745, with unchanged 811 registers,
40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its worst path moved to
branch/recovery logic at 18.076 ns; divider completion was a close
second at 18.075 ns. The median placement's worst path was 17.619 ns.
These arrival times include the vendor report's clock contribution
and are not reciprocals of its scored Fmax.

Prototype validation passed the existing ALU pytest suite in real
and ALTOPS modes (four pytest cases including its arithmetic models),
the existing pipeline suite, and strict Verilator lint. A Yosys SAT
miter proved old and new real-arithmetic finalizers equivalent for
every possible 134-bit div_token input with M_DIV selected, without
reachability assumptions. A separate integer model passed 400,000
selected-result comparisons over 100,000 arbitrary tokens and 32
directed quotient-prefix boundary comparisons. Selftest RVFI cosim
passed with ready buses and with both stall modes enabled. The
unchanged CoreMark validator passed canonical CRCs, UART validation,
memory bounds and marker checks at exactly 4,239,051 bracketed cycles
for ten iterations. The measured product is 191.41077 iterations/sec,
18.403 percent above 161.66. These are proposal-stage measurements;
rerun the unchanged formal and evaluation gates during implementation.
The prototype is restored after research; this YAML is the deliverable.

Expected fitness gain is 18 percent. Preserve the explicit per-digit
native subtractors and prefix quotient construction used in the probe;
folding the algebra back into post-selection negation would invalidate
the timing premise. Scope unused-signal lint annotations to the unused
extension bits [33:32] of the 35-bit trial differences, as in the
existing code's handling of discarded remainder bits. Do not weaken
any functional assertion or change arithmetic widths to silence lint.
The main risks are speculative-subtractor routing and the newly close
branch/recovery and divider-recurrence paths. Acceptance requires the
measured product strictly above 169.09636, or about 71.681 MHz at
4,239,051 cycles. No additional optimization category is proposed.

title: Move the final divider digit before EX/MEM with a two-bit head start
motivation:
The champion scores 161.66 at 68.53 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the registered
EX/MEM divider token and crosses m_finish, MEM result selection and
decode bypass before reaching ID/EX operand flops. The last radix-4
digit and sign correction still occur in series on that path. Earlier
r9s1 isolated divider sign correction but remained limited by a
register-file-to-execute path; r12s1 has now removed that competing
arithmetic launch path with fully resolved operand registers. This
makes divider completion repartitioning newly relevant. Removing MEM
forwarding instead would add dependency bubbles and threaten the
existing ten-clock progress bound on dependent divides.

The champion scores 161.66 at 68.53 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the registered
EX/MEM divider token and crosses m_finish, MEM result selection and
decode bypass before reaching ID/EX operand flops. The last radix-4
digit and sign correction still occur in series on that path. Earlier
r9s1 isolated divider sign correction but remained limited by a
register-file-to-execute path; r12s1 has now removed that competing

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Reschedule only division so EX/MEM carries a finished unsigned result
and a sign bit, rather than a thirty-bit-consumed prefix requiring
another division digit in MEM. Obtain the required two-bit head start
during request capture with a tiny first-digit circuit. Keep the
current nine-clock EX occupancy, retirement timing, forwarding
topology, multiply implementation and ordinary instruction timing.
This is one structural movement of work across the divider's register
boundaries; no additional instruction stage or bypass stall is added.

Let A and D be the existing normalized 32-bit operand magnitudes.
At request edge 0, compute q0=floor(A[31:30]/D) and r0=A[31:30] mod D.
If any D[31:2] bit is set, D>=4 exceeds the two-bit dividend prefix,
so q0=0 and r0=A[31:30]. Otherwise implement the exact two-bit division
for D[1:0] with a small combinational truth table or two width-bounded
restoring steps. For D=0, explicitly use q0=3 and r0=A[31:30]. Do not
infer full-width division, a variable shifter, or full-width trial
subtraction in this initial-digit circuit. Classify the full normalized
divisor before narrowing it. Initialize quotient_q={A[29:0],q0} and
remainder_q=zero_extend(r0); capture D, 3D, operation and sign as today.
A direct small circuit is sufficient: with N=A[31:30], D=1 gives

title: Decouple next-PC prediction from instruction memory with a small tagged target cache
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct JAL and conditional branches with a
sixteen-entry agreement table. Prior r4s2 trace research counted roughly
55,000 conditional misses and 14,000 JALRs, leaving less than two percent
cycle reduction even for ideal accuracy at the current 4,239,051 cycles.
Increasing direction-table accuracy alone therefore cannot justify the
4.6 percent acceptance threshold. Meanwhile fetch still computes its next
PC through instruction memory, B/J immediate reconstruction, a full-width
target adder, and selection. Earlier attempts retimed recovery or counter
lookup without removing this instruction-dependent target recurrence.

sixteen-entry agreement table. Prior r4s2 trace research counted roughly
55,000 conditional misses and 14,000 JALRs, leaving less than two percent
cycle reduction even for ideal accuracy at the current 4,239,051 cycles.
Increasing direction-table accuracy alone therefore cannot justify the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace instruction-derived taken-target prediction with one small,
PC-indexed, fully tagged branch target buffer (BTB). Use exactly sixteen
direct-mapped entries indexed by PC[5:2]. Each entry holds a valid bit,
the remaining PC tag, a full aligned target, a conditional/direct-JAL
type bit, and the conditional branch's displacement-sign bias. Store
tags as sixteen 26-bit words (PC[31:6]), targets as sixteen 30-bit
words (target[31:2]), and type/bias as sixteen two-bit words, with one
common synchronous write address/enable and asynchronous read index.
The tested arrays were btb_tag[0:15], btb_target[0:15], and
btb_kind[0:15], with btb_kind storing {is_direct_jal, displacement_sign}
and a separate btb_valid[15:0]. Reconstruct the target by appending
two zero bits; use btb_update_pc[5:2] as the common write address.
Use ordinary unreset payload arrays so Gowin can infer distributed
RAM; reset only the separate sixteen-bit validity vector. Require
fetch PC[1:0] == 0 before declaring a hit, completing the full-PC tag.
Retain
the existing sixteen local two-bit agreement counters and their current
update discipline. A matching conditional entry predicts taken when
its saved bias equals the agreement-counter MSB; a matching JAL entry
predicts taken unconditionally. A miss predicts PC+4. JALR remains
unpredicted. Remove the B/J immediate target adder and instruction-word
predecode from the fetch next-PC cone instead of retaining them as a
combinational miss fallback. Keep the registered PC driving imem_addr.

Train or replace a target entry exactly once when a valid, legal,
non-faulting conditional branch or direct JAL advances through EX.
Conditional branches allocate their PC+immediate target on either
outcome when that target is aligned; do not allocate an unaligned
target even for a not-taken branch. JALR, invalid slots, illegal
encodings, memory holds, and active divide waits never allocate.
Only conditional branches update agreement counters, using the
resolving instruction's actual displacement sign as today. Entry
tags, targets, type and bias update together. Reset clears validity;
inactive entry data need not reset. Lookup is read-before-write with
no same-cycle training-to-prediction bypass.

Carry the selected predicted-taken bit and its exact selected target
through IF/ID and ID/EX at the same edge that advances PC. Retain the
prediction with its instruction on holds. Add a 32-bit predicted_target
field after predicted_taken in each bundle. Capture predicted_target
with ID/EX's existing data domain on !stall || flush, independently of
validity; it needs no reset or flush clearing. Existing predicted_taken
and valid/control clearing make invalid target data inert. Because a
BTB is a hint and instruction memory
can change, the existing direction-only XOR recovery is insufficient.
EX must recover when actual_taken differs from predicted_taken OR when
both are taken and the authoritative target differs from the saved
predicted target. Specifically use (actual_taken ^ in.predicted_taken)
|| (actual_taken && in.predicted_taken &&
    resolved_pc_next != in.predicted_target), qualified by in.valid
and the existing ex_advance. Do not add a new recovery register.
An ordinary or
illegal instruction incorrectly hit by stale BTB state must recover
to PC+4. A stale taken target must recover even when direction matches.
This retains correctness for full-PC aliases, changed instructions,
reserved encodings, misalignment traps, and arbitrary symbolic streams.

Preserve reset then accepted EX recovery then accepted prediction as
PC priority. EX recovery repairs PC immediately and annuls the younger
slot at the existing edge, including imem stalls and dmem-release
cycles. No extra recovery stage or lost slot is introduced. Maintain
all existing operand interlocks, memory handshakes, divider timing,
link writes, authoritative RVFI next-PC values, contiguous retirement,
trap discipline, and nret=1. The BTB must never directly authorize a
memory operation or architectural write. Preserve every formal and
simulation gate and modify no evaluation-contract files.

A temporary prototype of this specific sixteen-entry architecture
measured Gowin placement-option frequencies 71.519, 74.530 and 74.530
MHz, median 74.530 MHz, versus the champion's 68.530 MHz median. Usage
was 3,882 logic cells, 857 registers, 55 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two
DSPs. The unchanged stalled CoreMark evaluator passed canonical CRC,
UART validation, memory bounds, completion and timing-marker checks:
4,272,503 bracketed cycles for ten iterations, versus 4,239,051 for
the champion. Their product is 174.441 iterations/sec, approximately
+7.91 percent above 161.66 and above the 169.09636 acceptance threshold.
At the measured candidate cycle count, acceptance requires median Fmax
above approximately 72.2465 MHz. These are proposal-stage measurements,
not tournament acceptance or a guarantee of the subsequent layout.

Offline cold replay of the canonical architectural control-flow trace
predicted 102,222 recovery events versus 68,859 for the existing
predictor, a difference of 33,363; measured RTL added 33,452 cycles.
Thus the improvement comes from clock rate despite worse prediction
accuracy. Fresh champion timing placed M completion and EX-to-D paths
in the worst 25; prototype timing still contains arithmetic and recovery
bottlenecks. Do not attribute the entire Fmax gain to one eliminated
path: altered mapping and routing also matter. Distributed-RAM inference,
full-target comparison fanout, conflicts on other code and placement
variation are the main risks. Keep confidence medium and rerun all
unchanged evaluation gates after implementation.

The prototype passed Verilator lint and full-field RVFI cosimulation
for selftest plus random1, random2 and random3, both with ready buses
and with both buses stalled. All 53 unchanged standard ALTOPS formal
checks passed. A directed cocotb probe passed eight cases: a trained
JAL site changed to a different taken JAL target, an ordinary ADDI,
a reserved branch encoding, or a misaligned JAL, each with ready and
stalled buses. It required an actual stale taken prediction on the
second visit, exact architectural PC/link/trap behavior, contiguous
retirement, and suppression of the stale-target store. These probes
supplement rather than replace the implementation's full unit suite;
its old predictor-specific models must be updated for cold BTB misses.
Restore temporary prototype RTL and tests after research; this YAML
is the proposal deliverable.

title: Finish unsigned division in X with parallel radix-16 trials at unchanged latency
motivation: The champion achieves 191.41 fitness at 81.140 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its branch recovery, divider completion and two-digit divider recurrence are close competing limits. Local control-cone probes moved the worst paths into the unchanged recurrence without improving scored Fmax. Prior r3s0 and a fresh split-subtractor probe show that replacing native carry chains with routed block-prefix or carry-select networks is counterproductive. Instead, remove the serial dependence between the two radix-4 digits in each ordinary divider round while retaining native subtractors and the complete sequential protocol.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion achieves 191.41 fitness at 81.140 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its branch recovery, divider completion and two-digit divider recurrence are close competing limits. Local control-cone probes moved the worst paths into the unchanged recurrence without improving scored Fmax. Prior r3s0 and a fresh split-subtractor probe show that replacing native carry chains with routed block-prefix or carry-select networks is counterproductive. Instead, remove the serial dependence between the two radix-4 digits in each ordinary divider round while retaining native subtractors and the complete sequential protocol.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real-arithmetic divider recurrence with one parallel radix-16 digit per round. Keep magnitude capture at edge zero and perform eight four-bit rounds at edges one through eight. The last round presents COMPLETE unsigned quotient and remainder to EX/MEM at the same edge eight that currently transfers a thirty-bit prefix. M then only selects quotient versus remainder and performs the existing captured sign correction before W. Nine-clock X occupancy, M completion, dependent-instruction stalls and retirement timing remain identical. This single local divider optimization uses radix-16 arithmetic to remove both serial radix-4 recurrence and M's final trial subtraction; it adds no pipeline stage or new execution policy.

Capture eight unsigned 36-bit odd divisor multiples D,3D,5D,7D,9D,11D,13D,15D from the normalized divisor at the existing request edge. All even multiples are constant left shifts of the appropriate captured odd multiple. Widen to 36 bits before shifting or adding: 15*(2^32-1) requires all 36 bits. Compute 3D,5D,9D by one shifted addition, 7D and 15D by shifted subtraction, and 11D=D+2D+8D and 13D=D+4D+8D with bitwise carry-save reduction followed by one native carry-propagate addition. Do not cascade two full adders to form those latter multiples. For the measured construction retain the existing captured 34-bit D and 3D fields in div_token_t; they are now unused by M and are pruned from the timed hardware. Keep their values available for current internal unit monitors. Do not resize or reorder the token bundle in this proposal. Reset the new multiple registers consistently with existing divider state and update them only on a request accepted in DIV_IDLE.

In each round form unsigned T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:28]}, width 36. Compute fifteen independent 37-bit zero-extended differences T-kD for k=1..15. Difference bit 36 is the borrow. Use the ordered threshold results to select the largest non-borrowing k: select[0]=borrow[1], select[15]=!borrow[15], and select[k]=!borrow[k] && borrow[k+1] otherwise. For positive D, the remainder invariant R<D gives T<16D, so the selected remainder satisfies 0<=T-kD<D and fits 32 bits. For D=0 every comparison succeeds, select[15] is the only active bit, and the consumed dividend prefix is retained as remainder. Never truncate the trial or divisor multiples before the borrow decisions.

Prepare sixteen masked 36-bit candidates {remainder_candidate[31:0],4-bit k}, with k=0 using T[31:0], and combine them in an explicit balanced binary OR tree. Set remainder_next to the upper 32 selected bits and quotient_next={quotient_q[27:0],selected_digit}. Remove both old radix-4 digits from alu.sv. During final_round, drive token.quotient=quotient_next and token.remainder=remainder_next; otherwise use the saved registers. If edge eight is blocked, save these COMPLETE values once and enter DIV_DONE. On a later consume, transfer the saved result without repeating the round. On immediate consume, transfer the same complete values and return to DIV_IDLE. In m_finish.sv, unsigned_div_result=remainder_op ? remainder : quotient; div_result=negate ? -unsigned_div_result : unsigned_div_result. This negation now starts from registered complete values and has no trial-subtraction/borrow-selection chain ahead of it. Preserve the existing M-kind mux and multiplication finalizer.

Preserve magnitude capture, signed quotient and dividend-signed remainder semantics, zero divisors, INT_MIN/-1, reset cancellation, held operands, final-result availability independent of consume, blocked completion, back-to-back division and independence of younger M operations. Keep the original RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arithmetic and exactly the same schedule in both configurations. Multiplication, integer ALU operations, decoder legality, forwarding, pipeline controls, memory requests, prediction and nret=1 remain unchanged. Modify no evaluator or formal contract.

Validate every four-bit round against an independent integer divmod model, all sixteen selected digits, thresholds around kD, high unsigned divisors, all signed combinations, zero divisors and overflow. Existing tests check every registered four-bit prefix; retain those checks for edges one through seven. Update only the edge-eight token expectation from a thirty-bit prefix to full 32-bit unsigned quotient/remainder. Retain exact latency, hold, reset, source and result assertions. The old finalizer SAT test requires a boundary adapter: compute its reference final radix-4 digit from an arbitrary old prefix token, supply that COMPLETE token to the new m_finish, and prove the same architectural signed result. Keep the proof exhaustive over the original token inputs; do not delete or bypass it. Run ALU real/ALTOPS tests, pipeline tests, unchanged formal/liveness and stalled CoreMark cosimulation with canonical CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation. Prove local equivalence of the radix-16 recurrence to two radix-4 steps under the reachable remainder invariant; normal ALTOPS formal cannot establish real divider arithmetic.

A temporary implementation of this complete-result construction measured Gowin placement-option frequencies 81.549, 89.531 and 89.531 MHz, with a scored median of 89.531 MHz versus 81.140 MHz. Option-zero usage was 4,343 logic cells, 951 registers, 40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The worst median-option path moved to branch/recovery at 16.464 ns arrival; the radix-16 recurrence followed at 16.461 ns. Arrival includes clock contribution and is not the reciprocal of scored Fmax. At unchanged 4,239,051 CoreMark cycles, projected fitness is about 211.21, a 10.34 percent gain. The implementation evaluator must measure actual cycles and rerun every gate; this is not tournament acceptance.

The composed actual-arithmetic and ALTOPS ALU tests, arithmetic models and pipeline runner passed. The pre-existing finalizer-only SAT test initially failed because its input still described a thirty-bit prefix; after inserting the reference final-digit adapter for the new boundary, that exhaustive test passed. Strict Verilator lint passed after explicitly comparing elaboration-time modulo expressions against zero and naming conditional generate blocks. Those lint-only source corrections were made after the reported P&R run; rerun scored timing during implementation. Full formal and CoreMark checks are being attempted within the proposal budget; any completed results will be appended below. No assertion was weakened.

An earlier radix-16 prototype retained M's last radix-4 digit and measured only 81.879 MHz, below the acceptance margin. Implement the COMPLETE-result construction above, not that earlier prefix variant. The expected gain comes from removing the serial division work at both boundaries while keeping the same operation schedule. Added divisor-multiple registers and parallel subtractor routing are material risks, as are newly close branch, multiplier and ordinary-ALU forwarding paths. Acceptance requires measured fitness strictly above 200.21486, about 84.872 MHz at unchanged cycles. Temporary RTL and test edits are restored after research; this YAML is the deliverable.

title: Overlap bus stalls with a two-entry fall-through instruction ring
motivation:
The champion reaches 191.41 iterations/sec at 81.140 MHz and 4,239,051
bracketed cycles for ten CoreMark iterations. Fetch still stops whenever
decode waits for a dependency, a divide or data memory, and decode cannot
use previously available instructions during an instruction-bus stall.
Structural attempt r11s1 measured 5.14 percent fewer cycles with a small
fetch queue, but its clock loss reduced the net gain to 3.01 percent.
That attempt preceded r12s1's resolved operand registers and r13s0's
parallel signed divider completion, which removed its reported dominant
register-file/multiply and divider-completion paths. Revisit this measured
source of throughput improvement on the substantially repartitioned core.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert exactly two fall-through instruction queue entries between fetch
and decode, decoupling fetch acceptance from backend acceptance. This is
one structural change to pipeline buffering and backpressure. Retain the
current sixteen-entry agreement predictor, direct-JAL prediction, fully
resolved ID/EX operands, all arithmetic and the nine-clock divide schedule.
Do not introduce a registered-only fetch stage: an empty queue must pass
a ready instruction directly into decode to retain the one-slot recovery
penalty and the existing ready-bus retirement-gap bound.

Each physical entry stores PC, the unmodified instruction and the
fetch-time predicted_taken bit: 65 bits per entry. Use a two-entry ring
with a two-bit occupancy count and separate one-bit read and write
pointers, all reset to zero. Select the logical head with three disjoint
masks: count!=0 AND !read_slot for slot zero, count!=0 AND read_slot for
slot one, and count==0 for the live {PC,instruction,prediction} tuple.
Bitwise-mask each entire tuple and OR the three candidates. Only count
and read pointer control this data mux; redirect and bus readiness must
not mask instruction data or source addresses. Fetch PC remains the
address of the next unaccepted instruction, directly driving imem.

Define backend acceptance independently of imemReady: decode can consume
the head when it is valid and neither operand_wait, execute_wait nor an
older data-memory hold blocks ID/EX. A ready live word bypassing an empty
queue advances fetch PC without allocating an entry. If decode is held,
capture that word and continue fetching until both entries are occupied.
A nonempty head remains usable while imemReady is low. Let backend_hold
be operand_wait OR execute_wait OR the real dmem hold. Buffered pop is
count!=0 AND !backend_hold; fetch_accept is imemReady AND (count!=2 OR
pop); push is fetch_accept AND (count!=0 OR backend_hold). Advance fetch
PC on fetch_accept. Increment/decrement count only for push-only/pop-only;
toggle read_slot on buffered pop and write_slot on push. This supports
simultaneous full-queue pop/push with read-before-write semantics, and
bypass consumption changes neither pointer. Write only the physical slot
addressed by write_slot on push; never copy a tail payload into a head.
Pointer parity and occupancy distinguish empty from full when read and
write pointers coincide. Capacity depends on registered occupancy and a
buffered dequeue, avoiding a live-instruction ready/valid loop.

An accepted EX redirect has priority over every queue event: flush both
entries, discard the current imem word, bubble ID/EX and install the full
recovery PC even when imemReady is low. On the following ready cycle the
target can bypass the empty queue. Correctly predicted branches retain
their queued path. Reset/redirect clear count and both pointers, but do
not gate the 130 payload flops' write enables or clear their data. Payload
capture during invalidation is harmless because occupancy becomes zero.
Predictor updates remain once per advancing legal
conditional branch, and stored predictions must never be recomputed after
enqueue. Reset cancels buffered instructions and all pending acceptance.

Route register-file addresses and forward_unit comparisons from the
selected head instruction, replacing core.sv's raw io_imemData forwarding
comparisons. Resolve operands only when the head actually enters ID/EX;
never queue register values or forwarding choices. Preserve youngest-writer
priority, trap-aware producer eligibility, x0 and W bypass. Separate an
empty-and-unready fetch bubble from backend holds, retaining full inert
controls for bubbles and exact immutable operands on a held instruction.
Do not change memory requests, dedicated registered effective addresses,
divide request/consume timing, real or ALTOPS arithmetic, retirement width,
RVFI source metadata, contiguous order, traps or decoder legality.

Validate empty/full transitions, simultaneous push/pop, backend-only and
imem-only stalls, divide holds, head dependencies on both source ports,
predictor updates while an entry waits, full-queue recovery with imemReady
low, and wrong-path stores/divides/illegal instructions. Preserve the
existing maximum ten-clock ready-bus retirement-gap check, explicitly
including recovery directly to a divide. Run unchanged formal and stalled
retirement cosim, including canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART text, bounded
memory accesses and marker-bracketed cycles. Update implementation-specific
fetch monitors to distinguish enqueue from decode acceptance without
weakening architectural or progress assertions.

Proposal-stage RTL measurements on this champion found 3,994,432
marker-bracketed cycles for ten iterations, 5.77 percent fewer than
4,239,051. Canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation and
selftest retirement cosimulation passed. The selected ring measured
Gowin placement frequencies 73.185, 78.766 and 78.766 MHz, giving a
scored median of 78.766 MHz. Option zero used 4,151 logic cells, 945
registers, 40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The product is
197.18949 iterations/sec, 3.019 percent above the 191.41 champion.
This is a measured improvement but does NOT clear the 4.6 percent
tournament acceptance margin. The honest expected impact is therefore
three percent with low confidence in acceptance, not an eight-percent
extrapolation from cycle savings.

The ring implementation matters: compacting entries measured 75.846 MHz,
removing recovery from their data enables reached 77.093 MHz, and the
separate-pointer masked-OR ring reached 78.766 MHz. A registered one-hot
head state measured 75.713 MHz; deriving the write pointer from count
and using nested head muxes measured 76.093 MHz. Use the specified
separate-pointer ring, not those slower alternatives. The median ring's
worst paths include X-to-D integer bypass, read-pointer through register
file to resolved operands, divider completion and divider recurrence,
all near 17.98 ns reported arrival time. That report includes clock
contribution and is not the reciprocal of scored Fmax.

On the final ring prototype, strict Verilator lint, all 29 adapted
pipeline cocotb tests, the queue/predictor cocotb test and all 53 unchanged
normal riscv-formal checks passed. The tests preserve architecture,
operand, request, retirement and ten-clock progress assertions. Measure
divide consumer residence at the decode head rather than at the now
independent fetch PC. One exact stalled-program cycle vector changes
because buffered fetches hide bubbles; its requests, results and holds
remain checked. Rerun all unchanged evaluation gates on implementation.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 200.21486, or median Fmax
above 79.97446 MHz at the measured cycle count. The remaining timing
loss is a material limitation, not evidence of an accepted winner.
Restore temporary RTL and test probes after research; this YAML is the
deliverable and proposes only this single structural queue change.

title: Distributed target prediction for direct branches and last-target JALR
motivation:
The current champion still computes predicted direct targets through the
instruction-memory word and a full-width B/J immediate adder. The r13s2
sixteen-entry direct-only BTB removed that recurrence, but added 33,452
CoreMark cycles from cold/conflict misses and left JALR unpredicted. Use
a larger explicitly distributed target table on the present champion,
including last-target JALR prediction, to retain the timing benefit with
fewer recovery events. The existing sixteen-entry agree table is already
accurate enough that increasing direction capacity alone offers little
chance of clearing the fitness margin. RAM inference is material: an
unannotated 32-entry probe inferred extra BSRAM and fell to 66.714 MHz;
explicit distributed storage reached 82.122 MHz with identical behavior.
