hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace instruction-derived next-PC prediction with one 32-entry,
direct-mapped, fully tagged branch target buffer covering conditional
branches, JAL and legal JALR. Index by PC[6:2]; each entry stores a
25-bit PC[31:7] tag, a 30-bit target[31:2], and two kind bits containing
{unconditional_jump, displacement_sign}. Maintain a separate 32-bit
valid vector. Use asynchronous lookup and one synchronous write port
for each payload array. Apply the Gowin-supported SystemVerilog
attribute (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) to all three payload
arrays; reset only validity, leaving payload unreset. This exact mapping
requirement avoids the extra block-RAM implementation measured in the
unannotated probe. Require fetch PC[1:0]==0 as part of a full-PC hit.

Retain the existing sixteen local agreement counters, PC[5:2] indexing,
reset state, saturation and training discipline. On a matching branch
entry, predict taken when the saved displacement sign equals the live
agree-counter MSB. On a matching JAL/JALR entry, predict its saved target
unconditionally. A miss predicts PC+4. The JALR entry learns the last
resolved target, so returns or other indirect transfers may miss when
their destination changes. Do not add a return stack or another history
predictor. Remove raw-instruction predecode and the immediate target
adder from the IF next-PC cone completely; do not retain a miss fallback.
Keep io_imemAddr driven directly by the registered PC.

Train or replace an entry exactly once on valid, legal, non-faulting EX
advance of a conditional branch, JAL or JALR, and only if the resolved
target is word aligned. Conditional branches allocate PC+immediate on
either outcome; do not allocate a misaligned conditional target even
when the branch was not taken. JALR stores the resolved rs1+immediate
target after bit-zero clearing. Write tag, target, kind and validity
atomically at the resolving PC's index. Never allocate on reset,
bubbles, illegal encodings, data-memory holds or active divide waits.
Only conditional branches train the agree counters. Use read-before-
write lookup with no same-cycle update-to-prediction bypass.

Add a full-width predicted_target to if_id_t and id_ex_t while retaining
predicted_taken. Capture the exact selected target together with its
instruction in ID/EX's existing data domain on !stall || flush. Hold it
on true stalls; no reset is needed for this data because existing valid
and predicted_taken clearing make bubble contents inert. Prediction
metadata and PC advancement must use the same live lookup at acceptance.

Keep authoritative branch/jump resolution unchanged. EX recovery is
in.valid && ex_advance && ((actual_taken ^ in.predicted_taken) ||
(actual_taken && in.predicted_taken &&
 resolved_pc_next != in.predicted_target)). The target comparison is
essential for changing JALR destinations and stale taken BTB entries.
An ordinary or illegal word reached through an old entry recovers to
its architectural sequential successor. Changed direct targets, tag
conflicts, reserved encodings and target faults must retain full
correctness. Do not assume that a matching tag validates an instruction.

Preserve immediate recovery with its existing one-slot penalty. Reset
has highest PC priority, then accepted EX recovery, then ordinary fetch
acceptance. Recovery overrides imem backpressure on data-memory release
and squashes younger side effects at the existing edge. Keep all real
and ALTOPS arithmetic, resolved operand registers, effective-address
transport, memory handshakes, link writes, trap suppression and nret=1.
RVFI always reports authoritative resolved next-PC and contiguous order.
No evaluation-contract files or correctness gates change.

A temporary prototype of exactly this 32-entry distributed design
measured placement frequencies 79.411, 82.122 and 82.122 MHz, for median
82.122 MHz. Option zero used 4,311 logic cells, 873 registers, 70 LUT RAMs,
four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC, UART,
memory-bounds, completion and timing-marker validation at 4,247,943
cycles for ten iterations, versus 4,239,051 for the champion. The product
is approximately 193.322 iterations/sec, about 1.00 percent above 191.41.
This measured gain does NOT clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin:
at this cycle count the candidate needs more than about 85.050 MHz.
Expected impact is therefore one percent with low confidence in
acceptance, not an unsupported above-threshold claim. Divider recurrence,
operand bypass, recovery fanout and cache routing remain timing risks.

The target-cache prototype passed full-field RVFI cosimulation on
selftest and random1/random2/random3, each with ready buses and with
both buses stalled, plus all 53 unchanged standard ALTOPS formal checks.
The distributed-memory attribute changes implementation, not logical
behavior. Strict Verilator lint passed with narrowly scoped unused-low-
bit annotations on the full-width BTB update address inputs. These are
proposal-stage measurements, not tournament acceptance. Rerun all
unchanged correctness gates and scored placements after implementation.
Restore temporary prototype RTL and tests; this YAML is the deliverable.

Extend independent predictor tests for cold misses, both halves of the
32-entry table, full-tag conflicts, reset, read-before-write updates and
acceptance after arbitrary holds. Add changing-target JALR, returns to

data-memory release. Check exact RVFI PC/link/trap/order, once-only
training and no wrong-path stores or divide launches. Update old
predictor-specific scoreboards for cold misses without weakening their
architectural assertions, progress bounds or memory-handshake checks.

title: Merge disjoint multiply limbs before a single carry-save reduction
motivation: The champion reaches 202.72 fitness at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its radix-16 divider has exposed closely competing recovery, arithmetic bypass and multiply-completion paths. Fresh control-cone probes removed redundant branch dependencies but regressed median Fmax to 83.819 and 84.116 MHz while multiply completion became critical. The current m_finish describes four overlapping 64-bit operands and two carry-save reductions, although the low-low product has only 32 meaningful bits and two terms can be merged into disjoint lanes.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion reaches 202.72 fitness at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its radix-16 divider has exposed closely competing recovery, arithmetic bypass and multiply-completion paths. Fresh control-cone probes removed redundant branch dependencies but regressed median Fmax to 83.819 and 84.116 MHz while multiply completion became critical. The current m_finish describes four overlapping 64-bit operands and two carry-save reductions, although the low-low product has only 32 meaningful bits and two terms can be merged into disjoint lanes.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the real-arithmetic multiplication finalizer in m_finish.sv. Keep the four existing signed 17-by-17 limb products, their EX/MEM registers, operation tags and all instruction latencies. Replace the two 64-bit carry-save reductions with one 48-bit reduction by first merging non-overlapping LL and HH fields. This is one local arithmetic representation optimization; it changes no pipeline, bypass policy, predictor or divider.

The multiplier operands a_lo and b_lo are signed 17-bit values with bit 16 fixed at zero. Hence LL=a_lo*b_lo is nonnegative, fits 32 bits, and mul_partial.ll[33:32] are always zero for real captured products. The low 16 product bits are exactly LL[15:0], since every other partial product starts at bit 16 or above. The product above bit 15 is therefore LH + HL + (HH << 16) + LL[31:16], modulo 2^48. The last two terms occupy disjoint lanes and can be concatenated rather than added.

Use exactly three 48-bit terms:
  term_lh = {{14{mul_partial.lh[33]}}, mul_partial.lh};
  term_hl = {{14{mul_partial.hl[33]}}, mul_partial.hl};
  term_ll_hh = {mul_partial.hh[31:0], mul_partial.ll[31:16]}.
Compute sum = term_lh ^ term_hl ^ term_ll_hh and
carry = ((term_lh & term_hl) | (term_lh & term_ll_hh) |
         (term_hl & term_ll_hh)) << 1, both at exactly 48 bits.
Set upper_product = sum + carry using one native 48-bit addition;
product = {upper_product, mul_partial.ll[15:0]}.
Keep the existing high_word selection of product[63:32] versus
product[31:0], and the existing M-kind output mux. Dropping HH bits
above 31 is exact because their original shift by 32 places them
outside the retained 64-bit product. Preserve signed LH/HL extension
BEFORE addition; treating those cross terms as unsigned corrupts MULH
and MULHSU. Do not reintroduce a separate LL-upper addition, which
would restore the removed arithmetic level.

Leave alu.sv, core_pkg.sv, all packed field widths/order, partial-product capture enables and reset behavior unchanged. Keep the entire RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branch unchanged: it bypasses real multiplication and cannot establish this arithmetic identity. Leave real/ALTOPS division, M completion scheduling, X pending hazards, forwarding, memory side effects, traps, nret=1 and all RVFI fields unchanged. The new finalizer consumes only the registered EX/MEM token, including while younger M operations run or memory stalls hold that token.

A temporary implementation of precisely this construction measured Gowin option frequencies 92.189, 91.009 and 91.009 MHz, median 91.009 MHz versus the champion's 85.936 MHz. The option-zero mapping uses 4,452 logic cells, 951 registers, 40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and three DSPs; the champion uses 4,380 logic cells, the same register/memory counts and two DSPs. Thus this is a timing-for-area trade, not a DSP reduction claim. The median-option worst path is now the divider recurrence at 16.282 ns arrival; option zero is limited by branch/bypass control at 16.142 ns. Vendor arrival includes clock contribution and is not the reciprocal of scored Fmax. At unchanged CoreMark cycles, projected fitness is approximately 214.69, about 5.9 percent above the champion.

A Yosys SAT miter proved the optimized real finalizer equal to the independent 64-bit expression LL + (signed(LH)<<16) + (signed(HL)<<16) + (signed(HH)<<32) for every 32-bit LL, arbitrary signed 34-bit LH/HL/HH and both high_word values. The only input restriction is LL[33:32]=0, a guarantee of the existing zero-extended 16-bit low limbs. There are no sign or reachability restrictions on the cross/high terms. Preserve this proof as an additional test rather than replacing existing division equivalence tests. Validate the low-low width guarantee separately from the actual alu limb declarations or a local proof. Strict Verilator lint passed. All 53 unchanged normal formal checks passed. Selftest RVFI cosimulation passed both with ready buses and with instruction/data stalls. The unchanged canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validator passed, and the IPC evaluator measured exactly 4,239,051 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. Thus the measured product is 214.69192 iterations/second, 5.9056 percent above the rounded 202.72 champion. The full existing test_alu.py plus test_pipeline.py pytest run passed all ten collected tests, including real and ALTOPS composed arithmetic runners, the divider finalizer SAT check and the radix-16 RTL equivalence proof. The separate IF/pipeline run also passed, and the finalizer-specific multiplication SAT proof passed. No existing assertion or test expectation was changed. These are proposal-stage measurements; implementation must rerun the full unchanged gates.

Extend real MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU tests with all-zero/all-one limbs, 0x0000ffff/0x00010000 boundaries, signed extrema, opposite signs, low-middle carry propagation, high-half carries and back-to-back M operations under holds. Retain every existing exact-result, latency, reset, hold and ALTOPS assertion. Run unchanged formal/liveness and stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker gates. Expected cycles are exactly 4,239,051; measure them. Acceptance requires measured fitness strictly above 212.04512, about 89.887 MHz at unchanged cycles. The proposal-stage timing clears this threshold but is not tournament acceptance. The margin is modest, extra DSP inference is a material mapping change, and divider/control paths remain close competitors. Do not add unrelated control-cone changes. Temporary RTL probes have been restored; the sole deliverable is this YAML.

Preserve high/low selection, M-kind mux, divider, ALTOPS and all interfaces/latency.

Add real multiply limb/carry/sign boundary vectors and a local SAT equivalence test for the actual optimized finalizer against the independent four-term 64-bit product expression, constraining only LL[33:32] to the zeros guaranteed by the existing low-limb multipliers. Retain all existing multiply/divide, composed-pipeline, timing, hold, reset, ALTOPS and equivalence checks.

title: Decouple fetch acceptance with an instruction ring and registered annulment
motivation:
The champion scores 202.72 at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural attempt r14s1 demonstrated 5.77 percent
fewer cycles with a two-entry instruction ring, but its clock loss kept
fitness below acceptance. The current radix-16 divider removes that
attempt's reported worst arithmetic recurrence. A proposal-stage
ring-only probe on this champion still reached just 78.969 MHz:
buffering leaves EX branch resolution feeding forwarding and backend
hold into ring and PC enables. The proposed structural partition adds
the control boundaries needed to preserve elastic fetch's clock speed.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 202.72 at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Structural attempt r14s1 demonstrated 5.77 percent
fewer cycles with a two-entry instruction ring, but its clock loss kept
fitness below acceptance. The current radix-16 divider removes that
attempt's reported worst arithmetic recurrence. A proposal-stage
ring-only probe on this champion still reached just 78.969 MHz:
buffering leaves EX branch resolution feeding forwarding and backend
hold into ring and PC enables. The proposed structural partition adds
the control boundaries needed to preserve elastic fetch's clock speed.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition fetch/decode acceptance into a two-entry fall-through
instruction ring whose backend hold is independent of resolved branch
outcomes. Register wrong-path annulment at X while retaining immediate
PC repair. Separate pending-producer interlocks from completed-result
forwarding. These are the data, recovery and backpressure parts of one
elastic front-end boundary. Keep the existing predictor, resolved ID/EX
operands, EX/MEM arithmetic partition and nine-clock divider unchanged.

In if_stage, use exactly two fixed 65-bit slots containing
{pc,instruction,predicted_taken}, a two-bit count, and separate one-bit
read_slot/write_slot pointers. Select the head with a bitwise masked OR
of slot zero for count!=0 AND !read_slot, slot one for count!=0 AND
read_slot, and the live tuple for count==0. Neither recovery nor bus
readiness may mask instruction data or source-register addresses.
Preserve prediction as a fetch-time snapshot in each buffered tuple.
Keep io_imemAddr directly driven by the fetch PC register.

Define backend_hold as operand_wait OR execute_wait OR the actual
older dmem hold, excluding instruction-bus readiness. With stall equal
to backend_hold, pop = count!=0 AND !stall;
fetch_accept = imemReady AND (count!=2 OR pop);
push = fetch_accept AND (count!=0 OR stall).
A ready live instruction bypasses an empty ring without moving either
pointer. Buffered instructions can issue during imem stalls; fetch can
fill free slots during dependencies, division and dmem waits. Toggle
each pointer only for its buffered pop or push; update count only for
push-only or pop-only. Support full simultaneous pop/push with
read-before-write behavior. Write only slots[write_slot] on push; never
compact payloads or derive the write pointer from occupancy.

Reset or accepted recovery clears count and both pointers, with priority
over normal queue events. Payload writes remain controlled solely by
push: a simultaneous discarded write is harmless with count cleared.
Do not reset payload data or put redirect on their data/write enables.
Recovery repairs the fetch PC immediately even when imemReady is low;
otherwise advance PC only on fetch_accept. Fetch/decode valid is
count!=0 OR imemReady, independent of immediate redirect. Existing IF
flush can be tied low; raw head data remains visible when invalid.

Replace immediate IF/ID squashing with a separate kill_ex register in
ex_stage: reset it to zero; otherwise, whenever EX/MEM is not held by
actual dmem backpressure, set it to the accepted redirect. The recovery
edge may admit a speculative head into ID/EX, but the next X slot is
annulled while the repaired target is already at decode. Qualify is_mul,
is_div, next_reg_write and ex_advance with !kill_ex. A killed slot must
not launch/consume division, assert execute_wait, redirect, train the
predictor or forward. When it advances, clear the entire EX/MEM ctrl
bundle, m_kind and valid, while leaving unused data captures intact.
Preserve the dedicated effective-address register's original schedule.
Hold kill_ex through any actual EX/MEM hold. A normal recovery follows
an advancing branch/jump, so its next M slot cannot itself stall dmem.

!kill_ex AND !decoded_illegal AND decoded_reg_write AND

In forward_unit, compute operand_wait independently of the forwarding
priority arms as result_pending AND a match between the X destination
and either nonzero D source. Retain trap-aware next_reg_write and the
existing youngest-writer priority for data selection. Pending load/M
writers still block consumers rather than exposing an older value;
branches/jumps are never pending producers. This removes the spurious
branch-comparator-to-forwarding-to-ring-hold timing path without
relaxing fault suppression or dependency correctness.

Preserve nret=1, x0, both memory handshakes, exactly-once requests and
retirement, contiguous RVFI order, exact source metadata, target and
memory misalignment behavior, decoder legality and EBREAK discipline.
Leave all integer/M arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas, divider latency and
operand immutability unchanged. Train the sixteen-entry agree predictor
exactly once for each advancing legal non-faulting conditional branch.

The complete temporary RTL prototype passed strict Verilator lint and
unchanged selftest retirement cosimulation with ready and stalled buses.
All 53 unchanged normal riscv-formal checks passed. The independent
ring/predictor cocotb scoreboard passed 1,600 randomized cycles plus
directed queue transitions and predictor saturation/reset cases.
Sixteen selected existing pipeline tests passed after changing their
divide-residence monitors from fetch PC to decode-head PC. These include
unchanged ten-clock redirect-to-divide liveness assertions. A new test
also passed for killed load, divide, multiply, ALU, store, jump and
illegal slots with destination aliases, under ready and stalled buses.
The remaining internal prediction/forwarding scoreboards still require

the complete existing pipeline suite was not claimed as a prototype pass.
Canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation passed.
It measured 3,994,432 bracketed cycles for ten iterations and Gowin
placement frequencies 81.604, 87.038 and 87.038 MHz, giving a scored

Validate FIFO order, all push/pop combinations, full-queue recovery,

younger-writer priority, wrong-path loads/stores/divides/branches/illegal

writers. Adapt internal fetch monitors to separate enqueue from issue
and to model the speculative X slot and registered annulment. Preserve
all architectural checks, arithmetic expectations, and the maximum
ten-clock ready-bus retirement-gap assertion, including redirect directly
to DIV/REM. Run all unchanged formal and cosim gates and the complete
scored Gowin median during implementation. Temporary RTL/test probes
are restored after research; this YAML is the deliverable.

title: Preselect predictor correction targets and isolate branch outcomes from fetch holds
motivation:
The current champion scores 202.72 iterations/sec at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst timing path starts at a resolved EX branch operand and ends
at the fetch PC enable. The detailed vendor report exposes an indirect path through
trap-qualified writer eligibility and decode hazards, in addition to the intended
recovery path. Earlier r7s2 correction-offset preselection did not remove that
dependency and was still limited by arithmetic; r13s2/r14s2 target buffers introduced
cold/conflict misses. Optimize the existing direction-only predictor's correction
network without changing its predictions or miss penalty.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 202.72 iterations/sec at 85.936 MHz and 4,239,051 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst timing path starts at a resolved EX branch operand and ends
at the fetch PC enable. The detailed vendor report exposes an indirect path through
trap-qualified writer eligibility and decode hazards, in addition to the intended
recovery path. Earlier r7s2 correction-offset preselection did not remove that
dependency and was still limited by arithmetic; r13s2/r14s2 target buffers introduced
cold/conflict misses. Optimize the existing direction-only predictor's correction
network without changing its predictions or miss penalty.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the sixteen-entry agreement predictor, instruction-derived direct targets, direct-
JAL prediction and immediate one-slot recovery. Restructure only EX's predictor-recovery
fanout so the late branch outcome determines whether to redirect, while the saved
prediction independently selects the correction address and conditional branch faults
cannot affect fetch holds through forwarding eligibility.

In rtl/ex_stage.sv retain the current actual_taken, resolved_pc_next, ex_advance and
direction-mismatch redirect predicate. Replace only the correction-address assignment
with:
  redirect_target = in.predicted_taken ? (in.pc + 32'd4)
                  : (in.ctrl.is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target);
All operands of this address selection come from the already registered instruction, PC,
immediate, resolved rs1 and prediction. Keep the full-width PC+4, branch target and jump
target computations available in parallel; do not preselect an offset before a shared
adder. The correction address is meaningful only when redirect is asserted. On a miss,
actual_taken is the opposite of the saved predicted_taken: a predicted-taken miss always
corrects to PC+4, and a predicted-not-taken miss always corrects to the resolved
branch/jump target. Thus branch_cond no longer drives the full-width recovery-address
selection. JALR retains its exact resolved rs1+immediate target with bit zero cleared.

Remove the other branch-outcome-to-fetch-control dependency by defining:
  next_reg_write = in.valid && in.ctrl.reg_write
                && !in.ctrl.is_illegal && !misalign_jump;
Use the original registered decoder controls here, not ctrl_with_trap. The validated
decoder never sets reg_write for a conditional branch, so a conditional branch's
outcome-dependent alignment fault cannot suppress a real writer and must not enter the
EX forwarding producer predicate. A faulting JAL/JALR still has misalign_jump asserted
and must not forward or write its link. Keep ctrl_with_trap unchanged for the
architectural EX/MEM trap payload, including conditional branch faults and link
suppression. Do not replace the architectural resolved_pc_next with the speculative
correction candidate: RVFI must continue to report the actual successor even on
correctly predicted transfers or target faults.

Retain all existing advance qualification, once-only agreement training, prediction
capture, bus handshakes, recovery-over-imem-stall priority, data-memory holds, load/M
interlocks, arithmetic latency and ALTOPS behavior. Neither recovery nor training may
repeat while EX is held. Preserve nret=1, decoder legality, contiguous retirement order,
target alignment semantics and the unchanged formal progress bound. This adds no
predictor state, target cache, stage or extra recovery cycle.

A temporary prototype consisting of exactly these two EX assignment changes passed
strict Verilator lint and canonical stalled CoreMark validation at the unchanged
4,239,051 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. Gowin placement options measured 87.863,
90.699 and 90.699 MHz, yielding a 90.699 MHz median and approximately 213.96
iterations/sec: 5.54 percent above the 202.72 champion. Option zero used 4,393 logic
cells, 951 registers, 40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. These are proposal-stage
measurements, not tournament acceptance. The measured gain exceeds the 4.6 percent
threshold, but with less than one percentage point of headroom; placement sensitivity
and the remaining arithmetic/recovery-squash paths justify medium confidence. Reproduce
the exact two-assignment topology and rerun all unchanged correctness gates and scored
placements after implementation.

The exact prototype also passed all 53 unchanged standard ALTOPS riscv-formal checks,
including liveness, and full-field RVFI cosimulation for selftest plus
random1/random2/random3 with ready buses and with both buses stalled. The complete
existing IF-stage and pipeline cocotb suites passed. An added directed test passed with
ready buses and two stalled-bus seeds: faulting JAL/JALR instructions followed
immediately by consumers retained the previous destination value, taken misaligned
branches trapped, and untaken misaligned branches remained legal. It also checked
resolved PC continuity, contiguous order, once-only legal branch training and absence of
memory or divider side effects. A broader unit-suite invocation was stopped during the
unchanged full-width radix-16 equivalence proof; no complete full-unit-suite pass is
claimed.

Use existing predictor scoreboards plus directed regression cases to check both
correction directions, learned forward-taken and backward-not-taken branches, dependent
JALR links, target alignment faults, full-width target wraparound, and recovery
coincident with instruction stalls or older memory release. Check redirect_target
against the authoritative successor only when redirect is valid, and always check RVFI
pc_wdata against the architectural successor. Explicitly verify that a misaligned taken
conditional branch traps without appearing as a register producer, and that a misaligned
JALR cannot forward or write a link. Require no wrong-path store/divider launch and
unchanged one-slot recovery and retirement-gap bounds. Restore temporary prototype files
after research; this hypothesis YAML is the deliverable.
